works.title: Closed-Loop Fabrication of Regenerated Cellulose Battery Separator via Solvent-Guided Structural Regulation
works.abstract: Abstract The development of battery separators derived from renewable feedstocks that can simultaneously achieve high porosity, robust mechanical strength, excellent thermal stability, reliable electrochemical performance, and satisfactory environmental sustainability remains a core challenge in the field of sustainable energy storage material. Herein, we report a regenerated cellulose membrane prepared through a dissolution/regeneration process using lithium bromide Molecular dynamics simulation results show that water is the effective antisolvent for driving the formation of cellulose–cellulose H-bonds, yielding cellulose with a better crystalline structure. Subsequently, tert-butanol was utilized to replace water in the cellulose membrane precursor prior to drying, preventing capillary-induced pore collapse. This membrane exhibits high porosity of 70.1%, excellent electrolyte uptake capacity of 243.7%, ionic conductivity of 0.77 mS/cm, excellent thermal stability (no shrinkage at 150 °C), and roust mechanical strength. The Na/HC half-cells assembled with this membrane displays high cycle capacity retention rate of 87.1% at 0.1 C after 500 cycles, which is comparable to commercial separators. This membrane fabrication process enables closed-loop solvent recycling, and the membrane fully degraded after 4 months of soil burial, and life cycle assessment indicated lower impacts than commercial battery separators. These results establish a practical closed-loop strategy for sustainable, high-performance battery separators.

works.title: Unveiling the Overlooked Role of Alcoholic Sacrificial Agents in Photocatalytic H2O2 Synthesis: Beyond Hole Scavenging to Proton Donation
works.abstract: Abstract Two-electron oxygen reduction (2e– ORR) offers a green route for photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis, yet severe charge recombination restricts its efficiency. Alcoholic sacrificial agents are widely adopted to address this issue, but their transformation mechanism and exact contributions beyond hole capture remain poorly verified. In this work, we employed sodium anthraquinone sulfonate (SAS) as a model photocatalyst to systematically investigate the role of alcoholic sacrificial agents. The presence of alcohols substantially increased the H2O2 yield, with anhydrous methanol affording a maximum accumulated concentration of 98.2 mM, which is 818.3 times higher than that obtained in pure water. Two quantitative strategies (HRP-ABTS enzymatic colorimetry and FeCl2-based colorimetry) were adopted to exclude interfering signals, and the authentic generation of H2O2 was further validated via 31P NMR, 1H NMR, and MnO2 decomposition experiments. Then, deuterium isotope tracing revealed that all hydrogen atoms in the generated H2O2 originate exclusively from the methyl α-H of methanol rather than hydroxyl groups. Through quenching experiments, EPR spectroscopy, and in-situ FTIR analysis, we elucidated the transformation pathway of methanol on the catalyst surface. Furthermore, two common metal-containing and metal-free photocatalysts (NH2-MIL-125(Ti) and g-C3N4) were synthesized for verification, both exhibiting remarkably enhanced H2O2 productivity in alcoholic media. Via atomic-level proton tracking, this work overturns the conventional viewpoint that sacrificial agents contribute to promoting H2O2 generation by scavenging holes to promote charge separation and identifies the participation of methyl α-H in H2O2 generation. The elucidated reaction mechanism and alcohol conversion pathway offer valuable guidance for the rational design of high-performance photocatalysts toward efficient H2O2 photosynthesis.

works.title: Integrated Reactive CO2 and NH3 Capture and Conversion to Ammonium Carbamate: Material Design toward Low-Concentration Sources
works.abstract: Abstract Carbon dioxide (CO2) and ammonia (NH3) emissions are responsible for global warming and eutrophication, among other causes. Ionic liquids (ILs) stand out as versatile designer absorbent/catalyst materials that contribute to the capture and conversion of both gases. This work focuses on the efficient and innovative use of ILs in NH3 and CO2 integrated capture and conversion (ICC) to produce ammonium carbamate (AMC) using an efficient self-regenerating catalytic system operating at room temperature, with spontaneous product separation by precipitation. Experimental ICC tests were carried out using 10 ILs, with remarkable structural differences, and different NH3 and CO2 partial pressure and experimental times. Two different optimization routes were explored by tuning the IL material features through molecular design: (i) an NH3-driven mechanism using IL as the physical absorbent and (ii) a CO2-driven mechanism using IL as the reactive capture agent, selected to promote high CO2 chemical absorption and activation and easy IL regeneration and AMC removal. The use of an IL as a reactive capture agent strongly improves the process performance with fast ICC rates even at low NH3 and CO2 partial pressures, highlighting the CO2-driven approach as a versatile ICC technology capable of efficiently treating diluted NH3 and CO2 streams to produce value-added AMC products.

works.title: Interactive effects of spectral tuning and severe nitrogen deprivation on the energetic efficiency and lipid accumulation of Chlorella Sorokiniana
Plasticize Me Sweetly: Sugar-Based Plasticizers for Poly(lactic acid)
works.abstract: Abstract Carbohydrates are among the most abundant biopolymers in the world and offer a promising source for the synthesis of value-added chemicals. Galactaric acid is an attractive biobased building block that has not yet been fully exploited. Currently, regulatory, sustainability, safety-by-design, and performance requirements for polymer additives are becoming increasingly strict. As a result, innovation in this field must be accelerated to develop new materials with enhanced properties. With this objective, new sugar-based plasticizers based on galactaric acid have been synthesized. Poly(lactic acid) (PLA) was selected as a brittle, biobased polymer, to evaluate the ability of these additives to improve its mechanical properties. The best additive led to an increase of the elongation at break up to 260% when compared to the starting PLA. Experimental results have been supported by computational studies and show how small modifications in the molecular structure can influence both the synthesis and the performance of these additives.

works.title: Speciation Distribution, Valence Transformation, and Immobilization Mechanism of Cr during Portland Cement Hydration
works.abstract: Abstract Chromium (Cr) immobilization pathways in Portland cement may vary with cement-matrix characteristics. In this study, representative 32.5- and 42.5-grade cements (C3-3 and C4-2) were compared using controlled Cr(III)/Cr(VI) addition and multiscale characterization. XPS showed partial reduction of Cr(VI) to Cr(III) during hydration, while XAFS and 29Si NMR indicated Cr(III) association/incorporation with C-(A)-S-H-related structures. In C3-3-Cr, TEM, and SEM-EDS further revealed localized CaCr2O4 nanocrystals, indicating a combined structural association/incorporation–precipitation pathway. In C4-2-Cr, Cr was more diffusely distributed, and no resolvable Cr-bearing nanocrystals were observed in the examined TEM regions, indicating predominantly structural association/incorporation. These differences were associated with the higher hydration reactivity and more homogeneous C-S-H-rich microstructure of C4-2. The results demonstrate that cement-matrix hydration characteristics regulate the relative contributions of established Cr immobilization pathways, providing a mechanistic basis for the selection of cementitious matrices for Cr stabilization.

works.title: N, S, P-Codoped Carbon Quantum Dots as Corrosion Inhibitors for Mg–Air Batteries
works.abstract: Abstract In Mg–air batteries, electrolyte-induced self-corrosion and parasitic H2 evolution on Mg anodes lead to low anode utilization and poor discharge stability. Developing eco-friendly, highly efficient interface-regulating additives is therefore critical. Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) offer chemical stability and abundant surface groups, demonstrating strong potential for corrosion inhibition and electrochemical control. In this study, nitrogen, sulfur, and phosphorus ternary co-doped CQDs (NSP-CQDs) were fabricated via ultrasonic oxidation, wherein the orange peel acted as a carbon precursor, and thiourea and sodium tripolyphosphate acted as dopants. The as-prepared NSP-CQDs were added to a sodium chloride electrolyte to explore their effects on Mg anode corrosion and the discharge capability of Mg–air cells. Structural characterization showed that NSP-CQDs have a low-crystallinity carbon structure and exhibit localized graphite-ordering characteristics, with the surface rich in functional groups containing N, S, and P. EIS fitting results revealed that NSP-CQDs suppress Mg alloy self-corrosion, yielding an Rct of 319.5 Ω cm2 and an Rf of 915.1 Ω cm2. At 300 mg/L NSP-CQDs and 5 mA·cm–2, galvanostatic discharge produced a stable 1.24 V and 2005.4 Wh kg–1 specific energy. Furthermore, under intermittent operation at 10 mA·cm–2, the discharge voltage remained stable at 1.11∼1.13 V, with a cumulative operating time of up to 160 h.

works.title: Model-Informed Kinetic Synchronization for Intensified Methane-to-Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) Bioconversion
works.abstract: Abstract Biological conversion of methane into poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (PHB) offers a promising route for greenhouse gas mitigation, yet its industrial deployment remains constrained by inherently low volumetric productivity. To overcome this limitation, a multistage, repeated-batch strategy was developed to physically decouple biomass growth from PHB accumulation and synchronize their disparate kinetics using parallel reactors. Single-batch cultivation of Methylocystis sp. MJC1 revealed three phases: exponential growth, gas-transfer-limited growth, and PHB synthesis. Repeated-batch experiments using a dedicated cell generator and PHB producer demonstrated stable, reproducible biomass production without physiological deterioration. Based on the kinetic characteristics derived from these single- and repeated-batch cultivations, a simplified process model was constructed. Model-informed simulations identified a three-reactor configuration comprising a single cell generator supplying two parallel PHB producers as a critical step change, delivering substantial productivity gains while maintaining operational feasibility. Experimental validation of this configuration, using a transfer biomass concentration of 12 g/L, a transfer fraction of 79%, and a cell generator cultivation time of 20 h, yielded a volumetric productivity of 0.218 g-PHB/L/h, a 1.32-fold improvement over single-batch cultivation. Overall, this work establishes a robust and scalable framework for intensifying the production of methane-derived biodegradable polymers through synchronized multistage cultivation.

works.title: Sulfur Vacancy-Engineered Mn-Ni3S2@FeS Heterostructure for Efficient Alkaline Water/Seawater Splitting
works.abstract: Abstract Designing exceptional activity and durable noble-metal-free electrocatalysts for freshwater/seawater splitting remains an ongoing challenge for the practical deployment of the hydrogen economy. In this study, a heterostructured Mn-doped Ni3S2@FeS electrocatalyst on Ni foam with S-vacancies (Mn-Ni3S2@FeS) is prepared. Benefiting from the synergistic merits of the heterostructure, heteroatom doping, and the abundance of sulfur vacancies induced by Mn doping, Mn-Ni3S2@FeS drives the OER and HER with remarkable efficiency, necessitating exceptionally low overpotentials of 141 and 235 mV (OER) as well as 124 and 205 mV (HER) to achieve 10 and 100 mA cm–2, respectively. More importantly, Mn enhances the electronic conductivity of Ni3S2@FeS and triggers accelerated catalyst reconstruction, spawning the actual active phases of Mn-NiFeOOH for OER. Moreover, Mn-Ni3S2@FeS acts as a premier bifunctional catalyst capable of driving overall water and seawater splitting at impressively low cell voltages of merely 1.46 and 1.48 V to reach 10 mA cm–2, respectively, along with stable seawater electrolysis over 100 h at 500 mA cm–2. Density functional theory (DFT) simulations unveil that the coupling of Mn doping with S vacancies synergistically tailors the localized electronic configuration and optimizes the adsorption free energies of reactive intermediates, thus accelerating the intrinsic reaction kinetics for HER and OER. This study combines multiple synergistic strategies, offering valuable design insights for developing efficient catalysts for sustainable hydrogen generation.

works.title: Stabilizing Zinc Coordination Chemistry and Interfacial Water Reactivity with Acetohydroxamic Acid for Highly Reversible Zinc Anodes
works.abstract: Abstract Zinc acetate electrolytes have attracted increasing attention for aqueous zinc-ion batteries owing to their intrinsic buffering capability, tunable coordination chemistry, and cost advantages. However, the dynamically evolving Zn2+ coordination environment, coupled with water-induced interfacial side reactions, leads to uneven Zn plating/stripping. Herein, acetohydroxamic acid (AHA), introduced at a concentration comparable to that of zinc acetate, serves as a compatible cosolute to simultaneously regulate Zn2+ coordination and interfacial water chemistry. Solvation analyses demonstrate that AHA participates in and reconstructs the Zn2+ coordination network through partial replacement of acetate in the primary solvation shell, thereby stabilizing the dynamically evolving coordination environment. Meanwhile, preferential adsorption of AHA on the Zn surface and the reorganized water hydrogen-bond network reduce interfacial water accessibility to reactive Zn sites. The cooperative regulation of coordination and interfacial water chemistry effectively suppresses water-induced parasitic reactions and promotes homogeneous Zn plating/stripping. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte delivers highly reversible stability for over 2500 h in Zn||Zn symmetric cells and enables an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.3% maintaining over 500 cycles in Zn||Cu cells. This work presents a cosolute-mediated strategy that synergistically stabilizes bulk Zn2+ coordination and interfacial water chemistry, providing new insights into electrolyte design for highly reversible zinc acetate-based aqueous batteries.

works.title: Value-Added Electrochemical Transformation of Polyethylene Terephthalate Waste into Formate over Se–NiCoP
works.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste into value-added chemicals provides a promising strategy for alleviating plastic pollution and recovering valuable products. Herein, a MOF-derived phosphorization and selenization strategy was employed to synthesize Se-modified nickel-cobalt phosphide catalysts for efficient PET electroreforming. By optimizing the P and Se contents, the optimized Se–NiCoP catalyst was obtained, which exhibited significantly enhanced catalytic performance toward the ethylene glycol oxidation reaction. At 500 mA cm–2, Se–NiCoP required a potential of only 1.36 V, which was 260 mV lower than that required for the oxygen evolution reaction. During the electrochemical upcycling process, PET-derived ethylene glycol was selectively converted into formate, and a high formate Faradaic efficiency of 93.5% was achieved with a production rate of 3 mmol cm–2 h–1. Further structural characterization revealed that NiOOH was generated on the catalyst surface after electrolysis, indicating that Se–NiCoP underwent surface reconstruction during the catalytic process. This work demonstrates a promising application of PET powder as a waste-derived feedstock for energy-saving electrochemical upgrading into high value-added chemicals.

works.title: Layered FeS-Regulated VO6 Framework Coupled with Carbon-Coating Charge Rearrangement Boosting Long-Cycled Na3V2(PO4)3 Cathode
works.abstract: Abstract Currently, the dissolution of active V in Na3V2(PO4)3 (NVP) leads to the inferior long-term cycling efficiency and poses potential thermal safety risks. To address these deficiencies, this study proposes a hydrothermal method that uses pre-synthesized layered FeS as a template, to successfully prepare a unique NVP@FeS composite with uniformly dispersed cluster-like morphology. FeS regulates the NVP surface to maintain its interfacial structural stability by forming FeN4 ligands under the induction of Fe2+. Notably, FeN4 not only enhances the electronic conductivity but also effectively suppresses the formation of organic functional groups in the CEI layer. The FeN4 ligand forms a complex with the active material via ligand molecular chains within the NaFePO4 composite phase, thereby optimizing the stability of the unit cell. The introduction of FeS significantly modifies the V–O bond. XAFS and simulations coherently demonstrate that the length of V–O bond length decreases, indicating that higher bond energy exists in the VO6 framework to maintain the structural stability and enhance the immobilization of V inside the NVP bulk. Moreover, in situ EIS and DRT measurements verify the superior kinetic characteristics at the heterogeneous interfaces of the NVP@FeS cathode. Furthermore, heteroatoms of S and N both enter in the coated carbon layers during the hydrothermal process, which occupy the C sites to induce the charge rearrangement to boost electronic transportation. ELF illustrates that charges accumulate at the N site and dissipate at the S site. The gradient configuration of the enriched charge distribution is relatively attractive for O and induces O vacancy inside NVP, which increases the hole carrier to accelerate ionic migration. Correspondingly, NVP@FeS-2 exhibits a high capacity of 125.6 mA h·g–1 at 0.1 C. After 4000 cycles at 20 C, it still retains 95.5 mA h·g–1 with a capacity retention rate as high as 92.7%. The ARC test shows that NVP@FeS exhibits a markedly higher onset temperature for exothermic reactions, while the total heat release is significantly reduced.

works.title: Constructing a Flower-Like Microspherical Multifunctional Co3O4-NiO/mSiO2 Heterostructure toward Synergistic Regulation of Polysulfide with Ultrafast Charge Transfer Kinetics
works.abstract: Abstract The shuttle effect of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) and their sluggish redox reaction kinetics severely impede the utilization efficiency of sulfur (S) and significantly deteriorate the cycling stability of lithium-sulfur (Li–S) batteries. Herein, a three-dimensional (3D) flower-like microspherical nanoarchitecture (Co3O4-NiO/mSiO2), in which the Co3O4-NiO heterojunction nanosheets are uniformly anchored onto mesoporous silica (mSiO2) nanospheres, is synthesized. This architecture is synthesized via a scalable hydrothermal approach. As a separator-modifying component, the mSiO2 nanospheres serve as structural templates, while the Co3O4-NiO heterointerfaces, rich in surface polar sites, provide dual functionality: (i) abundant chemical anchoring sites and intrinsically catalytic active sites for LiPSs, and (ii) a 3D mesoporous conductive network enabling efficient, coupled e–/Li+ transport. Owing to these advantages, the Li–S battery achieves an initial discharge capacity of 1017.6 mAh g–1 and retains 68% of that capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. Crucially, under realistic conditions of high S loading (5.1 mg cm–2) and lean electrolyte (E/S = 3.0 μL mg–1), the battery delivers a volumetric capacity of 804.1 Ah L–1 and an energy density of 1728.9 Wh L–1, retaining 864.5 Wh L–1 after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a prototype pouch battery delivered an initial discharge specific capacity of 986.3 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C with an elevated E/S ratio (5.5 μL mg–1). Collectively, this deep work demonstrate that rational engineering of a 3D heterostructured separator modifier constitutes a viable and scalable strategy toward practical high-energy-density Li–S batteries.

works.title: Spray-Coatable Porphyrin Polymers for Light-Assisted Gold Capture and In Situ Catalytic Valorization
works.abstract: Abstract The escalating accumulation of waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) has positioned it as a prominent “urban mine”. Consequently, the efficient recovery and subsequent valorization of gold (Au) from WEEE are essential for both resource sustainability and environmental conservation. In this study, an amide-linked porphyrin-based porous organic polymer (PyP) was synthesized via a facile polymerization reaction, complemented by a versatile in situ spray-coating strategy for substrate immobilization in practical applications. Attributed to its dense nitrogen-rich sites, stable porous architecture, and the inherent photocatalytic activity of its porphyrin macrocycles, PyP demonstrated an exceptional Au recovery capacity of up to 2454.8 mg g–1. Mechanistic insights reveal that this superior performance is governed by an “adsorption-reduction” pathway, where Au(Ⅲ) species undergo in situ reduction to Au NPs on the porphyrin framework. Benefiting from the robust optoelectronic synergy between the Au NPs and the porphyrin units, the resulting Au-PyP exhibits enhanced interfacial optoelectronic synergy, leading to a 3.6-fold enhancement in photocatalytic H2O2 generation and enabling highly efficient photo-Fenton degradation of tetracycline (>99%). Moreover, a PyP-functionalized nonwoven fabric (PyP/NWF) achieved a 97.79% recovery rate in real e-waste leachates and retained a tetracycline degradation efficiency exceeding 97% after five cycles, without detectable Au leaching. The macroscopic immobilized format allows facile solid-liquid separation, reduces material loss, improves device compatibility, and suppresses secondary Au release. This work offers a scalable paradigm for the integration of precious metal sequestration, in situ catalyst fabrication, and photocatalytic environmental remediation within a sustainable “waste to wealth” framework.

works.title: Composting performance, nitrogen retention, and microbial succession differ among urea-only and organic co-substrate-amended Camellia oleifera shell formulations
works.abstract: Camellia oleifera shell is a lignocellulosic by-product, and its inefficient decomposition limits waste reduction and nutrient recovery. To identify practical amendment strategies, we compared urea alone (CK) with urea combined with goat dung (GD), C. oleifera seed meal (CM), or rice bran (RB) in terms of nitrogen retention, compost maturation, and microbial succession during C. oleifera shell composting over 77 days. Organic co-amendments improved compost heating and prolonged thermophilic conditions relative to urea alone. RB achieved the highest nitrogen retention (91.64 ± 0.96%), whereas CK had the lowest measured inorganic nitrogen concentration. Co-amendments increased bacterial diversity and were associated with succession of fungal communities toward saprotrophy. Bacterial community patterns were related to the carbon/nitrogen (C/N) ratio, electrical conductivity (EC), and the extract optical index (E4/E6), while fungal succession was more strongly associated with composting time. Overall, supplementing urea with organic co-substrate was associated with nitrogen retention and several maturity indices relative to urea alone, although no single amendment performed best on every compost quality criterion. Although RB’s final total nutrient content was below the cited 4.0% criterion and final-product safety was not established, these findings provide a practical basis for converting C. oleifera shell into a more stable, nutrient-retaining compost and support the resource-efficient utilization of this agricultural by-product.

works.title: Improved recombinant protein production and scale-up fermentation of Aspergillus oryzae hyphal-dispersion hydrophobin-deficient strain
works.abstract: In liquid fermentation of filamentous fungi such as Aspergillus oryzae , increased broth viscosity and biomass adhesion to bioreactor surfaces remain major challenges. We previously developed a hyphal dispersion mutant lacking two hyphal adhesion factors, namely, cell wall α-1,3-glucan (AG) and biofilm galactosaminogalactan (GAG) (AGΔ-GAGΔ strain). The culture broth of the AGΔ-GAGΔ strain has low viscosity, which improves mixing and enzyme production. However, mycelia still extensively attach to bioreactor walls and downstream equipment, which impairs mixing and reduces product recovery. The hydrophobin RolA, a surface-active protein of A . oryzae , densely coats conidia and hyphae and contributes to cell surface hydrophobicity. In this study, we disrupted the rolA gene in AGΔ-GAGΔ (AGΔ-GAGΔ-Δ rolA strain) and evaluated the effects of this disruption on hyphal adhesion to the walls of culture vessels, enzyme production, and bioreactor performance. At the flask scale, the adhesion to glass surfaces was significantly reduced and activity of recombinant xylanase was increased by 14%. Improved culture recovery at the end of fermentation further increased total enzyme yield. In a lab-scale stirred-tank bioreactor (4 L), both growth and enzyme production were increased. In a 200-L bioreactor, xylanase activity was also higher in AGΔ-GAGΔ-Δ rolA and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis predicted improved hydrodynamic properties at equivalent volumetric power consumption. Fermentation of AGΔ-GAGΔ-Δ rolA was successfully scaled up to a 3000-L bioreactor. Overall, the AGΔ-GAGΔ-Δ rolA strain has increased enzyme production and scalability, supporting its suitability for industrial applications.

works.title: Biomechanical determinants of annular suture repair in an idealized post-discectomy annular defect: a finite element study
works.abstract: Background A residual annular defect after lumbar discectomy can allow recurrent nucleus pulposus (NP) displacement. Annular suturing may improve containment, but the roles of suture number, axial spring stiffness, placement, and edge apposition are unclear. Methods A public human L4-L5 finite element model was used to compare an intact disc, an unrepaired posterolateral full-thickness annular defect, open-gap repairs with one to three sutures, and graded three-suture partial-apposition repairs. The NP was retained, so the model represents an idealized post-discectomy defect. A 1-MPa expansive nucleus-boundary pressure preload was followed by axial compression to 2,000 N, with or without a 7.5-N m flexion moment. Primary outcomes were peak contained NP protrusion and the positive-only area under the protrusion-load curve (AUC). Rim stress and intradiscal pressure were secondary outcomes. Placement, suture number, axial spring stiffness, pretension, defect size, preload, and mesh density were varied in sensitivity analyses. Results The defect increased peak protrusion from 0.107 to 0.358 mm under pure compression and from 0.183 to 0.474 mm under flexion plus compression. Every primary load-targeted repair reduced protrusion. Open-gap repairs restored 29%–32% of the defect-to-intact AUC difference at 1 MPa and about 90% at 0.1 MPa. Among untensioned single sutures, only those crossing the deep, load-opening part of the defect produced large reductions. Suture number and axial spring stiffness changed peak protrusion by at most 1.0%. As the mean residual gap decreased from 1.69 to 0.80 mm, the AUC fell from 235 to 102 mm N under pure compression. Rim stress remained above intact in every repair. The ordering of repairs was robust, but the size of improvement depended on preload, protrusion definition, and mesh density. Conclusion In this idealized model, mechanically engaged suturing improved containment. Edge apposition and placement mattered more than suture number or axial spring stiffness. Improved containment did not normalize annular stress. Closing the protrusion pathway and restoring annular load transfer are therefore distinct goals.

works.title: Exogenous physical stimulation as a programmable input to bone immunometabolism: mechanisms, materials, and controversies
works.abstract: Bone repair materials are shifting from passive mechanical support toward active modulation of the host immune microenvironment, with immunometabolism linking material cues, macrophage state and bone regeneration. This non-registered, PRISMA-informed scoping review examines whether electrical and piezoelectric, ultrasound-driven piezoelectric or mechanical, near-infrared photothermal, photobiomodulation and magnetic stimulation can be regarded as programmable inputs to bone immunometabolism. Europe PMC, OpenAlex, PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus were searched from January 2021 to October 2026. The five database exports yielded 4,146 records; DOI/title de-duplication removed 1,957 duplicates, leaving 2,189 records screened. Screening retained 104 candidates; 102 full texts were verified. 85 primary research articles and 17 contextual records. Seventy-four primary articles contributed 75 input-class entries; only one delivered two independent inputs. Evidence connects stimulation, metabolic change, immune phenotype and bone outcome, but not within one validated causal chain. Only three studies reported both an extracellular flux/OCR measurement and immunophenotyping in macrophages, with attribution limited by separate experiments, co-delivery or assessment at only the selected dose. No study measured flux and phenotype across multiple matched doses. Clinical evidence remains uncertain because a network meta-analysis produced imprecise estimates and the TRUST trial found no acceleration of radiographic healing or functional recovery with low-intensity pulsed ultrasound. Four methodological problems persist: incompatible dose windows, incomplete causal attribution, over-reliance on M1/M2 labels and interpretation of pathway-protein changes as metabolic flux. Across 18 ultrasound-driven piezoelectric and 21 near-infrared photothermal entries, intensity was reported in 15 and 20, duration in 11 and 19, and temperature in 0 and 12; no entry reported CEM43. Programmable control therefore remains a hypothesis until target-site dose or field exposure, flux and function are measured together and reporting is standardized.

works.title: Controlling CRISPR: a review of current anti-CRISPR technologies
works.abstract: Anti-CRISPR systems are emerging as essential regulators of CRISPR-Cas technologies, providing a controllable “off-switch” for genome editing, transcriptional regulation, and gene-drive applications. This review surveys the expanding landscape of anti-CRISPR strategies, including naturally occurring Acr proteins, engineered Acr switches, small-molecule inhibitors, and nucleic acid-based inhibitors. Acr proteins, discovered in phages and other mobile genetic elements, exploit diverse mechanisms such as blocking CRISPR-Cas complex assembly, preventing target DNA or RNA binding, or directly inhibiting catalysis. Recent work has revealed additional noncanonical mechanisms, including RNA mimicry, host-factor hijacking, and enzymatic modifications of Cas proteins. In parallel, computational screening and machine-learning methods have accelerated discovery of Acr families and enabled de novo design of Cas13 inhibitors. This review also examines engineered control systems that make Acr activity conditional on chemical, light, miRNA, protease, or other environmental cues, enabling spatial and temporal regulation of CRISPR function. Small-molecule inhibitors and nucleic-acid inhibitors offer complementary CRISPR control, including the potential for improved delivery, tunable dosing, and modular design, though further assessment in therapeutic applications is necessary. Across applications, anti-CRISPRs have shown utility in improving editing precision, reducing toxicity, constraining gene drives, controlling CRISPRi/CRISPRa systems, and enhancing safety in therapeutic and agricultural contexts. Despite substantial progress, important challenges remain, including delivery, specificity across natural and engineered CRISPR variants, and governance. Future efforts will likely focus on rational design, multiplexed inhibition, and integration of anti-CRISPR systems into existing CRISPR-Cas therapeutic and environmental frameworks. As CRISPR continues to expand beyond the laboratory into medicine, agriculture, and ecological engineering, anti-CRISPR technologies will play a central role in enabling safer and more precise genome engineering.

works.title: Position-associated intraluminal flow disturbance in idealized straight anal fistula tracts under sphincter loading: a clinically motivated proof-of-concept fluid–structure interaction study
works.abstract: Background Anal fistula management remains clinically challenging because durable eradication of fistulous sepsis must be balanced against preservation of sphincter function. Although current surgical concepts emphasize fistula anatomy, internal-opening management, and drainage of septic tracts, the potential contribution of sphincter-induced biomechanical loading to intraluminal flow organization remains insufficiently explored. This clinically motivated proof-of-concept study investigated whether tract position within the sphincter complex is associated with different flow-disturbance patterns under controlled idealized conditions. Methods A female anal sphincter complex was reconstructed from pelvic MRI using Mimics and 3-Matic. Two idealized straight cylindrical synthetic fistula tracts with an identical diameter of 3 mm were embedded at anterior and lateral positions within the same anatomical model. Bidirectional fluid–structure interaction (FSI) simulations were performed using ANSYS Workbench. Standardized pseudocolor velocity maps from 0.01 to 0.06 s were processed using lumen region-of-interest R O I definition, color-to-velocity mapping, normalized velocity-index calculation, low-velocity segmentation, connected-component analysis, axial segmentation, and temporal reorganization analysis. Results Both configurations showed very low Reynolds numbers, consistent with viscosity-dominated laminar flow. Compared with the lateral tract, the anterior tract showed a lower mean velocity index 0.431 vs. 0.547, lower image-derived mean velocity 3.08 × 10 −3 vs. 3.91 × 10 −3 m/s, and higher low-velocity fraction 0.613 vs. 0.419 using the primary threshold of 0.4× v max . The anterior tract also showed a larger normalized maximum connected low-velocity area 0.593 vs. 0.328 and a more broadly distributed axial low-velocity burden. The anterior configuration demonstrated earlier and more sustained low-velocity organization, whereas the lateral configuration showed relatively preserved early flow followed by greater late-phase expansion and temporal reorganization. Conclusion In this idealized single-anatomy model, tract position was associated with distinct intraluminal flow-disturbance descriptors under sphincter loading. These findings do not establish a clinical mechanism of recurrence or predict failure of sphincter-preserving procedures. Rather, they provide preliminary biomechanical evidence supporting future patient-specific studies that incorporate realistic tract geometries, male and female anatomies, posterior configurations, biological variability, and clinical validation.

works.title: Animal models in peripheral nerve regeneration: from biological mechanisms to translational therapies
works.abstract: Peripheral nerve injuries remain a major clinical challenge, as functional recovery is often incomplete despite advances in microsurgical reconstruction and rehabilitation strategies. Animal models have played a central role in advancing the understanding of peripheral nerve regeneration, providing essential insights into the cellular and molecular processes involved in nerve degeneration, repair, and functional recovery following injury. Furthermore, they remain important for evaluating the safety, efficacy, and translational potential of emerging therapeutic strategies. This review examines the contribution of animal models to peripheral nerve regeneration research, focusing on their role across the translational pathway from mechanistic investigations to preclinical validation. The biological basis of nerve regeneration is discussed alongside the advantages and limitations of commonly used animal models, including rodents, rabbits, pigs, sheep, and non-human primates. The review also discusses how these models have been used to evaluate growth factor-based therapies, stem cell and cell-free approaches, biomaterials, nerve guidance conduits, bioelectronic interventions, and gene-based strategies. Current translational challenges, including species-related differences, long-gap defects, outcome assessment, and ethical considerations, are also addressed. Finally, emerging directions in regenerative medicine, bioengineering, extracellular vesicle therapies, advanced biomaterials, and gene modulation are explored. Collectively, the evidence highlights the continuing importance of animal models in bridging fundamental discoveries and clinical implementation, while emphasizing the need for clinically relevant preclinical frameworks to improve the translation of regenerative therapies for peripheral nerve repair.

works.title: Extracellular vesicle-loaded hydrogels for diabetic bone healing
works.abstract: The bone healing cascade is initiated by an inflammatory response, which in turn mediates regenerative repair and culminates in the restoration of bone tissue. An imbalanced immune response during the early stage of bone regeneration disrupts the healing cascade, delaying bone healing and compromising therapeutic outcomes. Diabetes induces oxidative stress and inflammation, disturbs bone metabolism, increases the risk of infection, decreases bone scaffold efficacy, and hinders bone defect repair. Interest in the use of smart hydrogels with precise stimulus responsiveness in bone repair and regeneration has increased. Integrated responsive groups or nanoparticles enable them to regulate the local microenvironment and facilitate bone regeneration. However, challenges remain due to fragility and poor tissue adhesion of hydrogels. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) serve as promising cell-free candidates for bone repair, yet direct injection leads to fast capture and elimination, curbing therapeutic outcomes. Hydrogel carriers modified with EVs are adopted to increase vesicle retention and repair performance. This paper summarizes the updated progress in the use of vesicle-loaded scaffolds for bone regeneration, covering vesicle origins and biomaterial combination tactics. It further clarifies relevant repair mechanisms, analyzes clinical translation hurdles, and proposes optimization directions for high-efficiency vesicles. These findings offer reference data for the design of advanced vesicle-based implants to facilitate bone recovery under diabetic conditions.

works.title: Reading the wrist as a mechanical observer of the collapsing pharynx: biomechanical inference of upper-airway soft tissue loading from wearable signals
works.abstract: The pharynx is a collapsible soft-tissue conduit whose patency is a mechanical equilibrium between intraluminal loading and tissue elastance, yet the transmural pressure that governs its collapse is accessible only through invasive laboratory manometry. Here, we reframe wearable sleep monitoring as inference over mechanically motivated surrogates of pharyngeal loading. From a Starling resistor and tube law description of pharyngeal collapse, we derive an explicit mapping from each wearable modality—photoplethysmography, electrocardiography, accelerometry, oximetry, and respiratory effort—to the mechanical term it is expected to reflect, casting the sensor array as a distributed set of mechanical observers of one collapse event. Three innovations follow: self-supervised pre-training restricted to mechanically admissible augmentations, retained only when a perturbed view remains a physically realizable airway state; a redundancy-aware fusion that combines correlated observers through a Sharpe-ratio-maximizing, closed-form weighting over their information covariance; and a proposed cumulative load index, formulated in the shape of a classical injury criterion, that summarizes a night of recording as an uncalibrated exposure to obstructive loading rather than an event count; the index is introduced as a hypothesis, not as a validated mechanical dose. Across two polysomnographic cohorts spanning ages 18–94, the framework surpasses 13 baselines in collapse detection and in three-way loading regime classification—sustained, absent, or delayed-onset loading—in both cohorts and retains its advantage when observers are lost, both under controlled channel dropout and under zero-shot transfer with only the two observers shared by the two corpora.

works.title: Al 2 O 3 ‐incorporated CuO / ZnO / MnO 2 ‐based catalysts for selective glycerol carbonate synthesis from glycerol under mild conditions
works.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Glycerol carbonate (GC) is a valuable glycerol‐derived chemical, and the development of efficient heterogeneous catalytic systems for its synthesis is important for sustainable glycerol valorization. RESULTS In this work, Al 2 O 3 ‐incorporated CuO/ZnO/MnO 2 ‐based catalysts were prepared by co‐precipitation for the transesterification of glycerol (GL) with dimethyl carbonate (DMC). The catalysts were characterized by XRD, FT‐IR, TGA, NH 3 ‐TPD, BET, XPS, and SEM, and the effects of catalyst composition and reaction conditions on catalytic performance were systematically investigated. Among the catalysts examined, the sample with a Cu/Mn molar ratio of 1:2 exhibited the best performance. Under the optimized conditions of 90 °C, 1.5 h, GL/DMC = 1:5, and 3 wt.% catalyst loading, a GC yield of 95.3% with high selectivity was obtained, and the catalyst retained acceptable catalytic performance over repeated cycles. Kinetic and thermodynamic analyses suggested that the reaction proceeds through a Langmuir–Hinshelwood–Hougen–Watson (LHHW)‐type pathway. CONCLUSION Overall, the results indicate that Al 2 O 3 incorporation provides an effective strategy for tuning the structure, stability, and catalytic behavior of CuO/ZnO/MnO 2 ‐based catalysts for selective GC synthesis under relatively mild reaction conditions. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: Severing the “Switch” of Reverse Current Decay Grants Dynamic Adaptability to Proton Exchange Membrane Electrolyzers
works.abstract: Abstract The direct integration of proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) with intermittent renewable energy sources induces severe degradation during frequent start-stop cycling. Although operational strategies can alleviate generic power fluctuations, the intrinsic failure mechanisms of PEMWEs under stepwise dynamic conditions have not been fully clarified. In this study, we investigate the multi-pathway degradation behavior of PEMWEs under high-frequency current step variations and examine the possible contribution of zero-current intervals to degradation. We further reveal that zero-current intervals involve reverse current associated with electrochemical processes, accompanied by residual gases, catalyst structural deterioration, and membrane degradation. To mitigate this degradation, we introduce a titanium mesh-reinforced anode configuration that improves mechanical stability and mitigates localized voltage overshoot. Benefiting from this structural optimization, the PEMWE enables stable operation for 300 h under high-frequency stepwise fluctuations, with a low degradation rate of 0.18 mV h–1. Crucially, a seven-day photovoltaic-electrolysis field test further confirms stable start-stop operation of the optimized electrolyzer under real-world solar irradiance. By elucidating the interplay between electrochemical dynamics and structural evolution, this work proposes a practical engineering strategy verified via laboratory accelerated aging tests and outdoor photovoltaic-electrolysis field tests, which supports the development of applicable green hydrogen systems.

works.title: Selective Electrooxidation of Ethylene Glycol to Formate with Green Hydrogen in Co–O–Fe Clusters via Electron Localization-Mediated Dual-Site Synergy
works.abstract: Abstract The electrocatalytic upgrading of waste plastic-derived ethylene glycol to value-added chemicals is a promising route toward a circular carbon economy, yet it remains challenged by the lack of efficient non-noble catalysts with well-defined active sites and well-elucidated synergistic mechanisms. Herein, we report a fundamental study that goes beyond catalyst development to unveil a unique electron-buffering mechanism within Co–O–Fe clusters in CoFe-layered double hydroxide. This effect, coupled with the nanoneedle architecture, enables exceptional ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR) performance. A current density of 50 mA cm–2 is achieved at 1.52 V vs reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), and a formate Faradaic efficiency of 92.02% is reached at 1.7 V vs RHE after 6 h of electrolysis. More importantly, through a combination of in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, we decipher the distinct roles of the dual sites: Fe sites act as electron reservoirs, stabilizing low-valence Co, and, synergizing with Jahn–Teller distortion, primarily facilitate dehydrogenation and C–H activation. In turn, the Co sites are identified as the active centers for the directional cleavage of the C–C bond in glycolate/glyoxylate intermediates. Electron transfer through the Co–O–Fe bridge dynamically modulates the energy landscape of intermediates, steering the pathway selectively toward formate. When implemented in a coupled HER∥EGOR electrolyzer, this mechanism enables low-energy hydrogen production (5.97 kWh m–3). Our work provides atomic-level insight into cooperative electrocatalysis, offering a new design paradigm for the green and high-value transformation of carbon-based plastics.

works.title: Sericin-Inspired Multilevel Supramolecular Networks Enable Strong and Cold-Pressable Gelatin-Based Wood Adhesives
works.abstract: Abstract This study aims to address the challenge of developing formaldehyde-free wood adhesives with high strength, high toughness, and low-temperature processability. Inspired by the cooperative organization of sericin, a Gel/LA/TA bio-based adhesive was designed by integrating gelatin (Gel) as a continuous protein scaffold with α-lipoic acid (LA) and tannic acid (TA) to construct a multicomponent supramolecular network. Multiscale analyses revealed that LA and TA altered the molecular environment of gelatin, disrupted LA crystallinity, restricted molecular mobility, and promoted the formation of a dense supramolecular network dominated by hydrogen bonding and other noncovalent interactions. After 24 h postpress conditioning at room temperature, Gel/LA/TA-bonded plywood exhibited shear strengths of 2.7 MPa and 3.6 MPa for specimens pressed at 25 °C and 120 °C, respectively. Its delamination work reached 2591.21 N·m–1, representing a 474.2% increase over gelatin. The wood fiber pull-out and bridging at the fracture surface, along with a wood destruction rate of approximately 90%, demonstrated enhanced interfacial load transfer capability. Comparison with the control group containing octanoic acid indicates that the disulfide-containing structure of LA contributed additional reinforcement to the adhesive network. The Gel/LA/TA adhesive also exhibited thermally assisted self-healing behavior and adhesion to multiple substrates, and outperformed conventional phenolic resins in most environmental impact indicators in a life cycle assessment. This study provides a supramolecular design practical strategy for developing high-performance, low temperature processable, and environmentally friendly gelatin-based wood adhesives.

works.title: Systematic Evaluation of Membrane Materials and Process Design Trade-offs for Hydrogen Deblending
works.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen can play an important role as a fuel or feedstock in various industries, but transportation of hydrogen is challenging. Hydrogen blending with natural gas in existing natural gas pipelines can leverage the existing infrastructure to expand access to hydrogen for unconventional end uses. However, this approach would require on-point separation technologies to deblend the hydrogen from natural gas. This study evaluates the performance of 224 membrane materials, including polymers and carbon molecular sieves, for purity and required area in a single-stage system for hydrogen deblending. A two-stage membrane cascade is optimized for recovery of a target purity, and the costs of hydrogen recovery are estimated. We demonstrate that fuel-grade A hydrogen can be deblended at $0.320 kg–1 H2, but with a recovery of 84%. The costs are found to be most sensitive to the electricity cost and the cost of annualization of capital expenditures. Compared with other hydrogen transport options, the blending–deblending approach is economically favorable for long-distance H2 delivery.

works.title: New Vistas into Intensified Production Alternatives for Food Waste-Derived Novel Proteins
works.abstract: Abstract Alternative protein technologies are overwhelmingly designed and assessed for high-income markets, yet the regions with the greatest protein deficiency are rare where such processes are first deployed. Here, we close that gap for food waste-derived single-cell protein (SCP) by coupling multilevel process intensification with scenario-resolved technoeconomic and life-cycle assessment. We generate three SCP configurations from food waste biogas and evaluate each under three hydrogen/electricity scenarios through cradle-to-gate life-cycle assessment, Monte Carlo technoeconomic analysis, and first-of-a-kind deployment projection. Only co-cultivation of methanotrophic and hydrogenotrophic bacteria powered by dedicated renewable electricity approaches economic viability, with a minimum product selling price (MPSP) of $3.59/kg, an 11.5% probability of a positive net present value, and a global warming potential of 1.02 kg CO2-eq/kg SCP. The hydrogen and electricity supply route dominates the carbon footprint, and its effect on cost is comparable to that of process topology. First-of-a-kind plants carry a 73% premium over the mature cost. A 50-country overlay coupling socioeconomic viability with protein deficiency identifies 20 priority targets on a combined viability-need screen.

works.title: Quantitative Benchmarking of Ritter Amidation: A Sustainability Perspective Inspired by Roger A. Sheldon
works.abstract: Abstract Roger A. Sheldon transformed Green Chemistry by demonstrating that the sustainability of chemical processes should be evaluated through objective quantitative metrics rather than qualitative claims of “greenness”. Building on this philosophy, this perspective benchmarks representative Ritter amidation methodologies using harmonized reaction-level boundaries and complementary green chemistry metrics, including carbon efficiency (CE), reaction mass efficiency (RME), process mass intensity (PMI), complete and simplified E-factors (sE-factor), solvent intensity (SI), and EcoScale. The comparison demonstrates that catalyst innovation and high isolated yield do not necessarily translate into improved sustainability. Instead, material consumption, particularly excess nitrile, reaction-medium demand, and downstream processing, dominates the environmental profile of most methodologies. At the reaction level, and within the benzamide series, solvent-free Ritter amidation provides the most favorable balance between synthetic performance and material efficiency; scale-up readiness is discussed qualitatively.

works.title: Recovery Boiler or Fuel Route? Consequential Break-Even Conditions for the Use of Kraft Prehydrolysis Liquor
works.abstract: Abstract Kraft mills that produce dissolving-grade pulp burn their prehydrolysis liquor in the recovery boiler. We quantify when converting this liquor to hydrocarbon fuels, at constant pulp output, lowers the climate impact of the mill. A consequential ex-ante life cycle assessment compares combustion with two routes scaled from the laboratory to industrial operation: one-step hydrodeoxygenation of furfural to hydrocarbons (HC route) and five-step synthesis of aviation-range hydrocarbons (AF route). The difference between each route and combustion is a linear function of the carbon intensities of the marginal heat and electricity, the supplies that respond to a change in demand, so the break-even conditions form maps on which any mill can be located. In Sweden, with steam-reformed hydrogen, the HC route lowers climate impact by 0.0537 kgCO2-eq per kg of pulp, but only where the marginal heat emits less than 0.0198 kgCO2-eq per MJ, as biomass heat does and natural gas does not. The AF route has a higher climate impact than combustion at any marginal intensity, by 0.333 kgCO2-eq per kg of pulp in its demonstrated sequence and, at best, by less than the uncertainty of the background data. In twelve of fifteen other impact categories, combustion has the lower impact.

works.title: Lubricate, Degrade, and Fertilize: A Multifunctional Superlubricating Hydrogel Inspired by Dolphin Skin
works.abstract: Abstract Engineering materials generally face challenges in simultaneously achieving high load-bearing capacity, superlubricity, and biodegradability. Additionally, they may impose an environmental burden upon disposal. Inspired by the microstructure of dolphin skin, this study developed a multifunctional superlubricating hydrogel composed of yam extract-PEGDA. It also proposed a dual-mechanism model in which micron-scale pore structures and hydration layer induced by hydrogen bonding synergistically contribute to the superlubricating performance. The hydrogel exhibits instantaneous superhydrophilicity, with a friction coefficient as low as 0.00191 under a contact pressure of 1.368 MPa. After 180 min of operation, the volumetric efficiency of the water hydraulic circular gear pump dropped to 58.3% with the uncoated bearing but remained at 82.7% with the hydrogel-coated bearing. After 30 days of soil incubation, the hydrogel showed ∼15.1% mass loss. Moreover, 14-day cultivation showed that soil with degraded hydrogel increased lettuce dry weight by ∼126.3% compared to the control group. This material combines the potential for sustained water-based lubrication with degradation-induced soil fertilization, providing a new strategy for developing green biomimetic lubricating materials.

works.title: Modulating NO3–/H2O Competitive Adsorption via a Defective ZnO/Cu Single–Atom for Ammonia Electrosynthesis
works.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NitRR) offers a sustainable route for nitrate removal and ammonia production, yet its efficiency is limited by sluggish multistep kinetics and competitive hydrogen evolution. Herein, a CuSA–ZnO@CW electrocatalyst was constructed by stabilizing O–coordinated Cu single atoms on defective ZnO supported by carbonized wood. The conductive wood-derived scaffold facilitates mass/electron transport, while the defective ZnO/Cu–O3 interface regulates local adsorption competition between NO3– and H2O. CuSA–ZnO@CW delivers an NH3 yield of 3561.9 μg h–1 cm–2 and a Faradaic efficiency of 97.07% at –1.1 V vs RHE, with stable performance over 36 cycles. Mechanistic studies reveal that ZnO preferentially accommodates interfacial H2O, whereas Cu–O3 sites selectively activate NO3– and promote NOX intermediate conversion, thereby reducing the free-energy requirement of the potential-determining step and suppressing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). This work presents a defective oxide–regulated single–atom interface for selective NO3– to NH3 conversion.

works.title: High-Throughput Biomining of Insect Proteins for Earthen Material Stabilization
works.abstract: Abstract Here, for the first time, the potential of insect biomass as a source of biopolymer stabilizers for earthen materials is explored. To address the heterogeneity, complexity, and combinatorial intensity associated with optimizing insect biopolymer-stabilized earthen materials, a micro-to-macro experimental pipeline, the Rapid Extraction and Binding Assessment Technique (REBAT) is introduced. By combining multiwell platforms with UV analysis, REBAT increases the rate of discovery of biopolymer stabilizers by ∼500 times compared with traditional trial-and-error approaches and ∼150 times compared with existing micro-to-macro methodologies. Using REBAT, strength gains in kaolinite earth stabilized with extracted cricket-, silkworm-, and locust-derived biopolymers (1.7–2.2×, up to 2.18 MPa) were found to strongly correlate with the mass of extracted protein (R2 = 0.66). Complementary microscale analyses (XRD, ATR-FTIR, and zeta potential analysis) indicated that stabilization arises from protein β-sheet structures forming van der Waals interfacial interactions between clay platelets. Through this framework, locust protein biomass rich in β-sheet structures emerged as the optimal source of biopolymer stabilizers for kaolinite earthen material stabilization. This high-throughput characterization pipeline provides a scalable, data-driven strategy for discovering new biopolymer stabilizers for earthen construction from mixed biomass sources.

works.title: Current Collector Augmented Reductive Dissolution of Spent Li-Ion Battery Black Mass for Regeneration of NMC622 Cathode
works.abstract: Abstract Overcoming reliance on strong acid and external reductants in the hydrometallurgical recycling of spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) offers a promising pathway toward an environmentally benign and cost-effective strategy. In this study, we developed a current collector augmented reductive dissolution strategy using a mild phosphorus oxoacid as the hydrometallurgical leaching medium. The process utilizes aluminum current collector already present in the spent LIB black mass as an in situ reducing agent. Importantly, the proposed system addresses two key limitations of previously reported aluminum-assisted leaching processes, i.e., reliance on strongly acidic conditions and sluggish leaching kinetics, by operating under milder acidic conditions while exhibiting accelerated leaching kinetics. At optimized conditions, the process achieved maximum leaching efficiencies of approximately 94%, 89%, and 91% for Ni, Co, and Li, respectively. This reductive pathway lowered the leaching activation energy to below 13 kJ mol–1, indicating favorable dissolution kinetics. The transition metals are selectively retrieved as oxalates by means of chemical precipitation with more than 98% yield and subsequently used as precursors to synthesize LiNi0.6Mn0.2Co0.2O2 (rNMC). rNMC exhibits a well-ordered layered hexagonal structure with minimal cation mixing and successfully emulates the electrochemical performance of its commercial counterparts. During the initial galvanostatic cycle, rNMC demonstrated a discharge specific capacity of 131 mAh g–1 at 1C across an elevated potential window of 2.9–4.5 V, tested in a Li|rNMC half-cell. At 1C, the half-cell showed a remarkable capacity retention of 71% after 1000 cycles, indicating excellent electrochemical stability. This investigation demonstrates a mild and effective reductive dissolution pathway for the selective recovery of transition metals and repurposing them as LIB cathode active material. The proposed route is cost-effective and has potential for future scale-up.

works.title: Entropy Engineering and Multi-Metal Synergy Stabilize Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes for Long-Life Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
works.abstract: Abstract Prussian blue analogues (PBAs), owing to their distinctive three-dimensional open framework structures featuring wide ion channels and excellent structural tunability, have drawn increasing attention as promising cathode materials for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). However, their electrochemical cycling stability is often hindered by the dissolution of transition-metal ions and structural degradation induced by intrinsic defects and coordinated water molecules. To address these limitations, a high-entropy Prussian blue analogue (HE-PBA) cathode material was synthesized by incorporating five transition metals (Mn, Co, Ni, Zn, and Cu) into the M1 sites. The resulting material demonstrates a reduced defects density and a lower level of coordinated water (K1.68(Mn0.22Co0.20Ni0.19Zn0.20Cu0.19)[Fe(CN)6]0.96□0.04·0.37H2O). Electrochemical tests reveal that the entropy-driven “cocktail effect” synergistically stabilizes the crystal framework and facilitates rapid Zn2+ diffusion. The M5HCF cathode delivers outstanding long-term cycling stability, retaining 62 mAh g–1 after 10,000 cycles, with an ultralow capacity decay of 0.0016% per cycle, and excellent rate capability (69 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1). Ex situ XPS tracks the dynamic evolution of M–N vs Fe–C redox contributions during cycling, clarifying the origin of the gradual plateau changes. These findings offer a practical strategy for durable AZIB cathodes.

works.title: De-inking and delamination: keeping plastic packaging in mechanical recycling
Turnstile metal–organic framework for the efficient separation of cyclic C6 hydrocarbons
Orientational locking in a turnstile metal–organic framework for cyclohexene/cyclohexane separation
Using industrial ecology to avoid burden shifting
Upgrading yeast-based low-carbon biomanufacturing by harnessing a universal in vivo evolution system
Reprogrammed E. coli for secretion of thermophilic cellulase cocktail for seawater-compatible lignocellulosic bioprocessing
works.abstract: Efficient, low-cost cellulase systems are essential for sustainable lignocellulosic biorefining, yet current platforms remain constrained by high production costs, reliance on downstream purification, and dependence on freshwater processing conditions. In this study, we engineered Escherichia coli to co-express and secrete a thermophilic cellulase cocktail consisting of a Bacillus licheniformis processive endoglucanase (H1AD14), a Chaetomium thermophilum cellobiohydrolase (G0SAE6), and a glucose-tolerant engineered β-glucosidase B8CYA8tm (V169C/E173L/I246A B8CYA8) from Halothermothrix orenii . N-terminal tagging with AnsB signal peptide enabled extracellular yields of 0.2–0.4 g/L for each enzyme, bypassing costly purification while retaining activity. The secretion was confirmed via immunoblotting using anti-His antibody, and catalytic activity was validated through enzymatic assays. The absence of E. coli native periplasmic maltose-binding protein (detected with anti-MBP antibody) in the extracellular medium ruled out cell lysis, confirming protein secretion. Using the Golden Gate assembly, we constructed and systematically evaluated synergistic enzyme combinations for hydrolytic performance. By optimizing secretion conditions, including media, inducer concentration, and incubation temperature, the total yield of secreted enzyme cocktail increased from 0.31 g/L to 0.74 g/L. The secreted cocktail effectively hydrolysed diverse lignocellulosic substrates and exhibited 100% activity in seawater, demonstrating potential for freshwater-independent biorefining. By combining secretion engineering, thermostability, and seawater tolerance in a single E. coli platform, this work offers a scalable, purification-free strategy for cellulase production that addresses key economic and environmental barriers to freshwater-independent lignocellulosic biorefining.

works.title: Engineering yeast consortia by partitioning glucose and multiple organic-acid utilization to enhance β-carotene production from simulated distillery wastewater
works.abstract: Synthetic microbial consortia (SMC) have emerged as a promising platform, often outperforming monocultures in metabolic efficiency. Despite this potential, the simultaneous co-utilization of glucose and diverse organic acids in wastewater for value-added chemical production remains a significant technical challenge. In this study, to achieve simultaneous co-utilization of glucose, lactate, and acetate to enable β-carotene production, an engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain Sc -CarLA was first constructed by introducing the lactate utilization pathway from Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 and the acetate metabolism pathway from Escherichia coli into the original S. cerevisiae strain Sc -Car. However, severe competition between glucose and organic acids metabolism significantly hindered fermentation, resulting in reduced carbon source consumption and ultimately yielding only 30.9 ± 2.7 mg/L of β-carotene, a ~32% decrease compared to the original strain Sc -Car. To overcome this bottleneck, a novel SMC was first proposed and constructed, which separates the glucose metabolic pathway from the organic acid utilization pathway into two specialized strains. A glucose-specialist strain Sc -CarG1 was constructed by deleting the ADY2 gene, which encodes a vital organic acid transporter, from strain Sc -Car. Concurrently, an organic acids specialist strain, Sc -CarLA2, was constructed by deleting glucose transporter genes GAL2 and HXT1-7 . Subsequently, the co-culture of these two strains, Sc -CarG1 and Sc -CarLA2, exhibited improved fermentation performance, rapidly depleting glucose within 12 h and completely consuming acetate and lactate within 36 h. A two-parallel regulatory strategy, compositional division of labor (DOL) of microbes and temporal DOL, was then employed to further optimize the fermentation performance. As a result, the β-carotene titer in the compositional DOL system reached 64.0 ± 1.5 mg/L at the optimal cell ratio of 1:2 ( Sc -CarG1: Sc -CarLA2). Finally, the temporal DOL system, characterized by the sequential inoculation of the organic acids-specialist strain Sc -CarLA2 followed by the glucose-specific strain Sc -CarG1, enhanced the β-carotene titer to 71.9 ± 2.8 mg/L. A novel SMC that partitions the glucose metabolism pathway and organic acids utilization pathways into two specialist strains was first constructed, efficiently alleviating the bottleneck caused by carbon catabolite repression between glucose and organic acid metabolism, thereby facilitating rapid utilization of carbon sources and significantly boosting β-carotene production.

works.title: Integrated no‐cook and high gravity ethanol technology from cassava: laboratory‐to‐pilot scale toward sustainable and low‐energy biofuel production
works.abstract: Abstract A no‐cook or simultaneous liquefaction, saccharification, and fermentation technology at very high gravity using cassava flour at 270 g L −1 at ambient temperature for bio‐ethanol production was developed at both the lab scale (1 L) and pilot scale (1000 L) in this work. The effects of auxiliary enzymes, yeast nutrients, and different dosages of starch‐hydrolyzing enzymes on ethanol production were investigated. Supplementation with cellulase, β ‐glucanase, and complex yeast nutrients showed no significant improvement in ethanol yield. In contrast, increasing the dosages of Stargen 002 (a granular starch‐hydrolyzing enzyme containing α ‐amylase and glucoamylase) at 2565 GAU kg −1 cassava flour and Amigase Mega L (glucoamylase) at 1.05 g kg −1 significantly enhanced fermentation performance. Under these conditions, ethanol concentrations of 14.4 and 14.0% v/v were achieved at laboratory and pilot scales, corresponding to fermentation yields of 86 and 83.66%, respectively. The simultaneous liquefaction, saccharification, and fermentation–very high gravity process demonstrated clear economic and environmental benefits, with pilot‐scale water and energy consumption of 16.57 L and 8.48 MJ per liter of ethanol, respectively. Replacing 32% of grid electricity with biomass enabled greenhouse gas emissions to match those of conventional technology while preserving energy savings, with further substitution making the process environmentally superior. At an industrial scale, reduced cassava and electricity costs significantly improved profitability, lowering production costs to 0.642 USD L −1 ethanol. In addition, cassava‐based distiller's dried grains showed potential as an animal feed co‐product with high fiber content (28.97%) and a moderate protein content (13.26%), highlighting the integrated no‐cook very high gravity system as a promising pathway for sustainable bioethanol production and circular bioeconomy development in Vietnam, improving resource efficiency and circularity as well as supporting Vietnam's national strategies for renewable energy transition.

works.title: Multifunctional tetramethylpyrazine-loaded carbomer gel for cutaneous radioprotection against radiation dermatitis
works.abstract: Background Radiation-induced dermatitis represents a common adverse reaction following tumor radiotherapy, and effective prophylactic and therapeutic approaches remain limited. Tetramethylpyrazine (TMP) exhibits promising anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. Nevertheless, its poor skin retention and incompletely elucidated molecular mechanisms targeting radiation-induced dermatitis restrict its clinical utility. As a clinically-approved pharmaceutical excipient, Carbopol® 940 imparts desirable skin-adhesive characteristics to gel formulations. Methods In this study, a TMP-loaded functional Carbopol® 940 gel (TMP-gel) with favorable translational potential was developed. Its therapeutic efficacy and underlying molecular mechanisms for alleviating radiation-induced dermatitis were systematically evaluated. Results In vitro cellular assays demonstrated that TMP-gel triggers the Nrf2 antioxidant cascade, suppresses NF-κB-mediated pro-inflammatory signaling, and inhibits pathological over-activation of Wnt/β-catenin signal transduction. In vivo experiments confirmed the potent therapeutic activity of the gel against radiation-induced dermatitis. Conclusion This multifunctional tetramethylpyrazine-loaded carbomer gel provides a novel biomedical platform enabling non-invasive concurrent prevention and intervention for radiation-provoked skin injury during tumor radiotherapy.

works.title: Effect of anterior and posterior horn suture stiffness on the biomechanical performance of a medial meniscal prosthesis: a finite element analysis
works.abstract: Background Meniscal injury is a common musculoskeletal disease. An artificial meniscal prosthesis is an effective choice for replacing allograft transplantation of the meniscus; however, the best method of fixation is still controversial. This finite element study aims to investigate the biomechanical effect of various anterior and posterior horn suture stiffnesses on a medial meniscal prosthesis under different knee flexion angles. Methods A validated three-dimensional finite element model of a human knee joint was used. A medial meniscal prosthesis of polycarbonate urethane (PCU) material was implanted, and spring elements were used to simulate the anterior and posterior horn fixation sutures and four levels of stiffness (13, 25, 62, and 200 N/mm) to represent available suture materials in the clinic. Knee flexion angles of 0°, 30°, and 60° were applied with combined anterior tibial load (134 N), compressive load (1150 N), and internal rotation moment (4 Nm). Tensile force in the sutures, meniscus translation (medial–lateral and anterior–posterior), and meniscus tibial contact stresses were extracted and analyzed. Results Increasing the suture stiffness resulted in increased force in the anterior horn sutures and the force in posterior horn sutures being mainly influenced by joint loading and not by suture stiffness. At 60° flexion, posterior horn tensile forces (50.11–52.35 N) were about 3.4–4.1 times greater than anterior horn tensile forces, which indicated the posterior horn as the major load-bearing structure. Increasing suture stiffness progressively decreased the medial–lateral and anterior–posterior displacements of the medial meniscus, and the 200 N/mm group of suture stiffnesses most closely approximated native meniscal kinematics. Medial tibial cartilage contact stress decreased with the increase of suture stiffness. It was found that 200 N/mm of suture stiffness most closely simulated the contact stress of the native knee for most loading conditions. The lateral compartment was not influenced by medial suture stiffness changes. Conclusion Suture stiffness is key to the overall biomechanical performance of artificial menisci. Stiffer fixation (200 N/mm) reduces the translation of the medial meniscal and tibial cartilage contact stress and restores the load distribution.

works.title: Immune microenvironmental regulation of odontogenic differentiation in dental pulp stem cells: mechanisms, signaling networks, and regenerative strategies
works.abstract: Dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) are a promising cell source for dentin regeneration, but their regenerative behavior is strongly shaped by the local immune microenvironment. This review integrates evidence on immune mediators, immune cell–DPSC interactions, intracellular signaling, and immunomodulatory biomaterials. Particular attention is given to how mediator concentration and exposure duration influence the balance between inflammatory injury and differentiation-associated responses. In one human DPSC model, 1 μg/mL lipopolysaccharide for 24 h increased IL-1β and TNF-α transcript levels 6.9-fold and 4.1-fold, respectively, illustrating the magnitude of the inflammatory response under defined experimental conditions. NF-κB, Wnt, Smad, MAPK, and related pathways link extracellular cues to cell survival, recruitment, and mineralization, although the direction of their effects varies with the stimulus and model. Biomaterials offer ways to influence these responses through factor delivery, ion release, or activation of endogenous signals. Culture mineralization, reparative dentin formation, and functional pulp–dentin regeneration represent different levels of evidence and should guide interpretation of these approaches. Integrating immunology, stem cell biology, and biomaterials science may therefore support more precise and clinically relevant strategies for dentin regeneration.

works.title: Aligned electrospun gelatin-carbon black nanofibers for cardiac tissue modelling
works.abstract: Replicating the complex myocardial microenvironment remains a fundamental challenge in cardiac tissue engineering. Although nanomaterials are increasingly incorporated into electrospun scaffolds to enhance biomaterials properties, it remains unclear whether improvements in cardiac function result primarily from increased conductivity or from broader modulations of the microenvironment. Here, we investigated how carbon black nanoparticles regulate the structural, physicochemical, mechanical, electrical, and biological properties of aligned electrospun gelatin scaffolds. Aligned gelatin scaffolds containing 0.1%–2% (w/v) carbon black were fabricated with fiber diameters of 0.15–0.20 μm. Directionality analysis confirmed preferential fiber orientation in all formulations. Carbon black addition preserved scaffold hydration at approximately 500%, improved hydrolytic stability, and produced hydrated elastic moduli similar to the microscale stiffness of native myocardium. The carbon black concentrations tested did not significantly enhance bulk scaffold conductivity, despite successful nanoparticle incorporation. Nevertheless, carbon black concentration was associated with differences in selected structural, molecular, and contractile readouts. All formulations supported H9c2 cardiomyoblast metabolic activity and alignment, while primary neonatal cardiomyocyte–fibroblast co-cultures developed organized sarcomeres, elongated myotubes, maintained cardiac-marker expression, and improved spontaneous contractions. This study, integrating multiscale materials characterization with functional biological evaluation, indicates that, under the tested conditions, the differences among formulations were associated with the combined scaffold microenvironment rather than with a demonstrated conductivity-dependent mechanism. These findings suggest that Gel-CB formulations, with their alignment and mechanical characteristics, preserve primary neonatal cardiac cells phenotype and functionality over early-stages cardiac models’ development.

works.title: Validation of a single-detector radiostereometric analysis setup for biomechanical research
works.abstract: Introduction Radiostereometric analysis (RSA) enables direct three-dimensional tracking of radiopaque markers placed in internal structures that are inaccessible to external optical measurement systems. The objective was to evaluate the agreement of a custom single-detector RSA system with a validated robotic reference and to compare its measurement performance with that of established optical and tactile measurement systems. It was hypothesized that RSA would show low trial-to-trial variability and measurement performance comparable to the comparator systems. Methods In this controlled laboratory study, programmed translational displacement of 5.00 mm in the anterior (AT), lateral (LT), and superior (ST) directions was performed in a synthetic knee model by a six-degree-of-freedom industrial robot. Ten displacement trials were performed in each direction. Evaluable trial counts were 10 for RSA and a stereo-optical measuring system (SOMS), 7–10 for a tactile measuring system (TMS), and 8–9 for an infrared measuring system (IRMS). Agreement between each system and the robotic reference was characterized by the mean bias with its 95% confidence interval, error standard deviation, 95% fixed-reference error limits, root mean square error (RMSE), and the proportion of errors within ±0.10 mm. Equivalence of the mean bias to zero within ±0.10 mm was assessed using two one-sided tests. Results RSA demonstrated biases of −0.083 mm for AT, −0.133 mm for LT, and −0.028 mm for ST. Error standard deviations ranged from 0.015 to 0.071 mm, and RMSE values ranged from 0.031 to 0.149 mm. Mean-bias equivalence was established for AT and ST, but not for LT. SOMS showed error standard deviations of 0.017–0.029 mm but systematically underestimated displacement in ST. TMS and IRMS showed direction-dependent variability, with error standard deviations of 0.093–0.125 mm and 0.112–0.367 mm, respectively. Discussion The presented RSA system measured static translations with low variability and measurement performance comparable to the established comparator systems. Mean-bias equivalence within ±0.10 mm was demonstrated for AT and ST, but not for LT. These findings support the use of the RSA system for static in vitro biomechanical experiments assessing macroscopic translations.

works.title: Material-aware preclinical digital twins for breast cancer: engineered matrices as causal and auditable interfaces
works.abstract: Imaging-calibrated breast cancer digital twins have retrospectively forecast treatment response in selected longitudinal imaging cohorts.
