Patient-derived (patient-sourced) organoids, tunable hydrogels, bioprinted tissues, and tumor-on-chip platforms now reproduce selected features of the tumor microenvironment. We propose integrating these components into a closed-loop architecture that has not been prospectively validated as a complete system in breast cancer. The missing interface is a material layer in which extracellular-matrix chemistry, mechanics, architecture, transport, remodeling, and spatial heterogeneity are measured and perturbed as model variables. The synchronized physical referent is a versioned ensemble of engineered tumor constructs. Patient -conditioned computational states are initialized or constrained by individual-patient observations, while construct measurements govern the experimental state. Uncertainty-aware algorithms select feasible perturbations to distinguish mechanisms or reduce predictive uncertainty; batch metrology and biological phenotypes update or falsify the computational counterpart. Biomaterials thereby serve as experimental actuators, measurement interfaces, and reproducible benchmark conditions. We specify twin identity and synchronization, a five-level validation ladder from material validity to health-system readiness, and a staged translational pathway. Biological incompleteness, coupled material properties, limited tissue, and uncertain transfer from constructs to patients constrain near-term use. The opportunity is a reproducible preclinical learning system with explicit validation gates before patient-level claims. Its predictions remain useful only when a physical experiment can refute them.

works.title: From K-snack to copolymer: conversion of silkworm pupa oil into poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyhexanoate) by engineered Cupriavidus necator H16
works.abstract: Abstract Silkworm pupae are continuously generated as a major byproduct of the silk industry and have long been consumed as inexpensive, high-energy snacks in Korea. However, consumer acceptance has become increasingly variable due to their distinctive appearance and odor. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) analysis revealed that silkworm pupa oil (SPO) consists of approximately 54% oleic acid, 29% linoleic acid, 17% palmitic acid, and minor amounts of cyclopropane fatty acids. Based on this composition, this study evaluated the feasibility of producing poly(3-hydroxybutyrate- co -3-hydroxyhexanoate) [P(3HB- co -3HHx)] using engineered Cupriavidus necator H16 with SPO as a sustainable substrate. Compared with other carbon sources, SPO supported comparable growth and polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) content, which was 2.64-fold higher than fructose and 1.42-fold higher than bean oil in flask cultures, demonstrating its potential as an efficient substrate. Supplementation with 1.0% fructose as an auxiliary carbon source further increased dry cell weight (DCW) and total PHA accumulation by up to 20%. To improve emulsification, various emulsifiers were screened, and Tween 20 enhanced DCW and PHA yield by 1.4-fold and 1.55-fold, respectively. The resulting film exhibited a tensile strength of 6.0 ± 0.6 MPa and an elongation at break of 53.4 ± 4.6%, and showed approximately 90% degradation after 7 days by Microbulbifer sp. SOL66. Overall, this study demonstrates that SPO is a promising and sustainable carbon source for PHA production, highlighting the valorization of silk industry byproducts into high-value biopolymeric materials.

works.title: Valorization of livestock biogas slurry through indigenous Oocystis sp. cultivation for nutrient recovery and production of plant-beneficial biomass
Perfluorooctane sulfonate impairs propionate-to-methane carbon transfer by disrupting syntrophic electron and thermodynamic coupling during sludge anaerobic digestion
Dual mechanism of pyrite-driven enhanced bio-oxidation of arsenopyrite
Diffusion integrity testing of small‐area sterilizing‐grade membrane filters in single‐use assemblies
works.abstract: Sterile filtration represents the final critical step in biomanufacturing, where a sterilizing-grade membrane filter removes microbial contamination from the drug product - making filter integrity verification essential. While bubble point and gas-liquid diffusion tests are established non-destructive methods for hydrophilic membranes, diffusion testing offers high sensitivity to small defects and operates at lower test pressures. However, applying diffusion testing to small-area filters integrated into closed single-use assemblies remains challenging because pressure changes measured by automated integrity testers can arise not only from membrane diffusion, but also from assembly-related effects such as gas-permeable tubing, upstream volume and thermal equilibration. For low-area devices, these background contributions can become comparable to or greater than the membrane signal, reducing test sensitivity and complicating interpretation. This work presents a practical method for implementing diffusion-based integrity testing of small-format sterilizing-grade filters in final sealed single-use assemblies. The approach quantifies assembly-specific background contribution and incorporates it into an adjusted diffusion specification, allowing membrane-specific diffusion to be resolved without altering the assembled system. By accounting for system-derived measurement noise, the method enables reliable end-user integrity assessment of closed assemblies that cannot be reconfigured to reduce upstream volume or replace high-permeability tubing materials.

works.title: Fluorine-Stabilized High-Valence Cobalt on Silicalite-1 Zeolite Synergizing with Adjacent Silanol Groups for Propane Dehydrogenation via Polarized C–H Bond Activation
works.abstract: Abstract Propane dehydrogenation (PDH) is vital to meet the rapid global demand for propylene. However, non-noble cobalt-based catalysts still suffer from inefficient C–H activation, necessitating precise microenvironment engineering. Herein, an NH4F-assisted in situ crystallization strategy for silicalite-1 (S-1) zeolite is developed to tailor both the framework structure and Co oxidation state. OH-FTIR spectra confirm that fluorine (F) incorporation heals silanol defects. At optimal F/Si = 0.23, F mediates interfacial interaction between high-valence Coδ+ sites and Si–O–F moieties. Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) mapping further reveals spatial colocalization of F and Co species. In the PDH reaction, electron-deficient Coδ+ species promote polarization and weakening of the inert C–H bonds of propane, initiating dehydrogenation; the activated H atoms are subsequently transferred to adjacent silanol groups (Si–OH), where they recombine on adjacent surface sites and desorb as H2. Consequently, the optimized Co2/S-1-23F (where “23F” refers to an F/Si molar ratio of 0.23 used in the synthesis gel) catalyst achieves 57.4% initial propane conversion and >97% propylene selectivity at 550 °C. Comprehensive characterizations indicate that F acts as a dual electronic and structural additive, and optimal PDH performance originates from balanced multifunctionality instead of maximum fluorine loading, offering a practical strategy for designing high-performance non-noble PDH catalysts.

works.title: Seed-Germination-Inspired Robust Protein-Based Bioadhesives Made by Regulating Dynamic Water
works.abstract: Abstract Soybean-meal adhesives offer a renewable alternative to fossil-derived formaldehyde resins for wood composites, but their bonding performance is highly sensitive to water availability during processing. Water promotes protein-chain mobility, wetting, and penetration into porous wood, whereas premature water loss during open assembly restricts molecular rearrangement, causes rapid thickening, and weakens interfacial development. Inspired by water regulation during seed germination, we constructed a temperature-sensitive poly(amidoamine)–glutaraldehyde network in a soybean-meal adhesive to regulate water loss and flow during processing. Before hot pressing, hydrogen bonding and network confinement reduced premature water loss; upon heating, weakened hydrogen-bonding interactions and network rearrangement reduced the confinement of associated water, thereby preserving adhesive flow and promoting interfacial penetration. After 2 h of open assembly, the modified adhesive retained 46% more water than the unmodified soybean-meal adhesive and 14% more than a PAE-modified soybean-meal adhesive. Subsequent hot pressing produced plywood with a wet shear strength of 0.71 MPa, 1320% and 78% higher than the respective controls. Under standard processing conditions, wet shear strength reached 1.39 MPa, representing increases of 184% and 34%. Comparative life-cycle assessment further indicated lower potential environmental impacts than conventional urea-formaldehyde and phenol-formaldehyde resins within the assessed system boundary.

works.title: Fabrication of a Scalable Anti-scaling Cathode and an Integrated Device for Extraction of Mg(OH)2 from Seawater
works.abstract: Abstract Cathode scaling is a critical bottleneck in direct seawater electrolysis. Although several anti-scaling cathodes have been reported, it is difficult for them to achieve large-scale application due to their small size, high cost, or short lifetime. Herein, a scalable anti-scaling cathode and an integrated device are proposed to demonstrate the practical potential of direct seawater electrolysis. In-situ observations reveal that its stable anti-scaling performance during at least 1000 h is attributed to the surface microstructure, where a thick hydrophobic layer more than 40 μm covers most of Sn microcones in the bottom layer, while only NiFeCo nanocones standing on the tips of Sn microcones are exposed. The essential feature of this hydrophobic hierarchical cone structure is highly dispersed electroactive areas in a stable hydrophobic surface. An integrated device on the basis of this anti-scaling cathode is assembled, and Mg(OH)2 nanoparticles with a purity up to 98.3% are successfully extracted from seawater with an energy consumption of 3.26 kW h kg–1 Mg(OH)2. The stable cell voltage during 1000 h of seawater electrolysis further supports its anti-scaling capability. The novel cathode and integrated device are expected to have application potential in fields such as hydrogen evolution from seawater, softening of reverse osmosis concentrate, and separation of magnesium/lithium from salt lake brine.

works.title: When Are Anaerobic Digestion and Black Soldier Fly Bioconversion Solutions Sustainable in Humanitarian Waste Management? A Life Cycle and Feasibility Assessment
works.abstract: Abstract Humanitarian operations generate significant quantities of biowaste, the biodegradable fraction of organic solid waste (OFMSW), in contexts where collection, segregation, and controlled end-of-life treatment are often limited. In such settings, biological waste valorisation technologies may contribute to reducing environmental impacts while supporting local resource recovery. However, their performance depends strongly on operational and socio-economic conditions. This study assesses anaerobic digestion (AD), black soldier fly (BSF) bioconversion, and composting as organic-waste treatment options for humanitarian settings through a context-sensitive life cycle and feasibility framework. The analysis builds on evidence generated in the EU-funded Bio4HUMAN project for the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and South Sudan (SSD) and on life cycle assessment (LCA) principles applied to the treatment of biowaste. AD, BSF, composting, and uncontrolled open dumping disposal are considered as alternative end-of-life routes. A feasibility layer is subsequently incorporated to account for key contextual factors, including waste segregation practices, contamination risk, infrastructure availability, technical capacity, output valorisation, market access, governance readiness, and health and biosafety constraints. The results indicate that neither AD nor BSF bioconversion can be considered universally preferable across humanitarian contexts. AD is most suitable where segregated organic waste, local biogas demand, operational capacity, and safe digestate valorisation are available. In contrast, BSF bioconversion showed potential for resource recovery, but its sustainability was highly sensitive to the existence of safe and locally validated outlets for larvae biomass and frass. When larvae-feed credits were reduced or removed, BSF performance declined, confirming that recovered-product credits should not be assumed in the absence of documented local valorization pathways. Under the current mixed-waste baseline and the balanced weighting case, the contextual sustainability score ranked composting as the most favourable option in both DRC and SSD, followed by modular renewable micro-AD, micro-AD, and BSF bioconversion, while open dumping was used as the current unmanaged benchmark. However, this ranking does not imply direct deployment readiness under mixed or contaminated waste conditions, since all biological routes require source-separation, contamination control, and safe output valorisation. The source-separated scenario reduced feasibility penalties for all biological options but did not automatically reverse the ranking because composting also benefits from improved waste-stream quality. Overall, the results support a context-sensitive framework combining LCA-derived environmental burdens, recovered-product credits, and feasibility penalties, rather than universal rankings, for selecting organic-waste technologies in humanitarian settings.

works.title: Graphene/Si Heterojunction Platform with a Multifunctional Atomic Bridging Layer for Photoelectrochemical CO2 Reduction
works.abstract: Abstract The facile integration and stability of Si-based photoelectrode architectures are the remaining challenges in the photoelectrochemical (PEC) conversion of CO2 to fuels. In this work, the single-atomic-layer graphene is used as a functional bridging layer to integrate both Si photocathodes and photoanodes, which enable the direct electrodeposition of metal-based electrocatalysts (Cu, Ag, and In–Sn alloys) and a semiconductor-based catalyst Ni–Fe layered double hydroxide (Ni–Fe LDH) on graphene/Si heterojunction electrodes for PEC CO2 reduction and O2 evolution reactions, respectively. We demonstrate a PEC device with a full-cell configuration consisting of an In–Sn/graphene/Si heterojunction photocathode and a Ni–Fe LDH/graphene/Si heterojunction photoanode, exhibiting a reduced photovoltage of ∼1080 mV compared to the electrochemical counterparts. A self-powered PEC CO2 reduction with a solar-to-fuel conversion efficiency of 3.2% can be obtained by integrating the graphene/Si heterojunction photocathode and photoanode with a Si photovoltaic. In addition, in situ PEC X-ray absorption spectroscopy analyses show that the electrodeposited catalysts on the graphene layer lead to the transport of photogenerated electrons and preserve durability throughout the reaction. Utilizing graphene as a chemically inert atomic bridging layer enables the seamless integration of Si photoelectrodes with various catalysts, providing a platform for the PEC CO2 reduction reaction.

works.title: Efficient Chemical Upcycling of Waste Poly(ethylene terephthalate) Bottles through Hydrolysis Catalyzed by Terephthalic Acid
works.abstract: Abstract Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) depolymerization supports the sustainable use of resources by recovering the monomer pertaining to the circular economy. The recycling rate of PET waste is quite low; consequently, there is a need to create accessible and low-carbon-footprint depolymerization technologies to rely on this plastic waste in value-added applications. This study uses terephthalic acid (TPA) as a catalyst to hydrolyze waste PET into its monomer, TPA. During hydrolysis, TPA facilitates the selective cleavage of PET’s ester bonds, allowing for efficient breakdown and recycling of PET flakes. Optimized reaction conditions for the TPA-assisted hydrolysis achieve up to 99.9% PET conversion, a maximum TPA yield of 95.3%, and over 98% purity, matching commercial TPA standards. This work primarily focuses on conversion and the role of workup in improving product recovery and purity. The end quality of the TPA obtained was further confirmed by HPLC, and 1H NMR and 13C NMR for purity assessment found high-purity TPA. Additionally, this study emphasizes the importance of workup in enhancing both the recovery and purity of the final product.

works.title: Amphiphilic Isocyanate-Free Polyurethanes Synthesized via Transurethane Polycondensation: Self-Assembly and Rheological Behavior in Aqueous Solutions
works.abstract: Abstract This study reports a more sustainable and cost-effective preparation of isocyanate-free hydrophobically modified ethoxylated poly(ether-urethane)s (TU-IFHEURs) with internal and terminal hydrophobes via a melt transurethane polycondensation of PEG (M–n = 400–20,000 g mol–1) with a fatty diamine-based bis(2-hydroxyethyl carbamate). This method reduced the need for expensive PEG bis(glycidyl ether)s and toxic (di)amines, as well as reaction steps and time. Calculated green chemistry indicators showed reduced Efactor and energy consumption compared to previously reported poly(hydroxy-urethane) analogues. Obtained TU-IFHEURs exhibited M–n ranging from 2,200 to 35,800 g mol–1 and varying molar ratios of hydrophobic-to-hydrophilic moieties, as elucidated by SEC and NMR. For the first time, their hierarchical self-assembly behavior in aqueous solution was visualized by cryo-TEM. Depending on the PEG chain length, hydrophobe content, and solution concentration, spherical core-corona-like, worm-like, and vesicle-like assemblies were observed. DLS, cryo-TEM, and rheological results confirmed that the associative behavior of TU-IFHEUR aqueous solutions was concentration- and structure- dependent. The solutions demonstrated a particularly good match for rheology modifiers, providing structural integrity at rest, high shear-viscosity at low shear rates, and shear-thinning behavior at higher shear rates, desirable for coatings, paints, and other waterborne formulations.

works.title: Enhancement of Anaerobic Digestion of Agricultural Waste via Iron Cycling Driven by a Hematite-Calcium Peroxide Coupling System
works.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic digestion is an effective biotechnology for converting lignocellulose-rich agricultural waste into renewable energy, but the recalcitrant lignocellulosic structure limits substrate degradation and methane production. To overcome this limitation, a hematite-CaO2 coupling system was constructed to explore potential Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling and its role in promoting lignocellulose conversion into methane. The results demonstrated that Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling was established in the hematite-CaO2 system through microbial Fe(III) reduction and CaO2-induced Fe(II) oxidation, which promoted •OH generation and consequently facilitated lignocellulose degradation. FTIR analysis confirmed the cleavage of lignin–carbohydrate linkages. Consequently, cumulative methane production increased by 17.4% in the Fe-CaO2 group compared with the control group. In addition, the hematite–CaO2 coupling system reduced the demand for exogenous Fe(III) sources and promoted the transformation of iron oxides toward more crystalline minerals. Consistently, microbial electron transfer capacity increased by 15.8%. Furthermore, microbial community analysis revealed that lignocellulose-degrading microorganisms were enriched in the control group, likely due to the limited degradation efficiency at the end of the experiment. Moreover, metagenomic analysis revealed that the relative abundance of genes involved in the sequential conversion from lignocellulose degradation to methane production increased. Overall, this study provides new insights into Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling-mediated lignocellulose degradation and highlights a promising strategy for enhancing renewable energy recovery from agricultural waste.

works.title: High-Level De Novo Biosynthesis of Apigenin Via Systematic Metabolic Engineering in Yarrowia lipolytica
works.abstract: Abstract Apigenin, a bioactive flavonoid with promising nutraceutical and industrial applications, faces challenges in production due to the unsustainability of plant extraction methods. In this study, we engineered Yarrowia lipolytica as a cell factory for de novo apigenin biosynthesis via systematic metabolic engineering. Initially, the most efficient type II flavone synthase from Erigeron breviscapus (EbFNSII) was identified using whole-cell biocatalysis. Subsequently, the apigenin biosynthetic pathway was constructed in Y. lipolytica Po1f (Δku70). Then, using an exogenous precursor feeding strategy, naringenin was identified as a crucial node in carbon metabolic flux. Additionally, we optimized the shikimic acid pathway by inhibiting competing pathways and overexpressing essential genes, thereby increasing the availability of L-tyrosine. Next, increasing the supply of malonyl-CoA further boosted carbon metabolic flux, which enhanced apigenin production by 2.41-fold, reaching 58.26 mg/L in shake flasks. Finally, an apigenin titer of 1236.25 mg/L was achieved by the engineered strain YLAPI-8 in a 2.4-L bioreactor under fed-batch fermentation, representing the highest titer reported to date. This study establishes an efficient platform for apigenin production and offers guidance for achieving high titers of flavonoids in Y. lipolytica.

works.title: Cu-Anchored Keggin Ti–Oxo Cluster/Boron-Doped Carbon Nitride Heterojunction for CO2 Photoreduction
works.abstract: Abstract Efficient and selective photocatalytic CO2 conversion in pure water requires both effective utilization of photogenerated charge carriers and well-defined catalytic active sites. Here, a Cu-functionalized Keggin-type titanium–oxo polyoxometalate/boron-doped carbon nitride photocatalyst (Cu–PT/BCN) was developed to integrate interfacial charge regulation with surface catalysis. Phosphate-centered PT clusters were grown in situ on two-dimensional BCN, followed by solvent-assisted ultrasonication to improve interfacial contact and cluster dispersion. The terminal {PO4} groups of the PT clusters were further used to selectively anchor atomically dispersed Cu species. Under UV–vis irradiation in pure water, the optimized Cu–PT/BCN exhibited markedly enhanced CO2 photoreduction activity, with CO2 conversion rates 7 and 30 times higher than those of BCN and pristine CN, respectively, while maintaining nearly 100% selectivity toward CO. Mechanistic studies revealed that charge transfer between BCN and PT follows a Z-scheme pathway, resulting in substantially improved separation of photogenerated charge carriers. The electrons retained on PT are subsequently transferred to Cu sites, which promote CO2 adsorption and activation and facilitate its selective reduction to CO. In situ microsecond transient absorption spectroscopy revealed an electron transfer efficiency of 80.5% under reaction conditions, while CO2 adsorption measurements and in situ Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy further confirmed enhanced CO2 adsorption and stabilization of the key COOH* intermediate. This work highlights metal-oxo clusters as versatile components for integrating charge regulation with catalytic-site engineering in photocatalytic CO2 reduction in pure water.

works.title: Identification of a Novel D-alanine–D-alanine Ligase from Nocardioides kribbensis for Efficient In Vivo Biosynthesis of Shinorine in Engineered Escherichia coli
works.abstract: Abstract Shinorine, a UV-absorbing mycosporine-like amino acid (MAA), is biosynthesized from sedoheptulose 7-phosphate via a conserved gene cluster (mysA, mysB, mysC, and mysD). The final step, catalyzed by MysD, a homolog of D-alanine–D-alanine ligase (DDL), converts mycosporine-glycine to shinorine. In this study, a novel MysD from Nocardioides kribbensis was expressed, purified, and biochemically characterized. The enzyme showed optimal activity at pH 8.0 and 40 °C, with obvious enhancement by Mg2+ and K+. Kinetic analysis revealed Michaelis constants (Km) of 78.7 μM for ATP, 84 μM for the first D-alanine, and 785 μM for the second D-alanine, with a catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km) of 433 M–1 s–1. Chromosomal integration of this gene into a mycosporine-glycine-producing engineered strain enabled efficient shinorine biosynthesis. Through strain engineering combined with fed-batch fermentation, shinorine titers reached 243.36 mg/L in shake-flask culture and 1.96 g/L in fed-batch fermentation, demonstrating the potential for scalable microbial production of this natural sunscreen compound.

works.title: Energy-Efficient and Low-Carbon Recovery of Organic Compounds via Electrified Deep Eutectic Solvent-Based Extractive Distillation
works.abstract: Abstract Methyl ethyl ketone (MEK) and ethanol (EtOH) form an azeotrope at atmospheric pressure, making their effective separation and recovery by conventional distillation difficult. In this study, two imidazole-based deep eutectic solvents (DESs) were selected as entrainers for extractive distillation of the MEK-EtOH azeotrope. Their separation performance was evaluated by ternary vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE) experiments, and the data were correlated using the non-random two-liquid (NRTL) model. Quantum chemical calculations revealed that strong hydrogen-bonding interactions between the DESs and azeotropic components are essential for efficient separation. Extractive distillation processes using dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and the best-performing DES as entrainers were designed and optimized via multi-objective optimization coupled with multi-criteria decision-making. Life cycle assessment was performed using Eco-indicator 99 (EI-99). Compared with the DMSO-based process, the DES-based process achieved lower total annual cost (TAC), CO2 emissions (ECO2), and EI-99 score, but exhibited a relatively lower thermodynamic efficiency. Compared with the non-electrified DES-based process, the flash vapor compression heat pump (FVCHP)-electrified DES-based process reduced TAC, ECO2, and EI-99 by 5.81%, 43.64%, and 50.71%, respectively. This study offers a low-carbon and economical strategy for azeotrope separation.

works.title: Converting Waste Tires into Blue Ammonia: Safe and Sustainable Process Design, Multiobjective Optimization and Comprehensive Assessment
works.abstract: Abstract Ammonia synthesis based on steam methane reforming (SMR) is characterized by intensive energy consumption and high carbon emissions. To address these limitations, novel processes integrating gasification and carbon capture technologies were proposed for converting waste tires into blue ammonia. Detailed safety, techno-economic, and life cycle assessments were conducted to evaluate comprehensive performance. Machine learning-driven multiobjective operation optimization was carried out for reducing levelized cost of ammonia (LCOA) while enhancing safety and sustainability scores based on safe-and-sustainable-by-design framework. Our results highlight the critical role of artificial neural networks in achieving efficient optimization. Additionally, the quantitative impacts of integrating various renewable energy sources were investigated. The results showed the conventional gasification (CG) integrating methyldiethanolamine (MDEA)-based carbon capture alternative achieved the optimal LCOA at 358.1 $/ton in current electricity scenario. A peak environmental sustainability score of 0.443 was achieved, outperforming traditional SMR integrating MDEA-based carbon capture pathway by 13.04%. The safest process is CG integrating monoethanolamine-based carbon capture. Under the renewable scenario, the LCA results highlighted the critical role of renewable energy integration in enhancing the environmental sustainability of waste tires-to-ammonia processes, especially achieving a 0.344 increase in environmental sustainability score with onshore wind electricity at a lower LCOA of 406.0 $/ton in plasma gasification integrating MDEA-based alternative.

works.title: Stability-Guided Selection of Terpene-Based Hydrophobic Deep Eutectic Solvents for Sustainable Liquid-Phase Processes
works.abstract: Abstract Terpene-based hydrophobic deep eutectic solvents (HDESs) are promising alternatives to conventional hydrophobic organic solvents, but their practical applicability depends on stability under processing conditions. Here, sixteen binary terpene-based HDESs composed of menthol, thymol, limonene, linalool, carvone, camphor, and borneol were systematically evaluated using a stability-guided selection approach. Density, viscosity, temperature-dependent flow behavior, volatility-related mass loss, water uptake, and compositional stability after water contact, heating, ultrasound treatment, and UV irradiation were investigated. All systems had densities below 1.0 g cm–3, while viscosity at 25 °C ranged from 1.351 mPa·s for LIM-CARV to 35.506 mPa·s for MENT-THYM. Volatility-related mass loss at 100 °C varied from 3.5 to 39.0%. After contact with a 100-fold excess of water, the water content of the recovered HDES phase ranged from 961 to 30,781 ppm, demonstrating pronounced composition-dependent hydration. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) profiling showed that most systems preserved more than 95% of their original components after the applied treatments. THYM-CARV showed the most favorable overall stability profile, with only 3.5% mass loss and ≥99.9% preservation of the original components after thermal, ultrasonic, UV, and water-contact treatments. These results demonstrate that terpene-based HDESs should be selected using integrated structure–property–stability criteria rather than hydrophobicity or component origin alone.

works.title: Thermally Treated Oyster Shell Exacerbates Phosphorus Immobilization during Acidic Soil Amendment
works.abstract: Abstract Soil acidification constrains crop productivity, and oyster shell (OS) waste is increasingly used as a sustainable liming material. Phosphorus (P), one of the three essential macronutrients for crops, can react with calcium (Ca)-containing materials during liming and thereby affect its bioavailability. However, cooking-related thermal treatments alter the physicochemical properties of OS, and whether this alteration affects phosphorus bioavailability during liming remains unclear. We hypothesized that thermal loss of the OS organic matrix strengthens calcium (Ca2+)-phosphate (HnPO4(3–n)–) interactions, promotes calcium phosphate (CaP) nucleation, reshapes soil microbial P-cycling responses, and thereby reduces plant-available phosphorus despite effective acidity neutralization. To test this, we compared raw (ROS), steamed (SOS), and grilled (GOS) OSs via organic matrix characterization, binding energy analyses for interfacial mechanisms, and pot experiments with maize in acidic soil for phosphorus bioavailability. Thermal treatment progressively degraded the organic matrix, particularly carboxyl-rich proteins, and subsequently enhanced phosphate binding on CaCO3. These stronger interactions accelerated heterogeneous CaP nucleation and promoted the formation of apatite-like CaP phases on thermally treated surfaces. In pot experiments, ROS increased maize shoot biomass and phosphorus uptake relative to SOS and GOS, and maintained higher soil-available phosphorus with lower Ca-bound phosphorus fractions, despite all treatments raising soil pH to a similar extent. At the microbial level, thermally treated OS was associated with a predicted phosphorus-starvation response and reduced soil phosphatase activities, whereas ROS sustained a more active microbial phosphorus-mineralizing community. Together, the abiotic interfacial reactions and the coupled microbial responses acted in concert to reduce phosphorus bioavailability under thermally treated OS, while ROS preserved both the organic-rich surface and microbial phosphorus turnover. Collectively, these results show that thermal treatment of OS enhances phosphate binding and CaP immobilization, reducing phosphorus bioavailability despite comparable acidity neutralization, and identify raw oyster shell as the preferred amendment for preserving phosphorus availability in acidic soils.

works.title: Dynamically Co-assembling Guaiacol Glyceryl Ether and Cellulose Nanocrystals for Iridescent Films Construction: The Visualized and Sensitive Monitoring for Food Spoilage
works.abstract: Abstract With the increasing demand for food safety and quality monitoring, sustainable and intelligent packaging that enables real-time, visual, and non-destructive indication of food freshness has become a key research direction. However, most existing indicators rely on synthetic dyes, which raise safety concerns and environmental issues. In this work, cholesteric cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) served as chiral building blocks to construct the liquid–crystalline skeleton, and chitosan (Cs), xylose (Xyl), and guaiacol-glyceryl ether (GGE) were introduced to construct a multi-component composite iridescent film via evaporation-induced self-assembly. Chitosan and xylose modulate the internal hydrogen-bonding network, while GGE acts as a co-assembly regulator to endow the film with stimulus-responsive optical evolution. The microstructure, mechanical properties, thermal stability, and pH-responsive behavior were systematically investigated. The optimal formulation achieved a tensile strength of up to ∼5.7 MPa and a toughness of ∼44 MJ/m3, which were 4.5 MPa and 42 MJ/m3 higher than those of pure CNC films. Meanwhile, its peak thermal decomposition temperature increased by around 40 °C relative to pure CNC films. The CXCG-4 film exhibited distinct, reversible pH-responsive iridescent color changes from orange to deep red (ΔE ≈ 23.3), enabling real-time visual monitoring of grape freshness. In an 8-day grape storage test at 25 °C, the CXCG-4 group retained the highest soluble solids content (12.8%) and ascorbic acid content (3.0 mg/100 g), with the lowest weight loss (24.6%), confirming its superior comprehensive performance. Unlike traditional CNC-based films, this work achieved responsive color variation relying on multi-component co-assembly rather than extrinsic dyes. The present dye-free, green, and degradable structural color film may provide a promising strategy for intelligent food packaging applications.

works.title: Carbon Nitride-Modified Zr/SBA-15: A Highly Efficient Catalyst for Reductive Etherification of Furfural to Isopropyl Furfuryl Ether
works.abstract: Abstract The direct conversion of biomass-derived furfural (FUR) into isopropyl furfuryl ether (IPFE) via one-pot reductive etherification is a sustainable and economical route. However, this process remains challenging due to the need for bifunctional catalysts with balanced Lewis and Brønsted acid sites. In this work, a series of carbon nitride (CN)-modified Zr/SBA-15 catalysts (ZrxCNy/SBA-15) were synthesized by a simple impregnation method and evaluated for the reductive etherification of FUR using isopropanol as both the solvent and the hydrogen donor. The introduction of CN significantly enhanced the catalytic performance by increasing the dispersion of Zr species, enriching Lewis acid sites (LAS), and introducing Lewis base sites (LBS) from nitrogen functionalities. The optimized Zr4.4CN3.6/SBA-15 catalyst achieved a remarkable IPFE yield of 91.6% under mild conditions, substantially outperforming the CN-free counterpart (14.9% IPFE yield). By optimizing the reaction conditions, a 94.2% FUR conversion and a 92.7% selectivity to IPFE were achieved at 150 °C within only 20 min, corresponding to a productivity of 52.5 mmol·g–1·h–1, which was significantly superior to the results reported in the literature. XPS and Py-FTIR characterization revealed that the synergistic acid–base bifunctional mechanism, together with enhanced Lewis acidity via electronic interaction between CN and Zr, is responsible for the high activity and selectivity. Poisoning experiments confirmed that LBS, LAS, and BAS are all essential for the cascade conversion of FUR to IPFE, and a plausible reaction mechanism was accordingly proposed. The catalyst also exhibited excellent reusability and structural stability over five consecutive cycles.

works.title: Systematic regulation of mycelial extracellular proteolysis, endoplasmic reticulum homeostasis, morphology, and bioprocess boosts recombinant laccase production in Coprinopsis cinerea
works.abstract: Laccase is an important green catalyst, particularly basidiomycete laccases, which have significant industrial applications in fields, such as food and biomass energy. However, the natural secretion of laccase by basidiomycetes is low. Heterologous expression of basidiomycete laccase in yeast or Aspergillus often changes the enzyme's properties due to inappropriate post-translational modifications. Therefore, using basidiomycetes for homologous recombination expression of basidiomycete laccase has great industrial prospects and economic benefits. This study used the native host for the homologous recombination expression of Laccase Lcc5 from Coprinopsis cinerea and developed a novel strategy to increase its extracellular activity. Silencing the protease Ccmpr , overexpressing the endoplasmic reticulum stress response gene Anhac 1, and silencing the morphological regulation gene rac 1 all increased the recombinant Lcc5 activity. The extracellular laccase activity of the rac 1-silenced Cc lcc5 -anti rac 1-2 was 1.84-fold higher than that of the original Cc lcc5 -13. In particular, the Cc lcc5 -anti ChiE 2& mpr -3, obtained by simultaneously silencing the chitinase ChiE2 and the protease Ccmpr , exhibited the highest extracellular laccase activity, 67.71 U/mL, which was 2.56-fold higher than that of Cc lcc5 -13. Optimizing the fermentation process of Cc lcc5 -anti ChiE 2& mpr -3 increased laccase activity in shake flasks to 76.03 U/mL when using 20 g/L yeast extract as the nitrogen source. At a stirring speed of 200 rpm, the laccase activity in a 1.5-L fermenter reached 109.95 U/mL. To our knowledge, this is the highest extracellular laccase Lcc5 activity in basidiomycetes reported to date. This is the first report of a multidimensional integrated strategy to enhance recombinant protein expression in C. cinerea by modulating protease gene expression, optimizing post-translational folding and secretion, and modifying mycelial morphology. This study will pave the way for laccase industrial production and accelerate the development of the C. cinerea high-expression system.

works.title: Fucoidan and xyloglucan hydrolysis predicted by protein domain architecture in GH29 α-l-fucosidases
works.abstract: Abstract Family GH29 α- l -fucosidases hydrolyze fucosylated glycoconjugates via a retaining mechanism and are therefore considered useful for the synthesis of medically relevant molecules such as α-fucosylated human milk oligosaccharides by transfucosylation using naturally abundant α- l -fucosyl donors. Fucoidan and fucosylated xyloglucan are naturally abundant polysaccharides that can serve as α- l -fucosyl donors. However, few GH29 α- l -fucosidases have been reported to hydrolyze these polysaccharides or use them in transfucosylation, although large-scale efforts have been made to characterize members of this family. Here, we describe a domain-context-based analysis that we employed to predict GH29 α- l -fucosidases likely to hydrolyze fucoidan and fucosylated xyloglucan. We predicted fucoidan- and fucosylated xyloglucan-hydrolyzing α- l -fucosidases based on the presence of co-occurring sulfatase domains, and relevant carbohydrate-binding modules and glycoside hydrolase domains, and fine-tuned our predictions using ecological niche information and Conserved Unique Peptide Patterns grouping. We recombinantly expressed and biochemically characterized seven of these predicted GH29 members from Rhodopirellula sp. SWK7 ( Rs Fuc), Rhodopirellula pilleata ( Rp Fuc), Novipirellula artificiosorum ( Na Fuc), Clostridium methylpentosum ( Cm Fuc), Rhodopirellula maiorica ( Rm Fuc), Bacteroides sp. ( Bs Fuc), and Bacterium HR17/ Candidatus Fervidibacter japonicus (HR17Fuc), and demonstrated that they catalyze the hydrolysis of fucoidan and fucosylated xyloglucan. While these α- l -fucosidases did not score positive in a cursory transfucosylation screen, these and other GH29 members predicted to hydrolyze fucoidan or fucosylated xyloglucan may be further explored for their transfucosylation potential in future studies. The domain-context-based prediction of substrate preference described here can be extended for other substrates and to other carbohydrate-active enzyme families. Key points • GH29 alpha-L-fucosidases with fucoidan or xyloglucan-specific domains were predicted • RsFuc, RpFuc, NaFuc, CmFuc, RmFuc, BsFuc, and HR17Fuc were recombinantly expressed • Fucoidan and fucosylated xyloglucan were hydrolyzed by these alpha-L-fucosidases

works.title: Finite element simulations drive the design of in vitro models of down-scaled crosstalk in oxygen metabolism
works.abstract: Introduction Engineering biological communities enables the investigation of behavioural patterns driven by inter- individual crosstalk across scales. Nevertheless, biomedicine could take advantage of this modelling framework to buffer phenotypic readouts from potential coexistence-related biases. Methods To explore this concept, here we used finite element models to probe oxygen consumption in multi-spheroid systems and understand whether they can constitute reliable models of coexistence in vitro (or in vitro ecosystems), by quantifying how individual metabolism is influenced by the number, size and spatial distribution of cell constructs as determinants of supplied oxygen levels. Then, we adapted one of the simulated configurations experimentally to provide a first proof of prediction consistency resorting to a rigorous method for metabolic characterization in vitro that we previously established. Results Computational and experimental outcomes display similar trends. Albeit a systematic validation of numerical predictions is still to be performed, such results coherently indicate a modulation of oxygen consumption driven by the local availability. Discussion These models may set the foundations to better understand cell-cell or organoid-organoid crosstalk and how it affects in vitro assays typically evaluated in coexisting cellular samples – such as pre-clinical testing for drug development – as well as be even extended to ecological sciences to assess the impact of resource sharing in the presence of heterogeneities and environmental disturbances.

works.title: Editorial: Biotechnological breakthroughs in viral pathogen detection and diagnostics
works.abstract: detection. Although individual studies demonstrate different combinations of analytical performance, workflow simplicity, multiplexing, and portability, these features should not be interpreted as having been achieved uniformly across all platforms.. One important direction is the development of diagnostic approaches that reduce dependence on conventional reagents and complex analytical workflows. In this context, Taken together, the contributions to this Research Topic illustrate complementary directions in pathogen detection rather than a single technological solution. The studies report distinct advances in spectroscopy and chemometrics, lateral-flow systems, electrochemiluminescence, isothermal amplification, and CRISPR-based molecular recognition. Their demonstrated capabilities vary, and not every platform combines rapid operation, portability, multiplexing, and reduced reagent requirements. Rather, these characteristics represent complementary design objectives whose integration remains an important direction for future development. Progress in biosensors, nanotechnology, computational and AI-assisted analysis, and decentralized testing may help bring these capabilities together, provided that their practical benefits are established through appropriate analytical and clinical validation.Nonetheless, it is important to highlight that the next generation of diagnostics cannot be defined by analytical sensitivity or specificity alone. A technically superior assay may have limited impact if it remains dependent on complex sample preparation, specialized instrumentation, trained personnel, centralized laboratories, or workflows that are incompatible with real-world clinical and field settings. Translation therefore requires a broader perspective in which analytical performance is considered alongside robustness, simplicity, affordability, portability, scalability, clinical validation, and the ability to generate information that can directly support decision-making.The studies gathered in this Research Topic reflect a transition from detecting pathogens to delivering actionable diagnostic information. Future progress will depend increasingly on integrating molecular recognition with miniaturized biosensors, multiplexed detection, intelligent data analysis, connectivity, and decentralized testing, while maintaining rigorous validation in clinically representative and diverse real-world settings. Such integration will be particularly important for emerging and zoonotic pathogens, where rapid detection, surveillance, and timely intervention are intrinsically interconnected.Ultimately, the future of pathogen diagnostics will not be determined by a single technology, but by the successful convergence of complementary innovations into diagnostic solutions that are fast enough to act, simple enough to deploy, robust enough to trust, and informative enough to guide decisions. The contributions to this Research Topic provide important examples of this trajectory and collectively demonstrate how biotechnology is helping to reshape the next generation of infectious-disease detection and diagnostics.

works.title: Metal–organic frameworks integrating Chinese medicinal bioactives for wound repair and burn applications
works.abstract: Burn dressings must support tissue preservation, infection control, and epithelial repair while accommodating changes in exudate and wound depth. Defined bioactive compounds associated with Chinese medicinal plants offer pharmacological starting points, but their performance depends on chemical stability, local exposure, and delivery within the dressing. Metal–organic frameworks provide several ways to address these requirements through guest loading, coordination assembly, and integration with hydrogels or fibrous matrices. This narrative review examines how those material choices influence wound repair, with particular attention to the evidence supporting burn applications. We distinguish direct thermal-injury studies from excisional, diabetic, infected, and tumor-associated wound models and separate carrier-mediated delivery from systems in which a bioactive compound forms part of the framework or is delivered by another component of the dressing. Curcumin-containing formulations provide direct preclinical burn examples, whereas berberine, baicalein, quercetin, shikonin, and resveratrol systems contribute complementary evidence on antimicrobial activity, redox regulation, and local delivery. These studies identify opportunities to coordinate drug exposure with material degradation; they do not establish interchangeable indications across wound types. The review develops a comparison framework linking particle size, surface chemistry, stability, and release to clinically relevant outcomes. Added value should be assessed against dose-matched free compounds, unloaded materials, and established carriers using epithelial repair, tissue tolerance, infection burden, and dressing performance alongside wound closure. Priorities for burn translation are exposure measurements in relevant wound environments, preservation of viable tissue, reproducible manufacture, and follow-up of scar function. Matching the location and timing of each material function to a defined burn-care task offers a practical route for selecting formulations for further development.

works.title: Targeted TPGS ultrasound-responsive nanodroplets modulate P-gp and mitochondria to enhance doxorubicin sensitivity in multidrug-resistant breast cancer
works.abstract: Although drugs targeting mitochondria or P-gp combined with traditional chemotherapy drugs represent a novel and effective treatment for multiple drug resistance (MDR). Nevertheless, the efficacy is still restricted by several obstacles, including significant toxicity. Nanoscale drug delivery systems (DDSs) offer a favourable solution to reduce the toxicity and side effects of systemic administration. Meanwhile, DDSs provide a promising strategy to implement spatially and temporally controlled drug release when combined with ultrasound-targeted microbubble destruction (UTMD). Therefore, novel ultrasonic nanodroplets (NDs) which consist of a shell of D-alpha-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol 1,000 succinate (TPGS) and a core of ultrasound-responsive perfluorohexane, loaded with doxorubicin (DOX) were synthesized in this study to overcome these drawbacks. The encouraging results both in vitro and in vivo indicated that these original NDs exhibit excellent biocompatibility, targeting ability and therapeutic effects. TPGS not only acted as the shell material of NDs, but also had anti-cancer ability in itself. Furthermore, TPGS inhibited the activity of P-gp and thus simultaneously enhanced the sensitivity of DOX they carried. This work was the first to synthesize and report DOX-TPGS-NDs integrating synergistic strategies into a single nanodrug carrier. Our findings may provide scientific evidence to support the potential applications for reversing MDR.

works.title: Next‐Generation Electrochemical Analytical Systems: A Critical Review of Biosensing Technologies, Miniaturized Platforms, and Future Intelligent Diagnostics
works.abstract: Electrochemical analytical systems have evolved from conventional sensing devices into advanced platforms capable of real-time monitoring, multiplexed analysis, and decentralized diagnostics. Progress in biosensing technologies, nanomaterials, microfluidics, wearable devices, and artificial intelligence has significantly improved analytical performance and expanded potential applications in healthcare, environmental monitoring, and food safety. This review critically evaluates recent advances in next-generation electrochemical analytical systems, focusing on biosensing technologies, nanomaterial-enabled platforms, miniaturized devices, precision diagnostics, and emerging intelligent analytical systems, and identifies the major barriers to their practical implementation. Advanced electrochemical biosensors, including enzymatic, immunosensors, aptasensors, nucleic acid sensors, and molecularly imprinted polymer-based platforms, have demonstrated remarkable sensitivity and selectivity. Nanomaterials such as graphene, carbon nanotubes (CNTs), MXenes, and metal nanoparticles have further enhanced signal amplification and electron-transfer efficiency. In parallel, miniaturized technologies, including screen-printed electrodes (SPE), paper-based devices, microfluidic systems, and wearable sensors, have accelerated point-of-care diagnostics. However, persistent challenges related to matrix effects, biofouling, reproducibility, standardization, long-term stability, clinical validation, and manufacturing scalability continue to hinder widespread translation. The future of electrochemical analytical systems lies in developing robust, standardized, and clinically validated intelligent diagnostic ecosystems that integrate advanced sensing technologies with artificial intelligence, digital connectivity, and automated data analysis. Achieving successful clinical translation will require greater emphasis on reproducibility, regulatory compliance, multicenter validation, and real-world applicability, rather than solely on achieving ever-lower detection limits.

works.title: Biostimulation Sustains a Carbonic Anhydrase‐Producing Bacterial Consortium for CO 2 Hydration and Residual Oil Utilization Under Simulated Reservoir Conditions
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Depleted oil reservoirs are potential targets for geological CO 2 storage; however, temperature, salinity, pressure, and nutrient scarcity can suppress microbial activity. In this study, a consortium comprising the carbonic‐anhydrase‐producing bacterium Bacillus licheniformis S5 and the petroleum‐degrading bacterium Bacillus cereus S0 was evaluated in a stirred high‐pressure liquid system containing simulated brine and residual crude oil. Nitrogen and phosphorus biostimulation promoted culturable growth. At 50°C and 10 MPa, the S5 + S0 consortium maintained higher colony‐forming unit (CFU) counts and more persistent apparent carbonic‐anhydrase‐associated esterase activity than either monoculture. S0‐mediated crude‐oil degradation produced fatty‐acid intermediates and surface‐active metabolites, reducing surface tension to 62.14 mN/m and increasing aqueous CO 2 mass transfer. Meanwhile, S5‐associated carbonic anhydrase activity promoted CO 2 hydration, and the consortium maintained HCO 3 − concentrations above 900 mg/L. Collectively, these findings support a bench‐scale mechanistic framework in which residual‐oil utilization, interfacial modification, and enzymatically mediated CO 2 hydration are functionally coupled under simulated reservoir‐fluid conditions. This framework provides a foundation for subsequent evaluation in oil‐bearing rock microcosms and core‐flood systems.

works.title: PHA Production and Wastewater Treatment With Phototrophic Purple Bacteria: Effect of Transitioning OLR and HRT on Biopolymer Composition and Process Yield
works.abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the effect of transitioning organic loading rates (OLR) and hydraulic retention times (HRT) on polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) production from wastewater using PHA‐accumulating phototrophic purple bacteria. These bacteria were cultivated under light‐feast anaerobic conditions in a photo‐assisted continuous stirred tank reactor (P‐CSTR) fed with acidogenic fermented cattle manure and sugarcane molasses. Transitioning OLRs of 0.7, 1.6, and 2.0 g COD/L.d were tested, followed by HRTs of 48, 72, and 112 h at the optimal OLR. The desired conditions to boost PHA production were an OLR of 0.7–1.2 g COD/L.d and HRT of 112 h, attaining a maximum PHA accumulation of 86.3% g PHA/g VSS, and production yield of 94.5% g COD PHA /g COD removed . The system also indicated efficient pollutant elimination of 96.6% NH 4 ‐N, and 82.5% COD. Shorter HRTs (48 h) were less effective in COD removal but promoted higher poly‐3‐hydroxyvalerate production in the copolymer content (48.8% of PHA). In contrast, poly‐3‐hydroxybutyrate content increased at high OLRs. The results highlight that transitioning OLR and varying HRT significantly influenced the process performance, PHA accumulation yield, and biopolymer quality. Thus, OLR and HRT are the critical control parameters for optimizing PHA production, tailoring polymer properties, and ensuring enhanced wastewater treatment.

works.title: Catalytic activity of Ni and La impregnated MCM ‐41 for the synthesis of biofuel additives through the acetalization of glycerol with furfural
works.abstract: Abstract Background Furfural is one of the valuable chemicals that can be generated from acid hydrolysis of cellulosic biomass waste. Synthesizing cyclic acetals via the reaction of glycerol with furfural is a sustainable approach for converting a biodiesel side‐product and nontoxic glycerol into fuel additives. Within this scope, this study aimed to react glycerol and furfural on Ni‐La/MCM‐41 catalyst series to obtain 1,3‐dioxane and 1,3‐dioxolan. Before the catalytic test, the catalysts were characterized using Fourier Transform Infrared (FT‐IR), X‐ray powder diffraction (XRD), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), and N 2 adsorption–desorption analysis. The reaction was performed in a batch‐stirred glass reactor for parametric studies to observe the influence of catalyst type (La/MCM‐41, Ni/MCM‐41, Ni‐La/MCM‐41), temperature (85 and 95 °C), glycerol/furfural molar ratio (1:4 and 1:5), and time (15 and 45 min). Results The optimum reaction conditions were determined as 1:5 glycerol: furfural molar ratio, 85°C, and 30 min duration with 20% Ni‐loaded MCM‐41 catalyst to obtain 38% glycerol conversion. In these conditions, the dioxolane and dioxane product selectivities were observed as 63% and 37%, respectively. Conclusion This study enables a way to valorize two biomass‐derived excess chemicals on La and Ni catalysts for the first time in the literature. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: Long‐term VOC and siloxane removal in an anoxic biotrickling filter inoculated with Methylibium sp.
works.abstract: Abstract Background Volatile methyl siloxanes in biogas hinder energy recovery due to abrasive silica deposits formed during combustion. Biological removal in biotrickling filters (BTFs) is constrained by low gas–liquid mass transfer, yet few studies separate transport from biological limitations in anoxic conditions. This study evaluates the long‐term performance of a BTF inoculated with Methylibium sp. for the removal of D4, D5, hexane, toluene and limonene under anoxic and microaerobic conditions over 265 days. Results Batch assays showed that co‐substrate availability was the primary factor enhancing Methylibium growth ( P = 0.002), strongest under microaerobic conditions (interaction P = 0.005), while nitrate had no effect ( P ≥ 0.75). In the BTF, toluene (RE > 97%) and limonene (RE 86%–98%) were consistently removed throughout operation. Hexane removal responded strongly to electron acceptor supply (RE 17–100%). In contrast, D4 and D5 RE were largely invariable (13.1 ± 0.7% and 27.6 ± 1.1%; ranges 8.8%–17.9% and 18.9%–30.3%) regardless of EBRT (4.4–15.5 min) or electron acceptor regime, with elimination capacities increasing proportionally with loading, a behavior characteristic of gas–liquid mass transfer limitation. The higher RE of D5 than D4, opposite to the ranking predicted from air–water partitioning, indicates that other factors also contribute. Conclusion The BTF achieved near‐complete VOC removal and partial siloxane abatement under biogas‐compatible conditions. Siloxane removal, relatively stable and largely independent of EBRT and electron acceptor, is constrained primarily by mass transfer rather than by biological capacity. These results support using the BTF as a first purification stage coupled with a downstream adsorption polishing step. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: Robust multivariable control for enhanced microalgae biomass and lipid productivity in continuous photobioreactors (Robust multivariable control in continuous microalgae photobioreactors)
works.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Microalgae have high potential as a primary source (lipids and carbohydrates) for sustainable energy production ( e.g. biodiesel, biogas, bioethanol) and high‐value biomass secondary products (feed and nutrient supplements). High production costs are the main barrier to commercializing microalgal‐derived biofuels. Thus, various methods have been proposed to enhance microalgal biomass and lipid content. This paper addresses enhancements in lipid and biomass productivity in microalgal continuous photobioreactors using nonlinear programming optimization and two robust control approaches. RESULTS The favorable selection of the dilution rate and the input nutrient concentration as manipulable variables, along with the design of controllers using robust nonlinear model predictive control and modeling error compensation approaches, leads to reliable and efficient multivariable control approaches aimed at improving biomass and lipid productivities in microalgae photobioreactors simultaneously. Numerical simulations of the proposed control approaches demonstrate good and robust closed‐loop performance under significant model uncertainties and external perturbations. CONCLUSIONS Two robust controllers with simple design and structure are introduced to address underlying uncertainties in the mathematical models of microalgae photobioreactors. The proposed control schemes enable simultaneous manipulation of the dilution rate and substrate input concentration to enhance lipid and biomass productivities. © 2026 The Author(s). Journal of Chemical Technology and Biotechnology published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: Combretum quadrangulare Kurz extracts trigger apoptosis in HepG2 cells through modulation of survivin , Bcl‐2 and caspase‐3 genes
works.abstract: Abstract Background Combretum quadrangulare Kurz is a medicinal plant widely used in Asia. The leaf and seed extracts have been highlighted for possessing diverse biological activities, including cytotoxic effects against cancer cells. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the cytotoxic effects of ethanol extracts from the leaves, roots, and seeds of C. quadrangulare Kurz on HepG2 liver cancer cells, with a focus on elucidating the mechanisms of apoptosis induction and associated gene expression changes. Results High‐performance liquid chromatography analysis revealed that the ethanol extracts of C. quadrangulare Kurz leaves (CLE), roots (CRE), and seeds (CSE) contained major phytochemical constituents, including phenolic acids, flavonoids, and terpenoids. After 72 h of treatment, CLE and CRE showed significantly higher cytotoxicity compared to CSE. Remarkably, CLE selectively targeted HepG2 cells over non‐cancerous cells. All three extracts effectively triggered apoptosis in HepG2 cells, as evidenced by Annexin V/PI staining. Molecular analyses revealed that the apoptosis was associated with decreased levels of the anti‐apoptotic genes Bcl‐2 and survivin, while caspase‐3 expression was markedly increased at both the transcriptional and translational levels. Notably, the expression levels of caspase‐8 and caspase‐9 remained unaffected, indicating that the apoptosis occurred independently of these initiator caspases. Conclusion The C. quadrangulare Kurz ethanol extracts demonstrated selective cytotoxicity against HepG2 cells by inducing apoptosis, characterized by the downregulation of survivin and Bcl‐2 and the upregulation of caspase‐3. These findings suggest that C. quadrangulare Kurz is a potential candidate for developing new anticancer therapies, warranting further investigation. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: A review of the inhibitory waste metabolites produced during mAb biomanufacturing
works.abstract: Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell culture underpins commercial manufacturing of most therapeutic monoclonal antibodies, yet productivity and product quality remain constrained by inhibitory metabolic by-products that accumulate across batch, fed-batch, and perfusion processes. While lactate and ammonium have historically dominated monitoring and control strategies, untargeted metabolomics and stable-isotope tracing have substantially expanded the inventory of bioprocess-relevant inhibitors. This review synthesizes current understanding of 17 inhibitory metabolites spanning eight metabolic pathways. These include branched-chain amino acid catabolites (isobutyrate, isovalerate, and 2-hydroxyisocaproate), aromatic amino acid derivatives (phenyllactate, indole-3-carboxylate), nucleotide-pathway by-products (cytidine monophosphate, guanosine monophosphate, and succinyladenosine), and apoptosis-correlated species such as glycerol-3-phosphocholine and oxidized glutathione. Reported concentration thresholds are compiled for better-studied inhibitors, while correlative evidence linking accumulation to apoptosis, reduced productivity, and altered glycosylation is summarized. We evaluate the analytical workflow combining LC-MS and NMR for discovery, Raman spectroscopy for in-line monitoring, and stable-isotope tracing for pathway validation. Control strategies are critically compared across three tiers: media and feed reformulation (amino acid limitation, dynamic pH, or oxygen-uptake-rate-driven feeding), targeted and multiplex genetic engineering (BCAT1 knockout, combined LDHA/PDK editing), and keto-acid precursor substitution. We close by identifying concrete gaps, chiefly the absence of cell-line-independent inhibition thresholds, and argue that coupling genome-scale metabolic models with PAT data is the logical next step toward predictive, closed-loop mAb manufacturing.

works.title: Issue Publication Information
Defect-Driven Bimetallic Modulation: Accelerating Electrocatalytic Ammonia Oxidation Kinetics via a Nitrogen-Deficient FeCuN-Derived Architecture
works.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic ammonia oxidation (AOR) offers an energy-efficient route to carbon-free hydrogen production but is constrained by sluggish multielectron-transfer kinetics and adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) scaling relationships. Here, electrodeposition yielded a nickel-foam-supported bimetallic FeCuN catalyst (FeCuN-BH), followed by high-temperature hydrogenation to introduce abundant lattice nitrogen vacancies (FeCuN-AH). The rationally engineered FeCuN-AH architecture demonstrates superior AOR performance, requiring an exceptionally low applied potential of 0.61 V vs the saturated calomel electrode (SCE) to reach 50 mA cm–2, together with an apparent Tafel slope of 934.7 mV dec–1, substantially lower than the 2408 mV dec–1 measured for FeCuN-BH, and stable operation over 50 h. Comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate a lattice nitrogen vacancy-mediated dual-site synergistic mechanism (LNVM-MSM). The incorporated nitrogen vacancies not only serve as preferential active centers for ammonia adsorption but also drastically reduce the kinetic energy barrier of the rate-determining step (RDS, *NH2 to *NH) from 2.04 eV on pristine copper sites down to 0.90 eV. Furthermore, these defect sites induce local electronic redistribution and modify intermediate adsorption energetics. By circumventing conventional scaling limitations, this defect-driven dual-site structure provides a robust and scalable framework for designing active, durable electrocatalysts for sustainable hydrogen extraction and advanced energy-conversion devices.

works.title: Modular Hydrogen-Driven Electrochemical Systems Integrated with a Proton Exchange Membrane Electrolyzer for Dynamic CO2 Capture in Occupied Enclosed Spaces
works.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-driven electrochemical CO2 capture systems (HECCS) offer a promising technology for direct air capture (DAC). However, the coordinated operation of HECCS with water electrolysis under dynamic conditions poses significant challenges, and the system-level optimization of the integrated system remains unexplored. In this work, a modular hydrogen-driven electrochemical CO2 capture system integrated with a proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer is proposed for time-varying CO2 capture in enclosed spaces. A multiperiod optimization framework with surrogate models of HECCS modules and the PEM electrolyzer is developed to optimize the design and operation of the integrated system. A case study of DAC for a 600 m3 enclosed space accommodating 50 occupants is exemplified to evaluate techno-economic performances of the integrated system. The results demonstrate that the modular configuration enhances operational flexibility by enabling adjustable module on/off states, series–parallel configurations, and independent regulation of gas flow and current density, allowing the system to maintain high electron efficiency under time-varying demands of CO2 removal. The total cost of the integrated system increases as the allowable CO2 concentration limit decreases, with operational costs dominating the total cost and accounting for about three quarters, whereas the capital expenditure of HECCS shares the smallest portion. For simultaneous CO2 removal and O2 supply in the occupied enclosed space, these findings provide deep insights and optimization guidance for the design of air quality control systems by using the HECCS integrated with PEM electrolysis.

works.title: Issue Editorial Masthead
Electronically Asymmetric RuNP–Co2N Heterostructures Trigger Chloride-Adaptive Kinetic Acceleration for Industrial High-Current-Simulated Seawater Electrolysis
works.abstract: Abstract The development of efficient electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) under universal-pH and seawater conditions is highly desirable for practical hydrogen production. In this work, an electronically asymmetric heterostructure catalyst of RuNP–Co2N is constructed to optimize HER kinetics. The experimental and theoretical calculation results demonstrate that the electron-deficient Ru sites exhibit a fast Volmer process and optimize hydrogen intermediate adsorption. A distinctive apparent activation energy (Ea) sequence is revealed: acidic < simulated seawater < pristine alkaline media. Multi-salt control experiments confirm that the anomalous kinetic acceleration is exclusively triggered by chloride (Cl-) adsorption, firmly excluding sodium (Na+) hydration effects. Consequently, RuNP–Co2N delivers exceptional simulated seawater performance, with its high-current performance outshining its alkaline counterparts. It requires 245 and 350 mV to achieve 500 and 1000 mA cm–2 in simulated seawater, respectively, highlighted by a 39 mV reduction at 500 mA cm–2 compared to that in 1 M KOH. Concurrently, it only needs 145 mV to reach 1000 mA cm-2 in acidic electrolyte. Moreover, outstanding HER stability is also maintained in diverse electrolytes at industrial-level current densities. This work provides an effective method for constructing high-performance Ru-based HER electrocatalysts through electronically asymmetric interfacial engineering.

works.title: Contrasting Lignocellulose Degradation and Humification Responses to Biochar, Manganese Dioxide, and Penicillium oxalicum during Donkey Manure Composting
works.abstract: Abstract Efficient valorization of lignocellulose-rich livestock manure requires not only the decomposition of recalcitrant biomass but also the stabilization of organic carbon during composting. Here, biochar, manganese dioxide (MnO2), and a five-strain Penicillium oxalicum inoculum were compared in the same donkey manure composting system to determine whether preferential degradation of individual lignocellulosic fractions was accompanied by a proportional humification response. Biochar produced the greatest humification response, increasing final humic acid content by 191.2% relative to the control while increasing cellulose degradation by 6.11 percentage points. MnO2 resulted in the highest lignin degradation rate (31.14%), together with greater laccase activity and relatively high abundances of auxiliary activity family 2 and manganese peroxidase genes. P. oxalicum inoculation produced the highest hemicellulose degradation rate (80.42%) and higher acetylxylan esterase activity. Fluorescence analyses revealed distinct dissolved organic matter transformation patterns, while bacterial community analyses and structural equation modeling showed different relationships between lignocellulosic components and humification among treatments. Greater degradation of an individual lignocellulosic fraction was therefore not accompanied by a proportional increase in humification. These findings indicate that amendment selection for lignocellulose-rich manure should consider organic carbon stabilization together with substrate degradation, providing a basis for the resource utilization of livestock manure.

works.title: Unraveling the Mechanism of Dual Hydrogen Sources in Reductive Lignin Depolymerization over Ru/C
works.abstract: Abstract Lignin valorization is a critical pillar for the economic feasibility of modern biorefineries and sustainable renewable energy production. However, lignin’s inherent chemical recalcitrance poses a fundamental barrier to its efficient conversion. While catalytic transfer hydrogenation (CTH) is highly effective for reductive depolymerization, the mechanistic role and necessity of co-feeding external molecular H2 remain ambiguous. Herein, we use milled wood lignin (MWL) to elucidate the mechanism of Ru/C-catalyzed depolymerization involving dual hydrogen sources. Comparative evaluations reveal that secondary alcohols serve as superior hydrogen donors compared to primary alcohols. Introducing pressurized H2 successfully suppressed solid char formation to ∼1% but provided only a marginal enhancement in phenolic monomer yields. Monitoring 2-propanol conversion revealed a lack of synergy between the hydrogen pools. The presence of external H2 decreased in situ alcohol dehydrogenation from 26.6 to 20.2%. Density functional theory (DFT) computations validate these experimental observations, indicating a competitive adsorption regime wherein molecular H2 outcompetes the bulkier donor solvent for active metallic Ru sites, hindering the primary CTH cycle. Ultimately, these insights reveal that the hydrogen donor solvent provides an entirely adequate hydrogen pool to effectively drive depolymerization, negating the need for additional pressurized H2 and guiding highly efficient, H2-free biorefinery designs.

works.title: Unveiling the Trade-Off between H2O2 Photosynthetic Efficiency and Stability for Sustained H2O2 Accumulation
works.abstract: Abstract Sustained hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) accumulation remains a critical bottleneck for conjugated organic polymers (COPs). Spirobifluorene-based COPs, namely NBT, BT, and 2FBT, were synthesized using benzothiadiazole derivatives as the crosslinkers to determine H2O2 adsorption and desorption properties. NBT exhibited a superior H2O2 production rate of 6.40 mmol g–1 h–1, an apparent quantum yield of 11.1%, and a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 1.19%. However, its long-term H2O2 accumulation declined relative to both BT and 2FBT, owing to excessively strong H2O2 adsorption arising from hydrogen bonding. Whereas BT exhibited enhanced H2O2 accumulation owing to its favorable production rate, rapid desorption, and minimal decomposition, thereby achieving H2O2 concentrations of 4.0 mmol L–1 in a stirred biphasic system and 19.2 mmol L–1 in a continuous-flow system employing a benzyl alcohol/water biphasic medium. This work proposes a fundamental trade-off between H2O2 photosynthetic efficiency and stability: an efficient H2O2 production rate should be synergistically coupled with weak adsorption and rapid desorption, even though the production rate is not maximal.

works.title: Retraction Note: Bioprocessing of camptothecin from Alternaria brassicicola, an endophyte of Catharanthus roseus, with a strong antiproliferative activity and inhibition to Topoisomerases
A bioluminescence immunosensor using engineered antibody for quantitative detection of African swine fever virus
works.abstract: Abstract African swine fever (ASF), caused by ASF virus (ASFV), poses a significant threat to global swine industries due to its high mortality and the lack of an effective vaccine. Consequently, it is critical to develop a rapid and quantitative detection method for timely monitoring of swine populations and accurate confirmation of ASF infection, thereby enhancing ASF prevention and control measures. Here, we developed an ultrasensitive bioluminescence immunosensor for quantitative detection of ASFV p30 (p30-UBI) by genetically fusing HiBiT (an 11-amino-acid peptide that binds the NanoLuc fragment LgBiT with high affinity, reconstituting bright bioluminescence) to the light chain constant region of monoclonal antibody (mAb) 16-5E7E8 as the detection antibody and using mAb 2-1B3G3 as the capture antibody. The p30-UBI exhibited broad linear ranges of 46 pg/mL to 250 ng/mL for recombinant p30 protein (a combined quantitative range covered by two calibration equations) with detection limits of 15.3 pg/mL. The practical utility of the p30-UBI was evaluated using tissue, serum, and swab samples from ASFV-challenged pigs. P30 was readily detectable in tissue and serum samples, whereas lower concentrations were measured in swabs, and p30 levels showed broadly similar patterns to ASFV p72 gene copy numbers determined by quantitative PCR (qPCR). Notably, in an exploratory analysis in which pigs from different vaccine groups and dose groups were combined, lower serum p30 levels at 7 dpc were significantly associated with longer survival after ASFV challenge (Spearman ρ = − 0.62, P < 0.0001, n = 53). These findings indicate that the p30-UBI is a promising quantitative analytical method evaluated in samples from experimentally infected pigs. Key points • A HiBiT-tagged antibody-based bioluminescence immunosensor was developed for ASFV p30 detection • The assay achieves detection limits of 15.3 pg/mL for p30 within 70 min • Lower serum p30 levels at 7 dpc were associated with longer survival in an exploratory analysis

works.title: The role of nMOFs in anticancer combinations of photodynamic therapy and immunotherapy
works.abstract: Nano Metal–Organic Frameworks (nMOFs) have emerged as a versatile class of porous materials with significant potential in biomedical applications, particularly in cancer treatment. This review explores the pivotal role of nMOFs in facilitating the combination of photodynamic therapy (PDT) and immunotherapy (IMT), focusing on their unique capabilities to additively enhance therapeutic outcomes. By serving as efficient carriers and delivery systems for photosensitizers (PSs) and immunotherapy drugs, nMOFs can serve as immune response modulators and enable targeted tumour destruction through reactive oxygen species (ROS generation, while simultaneously stimulating antitumor immunity. The combination of nMOF-based PDT with immunotherapy represents a promising strategy for more effective cancer treatments. This article highlights recent progress, challenges, and future perspectives in leveraging nMOFs for the additive cancer therapy landscape.

works.title: Zinc-doped carbon catalysts with peroxidase-like activity for Neutral-pH antibacterial applications via reactive oxygen species generation
works.abstract: Bacterial antibiotic resistance has evolved into a severe global public health threat, creating an urgent demand for non-antibiotic antibacterial strategies. Peroxidase (POD)-like nanozymes that generate bactericidal reactive oxygen species (ROS) from H 2 O 2 hold great promise for infection treatment; however, most carbon-based nanozymes suffer from intrinsically low catalytic activity and strict acidic pH preference, which severely restricts their antibacterial efficacy under physiological neutral microenvironments. Herein, zinc-doped carbon catalyst (Zn-CN) were synthesized within 2 min via an ultrafast one-pot microwave-assisted strategy, using 3,5-diamino-1,2,4-triazole as the carbon/nitrogen precursor and zinc nitrate hexahydrate as the dopant source. The synthesized Zn-CN exhibits intrinsic POD-like activity at neutral pH ( K m = 123.1 μM for H 2 O 2 ), and shows excellent salt tolerance and thermal stability.
