This approach differs fundamentally from conventional batch workflows which typically mandate clarification and concentration before affinity capture and offers a novel process integration in viral vector manufacturing. A single-column batch capture process was developed first and subsequently compared to continuous CaptureSMB configurations. Optimized CaptureSMB operation achieved consistent yields over four cycles, with recoveries exceeding batch operation (+14.3%) with concomitant higher productivity (+11.4%) and reduced buffer consumption (-79.2%). Critical quality attribute (CQA) analysis showed lower host cell protein levels and lower residual DNA in early CaptureSMB cycles, while full capsid ratios, thermal stability and transduction efficiency of rAAV5 particles remained unaltered across cycles and process modes. However, progressive backpressure and residual impurity accumulation in later cycles highlight operational challenges associated with direct capture of low-titer feed streams. These findings highlight that continuous twin-column CaptureSMB directly from secretion-derived perfusion harvest can improve operational efficiency, lower buffer requirements, and also maintain and, in some respects, enhance product quality. This novel strategy provides a promising route to address manufacturing capacity and cost challenges in rAAV gene therapy production.

works.title: Enabling Raman Spectroscopy‐Based Cell Culture Process Control via Real‐Time Chemometric Model Calibration
works.abstract: Raman spectroscopy, combined with chemometric models such as Partial Least Squares (PLS), is a powerful enabling technology for real-time monitoring and control of industrial cell culture processes. Specifically, the non-destructiveness and near-real time measurement nature of the technology offers great potential in how processes are designed, monitored, and controlled, yet its implementation in industrial settings has been limited. This is mainly due to extensive dataset requirements for chemometric model development, as dozens to hundreds of cell‑culture constituents are known to contribute to Raman scattering effects. Experimental artifacts and anomalies arising from different sites, scales, or equipment further exacerbate this issue. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel one‑point calibration methodology that reframes the model training and validation paradigm from the "best chemometric model for the historical data" to the "best model for the most recent and representative data". Implemented within an adaptive‑learning framework, this approach drastically reduces dependence on extensive historical datasets while better accommodating site-, process-, and run-to-run- variabilities for the 9-14 day fed‑batch Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cell culture processes investigated.

works.title: A Microfluidic TFF Device for Biopharmaceutical Process Development: Scale‐Down Verification of Ultrafiltration and Diafiltration Modes for Monoclonal Antibodies
works.abstract: Tangential flow filtration (TFF) is an essential operation in downstream bioprocessing, yet conventional scale-down models require large material volumes and often fail to capture scale-relevant hydrodynamics. A microfluidic TFF (µTFF) platform was developed that preserves wall shear rate and transmembrane pressure, enabling low-volume investigation of UF/DF processes. Through iterative design of channel geometry and membrane selection, the final device achieved stable operation, high recovery, and a reduced runtime of 2.33 h from feed volumes as low as 10 mL for UF and 1 mL for DF. When operated at matched shear, the µTFF platform captured key bench-scale filtration characteristics, including filtration time, TMP behavior, permeate-flux profiles, and yields above 88% with negligible permeate loss. The device also resolved membrane-dependent behavior across PES and RC chemistries, showing consistent cross-scale trends for PES membranes while highlighting the influence of membrane-specific variability on RC membrane performance and cross-scale comparability. Validated with BSA and subsequently with monoclonal antibodies, the µTFF system demonstrated reproducible buffer exchange, maintained protein integrity, and replicated key transport phenomena. Its low working volumes, rapid turnaround, and ability to maintain scale-relevant hydrodynamics position the µTFF platform as a high-throughput screening tool for TFF process optimization, supporting faster development cycles and evaluation of purification strategies.

works.title: Engineered Magneto‐Receptive E. coli
works.abstract: Naturally occurring magnetotactic bacteria have an inherent ability to sense and align to earth's geomagnetic field due to the presence of magnetosomes-membranous microstructures containing iron oxide nanoparticles. These functionalities can be exploited for tuning movements and guided spatial patterning in controlled magnetic field. While being arduous to culture in laboratories, these organisms have complex genetic make-up with tight regulation on their magnetosome synthesis. Inspired by the magnetotactic bacteria, we aim to render magnetic behavior to E. coli. We mimic the magnetosomes in magnetotactic bacteria by employing a membraneless proteinaceous compartment from the thermophilic iron storage protein, ferritin, fused with a magnetite-forming peptide, m6A. To enhance iron accumulation, the E. coli iron metabolism is engineered by tailoring the expression of iron influx and efflux genes. Numerical simulations support our observations of a highly responsive magnetic E. coli. This study presents a strategy to engineer magnetic response in E. coli which can be adopted to other bacteria.

works.title: Metabolic engineering of plasmid-free Escherichia coli for enhanced biosynthesis of O-succinyl-L-homoserine
Comparative effects and mechanisms of microbial inoculants and enzyme preparations on vermicomposting performance and antibiotic resistance reduction
Optimizing light/dark cycle drives microbial synergy and cofactor metabolism in filamentous algae-anammox granules for zero‑aeration nitrogen removal
Dual limit determination for recirculation control against inhibition and sludge washout in anammox expanded granular sludge bed reactor
works.abstract: Recirculation simultaneously alleviates substrate inhibition through dilution and intensifies sludge washout through increased upflow velocity, yet these opposing effects are rarely quantified as explicit limits for recirculation control. A dual limit approach was established for an anammox expanded granular sludge bed (EGSB) reactor treating partial-nitrification-pretreated food-waste anaerobic digestion dewatering liquor, with lower and upper recirculation limits defined by inhibition control and functional granule retention, respectively. During 360 d of operation, the nitrogen loading rate increased from 2 to 6 g N L −1 d −1 , while nitrogen removal efficiency remained generally within 84 to 90%. Apparent inhibition responses of free ammonia, free nitrous acid and nitrite were described using the Levenspiel model, yielding IC 10 app values of 43 mg NH 3 N L −1 , 4 μg HNO 2 N L −1 and 1500 mg NO 2 – N L −1 , respectively. Free nitrous acid imposed the highest dilution demand and determined an inhibition constrained lower limit of R = 17. Granules were further separated by size to resolve their composition, activity and settling behavior. The 0.5–1 mm fraction combined the lowest settling velocity with the highest relative volumetric activity index, supporting its selection for hydraulic-retention design. An experimentally critical granule diameter of 0.5 mm was therefore defined, and its settling constraint produced a hydraulically constrained upper limit of R = 23. Coupling the inhibition constrained lower limit and hydraulically constrained upper limit yielded a reactor-specific feasible control window of 17 ≤ R ≤ 23, converting recirculation selection from an empirical setting into a dual limit decision against inhibition and sludge washout.

works.title: Editorial Board
Wood-based three dimensional microreactors enabled by nitrogen doped interface engineering for high-efficiency catalytic reduction of various pollutants
Growth-decoupled terpene biosynthesis from CO2 by a photo-heterotrophic coculture
works.abstract: Abstract Microbial conversion of CO 2 to chemicals is essential for a sustainable bioeconomy. However, this process is often hampered by low carbon fixation rates. Photoautotroph-heterotroph cocultures can potentially overcome this bottleneck by leveraging a strong carbon sink in the phototroph to drive carbon fixation, which is then coupled to heterotrophic chemical production. Despite the potential, exploiting cocultures for chemical production, particularly of low-flux pathway products, remains challenging. In this study, we established a synthetic consortium comprising a sucrose-secreting Synechococcus elongatus strain and a limonene-producing Escherichia coli strain to produce limonene from CO 2 as the sole carbon input. Through multiplex promoter engineering of the csc regulon, we identified sucrose consumption dynamics favorable for limonene production in E. coli , showing that expression of the invertase ( cscA) alone is sufficient to support growth on sucrose via the moonlighting activity of the lactose permease ( lacY ). A detailed characterization of sucrose consumption and limonene production revealed a biphasic growth-production scheme in the engineered E. coli , consistent with carbon flux being preferentially directed toward biomass during exponential growth. Comparative proteomics supported this observation, with higher mevalonate-pathway enzyme levels in the post-exponential phase. These results suggest that chemical production from low-flux pathways in cocultures could be enhanced by strategies that restrain heterotrophic growth. Based on these insights, we achieved a proof-of-concept CO 2 -to-limonene conversion titer of 11 mg/L. This study provides a framework for overcoming metabolic bottlenecks in synthetic consortia and offers insights to guide the future development of CO 2 -to-chemical production systems.

works.title: Carbohydrate catabolite repression is functionally redundant for the fermentation of lignocellulose-derived sugars by Thermoanaerobacterium thermosaccharolyticum
works.abstract: The phosphotransferase system (PTS) is a conserved mechanism in most bacteria, responsible for carbohydrate transport and regulation. This system plays a key role in carbon catabolite repression (CCR), a regulatory process that prioritizes the metabolism of preferred sugars. However, PTS and CCR have received little attention in fermentations of oligomeric lignocellulose-derived carbohydrates. Thermoanaerobacterium thermosaccharolyticum, a thermophilic gram-positive anaerobic bacterium capable of fermenting a diversity of simple and complex carbohydrates, is a promising candidate for lignocellulosic ethanol production. This study investigated the role of PTS and CCR by deleting the ptsH gene in T. thermosaccharolyticum. Monomeric sugar utilization experiments revealed that deletion of ptsH resulted in the loss of selective sugar utilization by effectively disrupting CCR. Assays with 2-deoxyglucose and cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) confirmed that ptsH is involved in the T. thermosaccharolyticum CCR response and is cAMP dependent. Its deletion alleviates catabolite repression, especially for cellobiose. Remarkably, fermentation of hemicellulose-derived carbohydrates from sugarcane bagasse spent broth was not affected by deletion of the ptsH gene, indicating that CCR has minimal impact under lignocellulosic carbohydrate substrate conditions. This research provides new insights into sugar catabolism regulation in T. thermosaccharolyticum, and for the first time demonstrates that CCR is not important when fermenting lignocellulose-derived sugars.

works.title: L-Lysine production from glucose and chitin monomers using engineered Vibrio natriegens
works.abstract: Abstract Despite its industrial importance, microbial L-lysine production has largely been confined to classical producer strains, leaving the fast-growing, non-pathogenic marine bacterium V. natriegens mostly unexplored as an emerging biosynthetic platform. In this work, we established an L-lysine-overproducing V. natriegens DSM759 strain through a stepwise rational engineering strategy targeting the native biosynthetic pathway. Building on our prior systems-level analysis of the strain’s genetic and regulatory architecture, we identified key metabolic bottlenecks and targeted interventions to relieve them. The central intervention was relief of feedback inhibition on the two key regulatory enzymes, aspartate kinase (AK, lysC ) and dihydrodipicolinate synthase (DHDPS, dapA ). Transferring feedback resistance substitutions previously characterized in E. coli to conserved positions in the V. natriegens DSM759 enzymes produced L-lysine-insensitive variants with kinetic parameters comparable to the corresponding wild-type enzymes. Among the tested configurations, the strain co-expressing Vn.lysC2 and Vn.dapA1 :E84T reached the highest L-lysine titer (9.0 ± 0.6 mM) and yield (0.11 ± 0.01 mol Lys mol Glc −1 ), whereas overexpression of additional L-lysine pathway genes provided no further benefit. Exploiting the host’s substrate range, we further demonstrated L-lysine synthesis from the chitin-derived amino sugar N-acetylglucosamine (0.09 ± 0.00 mol Lys mol GlcNAc −1 ), highlighting the potential to valorize chitin-rich waste streams from the seafood industry. This work establishes a minimal rational strategy for L-lysine biosynthesis in V. natriegens DSM759 and positions it as a candidate platform for sustainable amino acid production. Key points • E. coli-derived rational engineering strategies were transferable to V. natriegens • Native pathway deregulation was sufficient to enable L-lysine production • Chitin-derived N-acetylglucosamine supports L-lysine synthesis

works.title: Comprehensive analysis of zearalenone exposure and molecular effects in Rhodococcus pyridinivorans K404
works.abstract: Abstract Zearalenone (ZEA) is a Fusarium-derived mycotoxin that contaminates cereal crops and persists in soils and aquatic environments. Microbial biodegradation is increasingly proposed as a sustainable remediation strategy; however, a critical but often overlooked question is whether chemical disappearance of a toxin reflects actual detoxification. Here, we investigated the biotransformation of ZEA by Rhodococcus pyridinivorans K404 using an integrated analytical, toxicological, and molecular framework using time-resolved chemical profiling, bioluminescent yeast estrogen screening (BLYES/BLYR), zebrafish embryo toxicity assays, and transcriptome-wide RNA-sequencing. Although strain K404 reduced the ZEA concentration in the culture supernatant by up to 90.3% within 72 h, substantial amounts of ZEA and its metabolites were associated with the bacterial pellet, indicating that extracellular depletion reflected both biotransformation and redistribution into a cell-associated fraction. This decrease in supernatant ZEA concentration did not translate into a proportional decrease in biological hazard. In microinjection experiments, treated samples showed significantly higher developmental toxicity; embryo mortality peaked at 72% after 48-h treatments before falling to 53% at 120 h. This transient increase in toxicity aligned with accumulation of hydroxylated metabolites, mainly β-zearalenol and α-zearalenol, implicating biotransformation intermediates as key causes of acute toxicity. The bacterial strain showed a stress-associated transcriptional profile, dominated by genes of iron acquisition and oxidative stress defense. These results demonstrate that microbial ZEA degradation can transiently heighten toxicological risk, instead of reducing it, underscoring that microbial biocontrol strategies in agroecosystems must not rely solely on chemical depletion data but require comprehensive toxicological assessment, particularly through chronic exposure and long-term ecotoxicity studies. Key points • Rhodococcus pyridinivorans K404 efficiently removed ZEA (up to 90.3% in 72 h) • Transient toxicity increased via metabolites, while ZEA estrogenicity declined. • Transcriptomics at 48 h links peak cellular stress to metabolite driven toxicity.

works.title: Comparison of enzymes and amyloid hexapeptide for antibiofilm activity
works.abstract: Abstract This study screened and evaluated a panel of enzymes for their capacities to inhibit biofilm formation and disperse established biofilms, and compared their efficiencies with our previously developed amyloid hexapeptide GI6. Seven enzymes (mutanase, dextranase, collagenase I, dispase II, cellulase, lysozyme, and Dispersin B) and GI6 were evaluated against Streptococcus mutans (S. mutans) for anti-biofilm, bactericidal, and biofilm eradication activities. A human enamel block caries model was established, and the anti-biofilm and anti-caries effects were characterized by TEM, CLSM, SEM, and micro-CT. Among the seven enzymes under the tested conditions, only DspB (0.25 mg/mL) showed anti-biofilm activity. Immunofluorescence staining confirmed the presence of the DspB substrate poly‑N‑acetylglucosamine (PNAG) in S. mutans biofilms. Like GI6, DspB lacked bactericidal activity and could not disperse established biofilms. SEM and TEM confirmed reduced extracellular polysaccharides (EPS) and non-bactericidal effects for both. In the human enamel block caries model, both DspB and GI6 inhibited biofilm formation and reduced enamel demineralization, with GI6 showing better efficacy at a lower concentration. These findings indicate that most tested enzymes are ineffective against S. mutans biofilm under the tested conditions, and that DspB inhibits biofilm formation only at higher concentrations than GI6, suggesting that GI6 exhibits superior antibiofilm efficacy and anti-caries activity under the tested conditions. Future efforts in caries prevention may benefit from more effective biofilm-disrupting agents. Key points • Both DspB and GI6 decrease biofilm formation, but fail to disrupt mature biofilms. • GI6 suppresses biofilm formation and enamel demineralization at lower concentrations than DspB. • Agents that more efficiently targeting EPS in mature biofilms would have caries superior prevention value.

works.title: Pilot- to field-scale evaluation of a two-stage vertical flow constructed wetland system for piggery wastewater treatment
works.abstract: Abstract Piggery wastewater is a high-strength effluent requiring efficient and sustainable treatment solutions. This study evaluates a two-stage vertical flow constructed wetland (VFCW) system through pilot- to field-scale investigation, with emphasis on hydraulic loading, passive aeration, and techno-economic feasibility. At pilot scale, the system was operated at flow rates of 4–6 L day⁻1. At 4 L day⁻1 (OLR: 653.4 ± 43 g m⁻2 day⁻1), optimal performance was achieved. The control wetland (CW) exhibited removal efficiencies of 88.95 ± 3.12% (COD), 86.32 ± 5.48% (TOC), 87.71 ± 1.12% (phosphate), 73.37 ± 4.95% (TAN), and 51.25 ± 3.46% (TN). In comparison, the passively aerated system (CW-A) showed improved performance, achieving 90.36 ± 2.98% (COD), 89.68 ± 3.87% (TOC), 90.23 ± 0.98% (phosphate), 87.23 ± 4.23% (TAN), and 67.12 ± 4.23% (TN). Passive aeration achieved using perforated pipes inserted within the VFCW, significantly enhanced nitrogen removal, particularly through improved ammonium oxidation and overall nitrogen transformation, while having only marginal effects on organic matter and phosphate removal. Based on pilot-scale results, scale-up was performed by maintaining a comparable organic loading rate, and a field-scale system treating 7200 L day⁻1 (OLR: 604.3 ± 90.6 g m⁻2 day⁻1) was implemented. The system achieved overall removals of 87.85 ± 12.47% (COD), 86.35 ± 12.08% (TOC), 91.08 ± 10.63% (phosphate), 81.02 ± 13.13% (TAN), 60.45 ± 12.74% (nitrate), and 64.86 ± 13.62% (TN). Stable performance was achieved after a 4–5 week stabilization period, with resilience to influent variability. Techno-economic analysis indicated a treatment cost of ₹45.5 ($ 0.48) m⁻3 and low energy consumption (0.16 kWh m⁻3). The results demonstrate that OLR-based scale-up enables reliable field performance, confirming VFCWs as a robust and cost-effective solution for decentralized piggery wastewater treatment. Key points • OLR-based scale-up ensured successful pilot to field translation. • Passive aeration enhanced TAN and TN removal whereas field-scale system achieved > 85% COD and TOC removal in VFCW. • Low-cost (₹45.5/m3) and energy-efficient (0.16 kWh/m3) treatment. Graphical Abstract

works.title: Turning black rice husk waste into activated biosorbent for methylene blue removal: adsorption behavior and process optimization
works.abstract: Abstract This study aimed to utilize black rice husk, an agricultural waste with significant environmental impacts, to produce a biosorbent. In this way, black rice husk, which would otherwise be released into the environment as agricultural waste, was transformed into a useful material, and its use as a biosorbent for removing methylene blue, a cationic dye, was investigated. A biosorbent was prepared from black rice husk via thermal carbonization, with H 3 PO 4 (1:2 by mass) as the activation agent. Experimental data showed that the Langmuir isotherm, with a correlation of 0.9997, provided a better fit. Furthermore, the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller test result showed that the surface area of the biosorbent was 295.35 m 2 g −1 . Additionally, response surface methodology was used to determine the interactive and individual effects of various parameters, including contact time, biosorbent dose, and solution pH, on methylene blue dye removal. The experimental results show that the biosorbent derived from black rice husk has strong potential as an environmentally friendly, cost‐effective adsorbent for dye removal. This study is the first to report the use of a biosorbent synthesized by treating black rice husk, an agricultural waste, with H 3 PO 4 as an activation agent to remove methylene blue dye.

works.title: Development and evaluation of a microwave‐assisted continuous system for olive pomace oil extraction and in‐line esterification/transesterification
works.abstract: Abstract This study developed and evaluated a preliminary continuous microwave‐assisted system integrating oil extraction from olive pomace and subsequent conversion into fatty acid ethyl esters (FAEEs) in a single processing unit. A conventional microwave oven was adapted for continuous operation by incorporating magnetron power adjustment and a proportional–integral–derivative (PID) temperature‐control system. Extraction and integrated extraction/reaction experiments were conducted at 50 and 70 °C using ethanol as both the extraction medium and reagent. Additional experiments involved continuous catalyst feeding. At 70 °C, microwave‐assisted extraction yielded 12.05 ± 2.65 wt% oil, corresponding to a recovery of 99.42%. When the reactor was coupled to the extractor, FAEE formation was limited without a catalyst, whereas continuous catalyst feeding increased the FAEE concentration to 58.24 wt% at 70 °C and 39.12 wt% at 50 °C. The integrated configuration demonstrated the feasibility of simultaneous lipid extraction and conversion directly from olive pomace. Pressure buildup and associated limitations in temperature measurement were identified as engineering challenges. Further development should focus on pressure‐resistant fittings, improved temperature sensing, and optimization of the alcohol‐to‐oil ratio to improve process stability and overall performance.

works.title: Noninvasive electrical impedance tomography monitoring during total aortic arch replacement: incremental value for prediction of postoperative neurological deficit
works.abstract: Introduction: Postoperative neurological deficit (ND) after total aortic arch replacement (TAAR) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with limited effective preventive therapies available. Intraoperative neuromonitoring plays a critical role in reducing postoperative ND. This prospective cohort study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of electrical impedance tomography (EIT) and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) for predicting postoperative ND in patients undergoing TAAR. Methods: A 16-electrode EIT system and NIRS were utilized for intraoperative cerebral neuromonitoring during TAAR. Correlations between intraoperative EIT and NIRS variables and postoperative ND were comprehensively analyzed. Results: The overall incidence of postoperative ND was 39.1% (59/151), including a 15.2% incidence of postoperative stroke. The time integral of absolute resistivity asymmetry index during hypothermic circulatory arrest (TRAI HCA ), the maximum absolute resistivity asymmetry ratio during HCA (MRAR HCA ), age, body mass index, supra-aortic branch involvement, and operative duration were independent predictors of postoperative ND. Incorporation of EIT parameters into the clinical prediction model significantly improved the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.752 to 0.817 ( P = 0.027). Moreover, the incremental prognostic value of EIT was further validated by improved risk reclassification and discriminatory ability for ND, with a net reclassification index of 0.510 ( P = 0.002) and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.072 ( P < 0.001). Conclusion: The EIT parameters have been demonstrated to be an effective means of predicting ND following TAAR. Cerebral EIT may represent a potential alternative for intraoperative noninvasive multimodal neuromonitoring options.

works.title: The regenerative hexagon: six domains shaping musculoskeletal regenerative outcomes
works.abstract: The classical regenerative triad of scaffold, cells, and growth factors has guided musculoskeletal regenerative medicine for over two decades, yet outcome variability after orthobiologic treatment is not explained by preparation parameters alone. Contemporary regenerative biology already recognizes that host immunity, mechanics, and metabolism shape repair; what is less developed is a framework that integrates these dimensions for orthobiologic treatment and states their interactions in testable form. We propose an update of the triad concept rather than a replacement of it: a Regenerative Hexagon that retains the three construct components and adds three host-state domains that modify the response to them. These are the Systemic Host Environment, encompassing the gut-joint axis, sleep, medications, conditioning, metabolic status, and the pre-existing immune profile; Biomechanics and Mechanotransduction; and Cellular Energetics, defined as the energetic and redox state of resident and administered cells, which biophysical modalities are proposed to modify. Six short diagonals connect non-adjacent vertices, forming two interlocking triads that generate the Regenerative Star, and the framework is read as a sequence of states across the phases of repair rather than as a static configuration. The evidence for each component is graded with explicit criteria, and interactions demonstrated within a single experimental system are separated from those inferred from separate literatures. Convergent mechanisms are proposed: sleep fragmentation in healthy volunteers and dysbiosis-derived endotoxin in mechanistic studies both engage Toll-like receptor 4 signalling, and host metabolic burden was associated with orthobiologic response in a preparation-dependent manner. We hypothesize that the pillars interact multiplicatively rather than additively, a proposition not yet supported by a quantitative model and testable in factorial trials. The Regenerative Star is offered as a hypothesis-generating framework rather than a validated clinical instrument, reorienting inquiry from which preparation is superior toward in which host a given preparation performs.

works.title: Osteochondral unit–based management of focal articular cartilage and osteochondral defects: a narrative review of surgical repair, clinical decision-making, and tissue engineering
works.abstract: The therapeutic goal for articular cartilage and osteochondral defects has increasingly emphasized osteochondral unit reconstruction. This review uses the principal osteochondral tissues targeted by each strategy as a framework to compare marrow stimulation, scaffold enhancement, osteochondral transplantation (autograft or allograft), cell-mediated regeneration, and engineered regeneration strategies in terms of their indications, clinical outcomes, limitations, and translational boundaries. A structured narrative synthesis was performed after searching PubMed and screening clinical studies, systematic reviews, and representative translational and preclinical studies; 127 references were ultimately included. Current evidence indicates that procedure selection is primarily informed by defect size and depth, subchondral bone status, lesion location, prior surgical history, and joint mechanical environment. Microfracture may be used for small, contained defects with limited subchondral bone involvement, but the long-term durability of the repair tissue remains inadequate. Autologous Matrix-Induced Chondrogenesis (AMIC) can enhance the reparative environment after marrow stimulation, yet evidence heterogeneity remains substantial across lesions and techniques. Osteochondral Autograft Transplantation (OAT) is suitable for small-to-medium, well-defined osteochondral defects in patients with high functional demands, although it is limited by autologous donor-site availability. Osteochondral Allograft Transplantation (OCA) can provide single-stage structural reconstruction for medium-to-large lesions involving subchondral bone or after previous treatment failure, but still faces challenges in graft availability, osseous integration, graft failure, and reoperation burden. Autologous Chondrocyte Implantation/Matrix-induced autologous chondrocyte implantation (ACI/MACI) is more applicable to medium-to-large focal full-thickness chondral defects, provided that the subchondral bone is largely intact or can be reconstructed concomitantly; its long-term outcomes are constrained by patient selection, correction of joint mechanics, rehabilitation duration, and cost. Hydrogels, biphasic or multiphasic scaffolds, and 3D bioprinting enable stratified biomimetic reconstruction, yet clinical evidence lags behind basic research. Therefore, articular cartilage repair should be individualized according to the osteochondral tissues involved and the extent of involvement, with concomitant correction of malalignment, joint instability, and meniscal deficiency. Future research should use standardized outcomes, long-term follow-up, and high-quality comparative studies to clarify the true added value and clinical translatability of emerging strategies relative to established procedures.

works.title: Establishment of an electrochemical sensor for detection of Helicobacter pylori based on CRISPR/Cas12a trans-cleavage activity
works.abstract: Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) is one of the main causes of gastritis and gastric ulcers. Therefore, early detection of H. pylori is of great significance for the primary prevention of gastric cancer. Taking advantage of the trans-cleavage ability of Cas effector proteins, we developed a novel CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated electrochemical sensor for the detection of the vacAs1 gene of H. pylori . In this system, gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) were first electrodeposited on the gold electrode, which not only served to immobilize nonspecific ssDNA but also improved the conductivity of the electrode, thereby enhancing the sensitivity of the sensor. By combining recombinase-assisted amplification (RAA) with the trans-cleavage activity of CRISPR/Cas12a, changes in the amount of ssDNA were induced, further altering electronic transfer on the electrode surface. The developed CRISPR/Cas12a-based electrochemical biosensor exhibited a wider detection range (5.4 × 10 −19 −5.4 × 10 −13 M) and a low detection limit (9.5 × 10 −20 M). Moreover, the biosensor showed good recovery for the detecting H. pylori in spiked stool and artificial saliva samples. In addition, the biosensor exhibited good specificity and stability, suggesting that it may serve as a potential tool for the rapid, stable, and efficient detecting of H. pylori .

works.title: A 3D co-culture strategy combining fetal liver bud-derived cells and adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cells for spheroid formation and decellularized liver scaffold colonization
works.abstract: Engineering liver-like constructs remains challenging because hepatic cell function depends on coordinated interactions between parenchymal progenitors, supportive stromal cells, and the highly organized extracellular matrix (ECM) microenvironment of the liver. Although three-dimensional culture can enhance cell–cell interactions, reproducing the structural and biochemical complexity of native hepatic tissue remains difficult. Decellularized liver scaffolds provide an organ-specific ECM while preserving relevant tissue architecture, whereas mesenchymal stromal cells may provide complementary cellular support to developing hepatic populations. Here, we investigated whether combining E12.5 fetal liver bud-derived cells (LBCs) with adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (AD-MSCs) could support 3D spheroid organization and subsequent colonization of decellularized rat liver scaffolds. LBCs isolated at different developmental stages exhibited distinct proliferative and functional profiles, with E12.5 cells showing the highest proliferative capacity and prominent progenitor-associated features while retaining measurable hepatic-associated function. Rat livers were decellularized by vascular perfusion, resulting in extensive cellular removal while preserving a porous and fibrillar ECM containing glycosaminoglycan-associated components, collagens I and III, biglycan, decorin, fibronectin, and vitronectin. Three-dimensional vascular reconstruction further demonstrated preservation of an extensive branching vascular network. E12.5 LBCs and AD-MSCs spontaneously assembled into compact and viable spheroids, and their co-culture maintained expression of AFP and albumin together with stromal-associated markers. Functionally, co-culture increased albumin release but reduced urea levels compared with LBCs spheroids alone, indicating differential modulation rather than uniform enhancement of hepatic-associated function. Finally, LBCs/AD-MSC co-cultures were introduced onto decellularized liver scaffolds under dynamic rotary culture. After 7 days, cells showed extensive attachment and interaction with ECM fibers, while nuclear staining demonstrated cellular distribution across different scaffold regions and penetration beyond the external surface. Together, these findings establish an experimental platform integrating fetal liver progenitor/stromal co-culture, scaffold-free 3D organization, and organ-derived ECM, providing a basis for further studies addressing cell-specific fate, spatial organization, vascular recellularization, and functional maturation of engineered liver constructs.

works.title: Development and external multicenter validation of a multimodal nomogram integrating MRI findings and PSA biomarkers for individualized risk assessment of clinically significant prostate cancer
works.abstract: Background Accurate identification of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa; Grade Group ≥2 [GG2+]) remains challenging because prostate-specific antigen (PSA) lacks specificity and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alone may lead to unnecessary biopsies. We developed an interpretable model combining routinely available MRI and PSA-related variables. Methods This retrospective multicentre study included a development cohort from Center 1 (n = 260) and external validation cohorts from Centers 2 (n = 91) and 3 (n = 29). Multivariable logistic regression integrated age, PI-RADS score, free-to-total PSA ratio, and PSA density (PSAD). Performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, reclassification, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis. External validation used the fixed model without refitting. Results In the development cohort, 112 patients (43.1%) had GG2+ disease. The model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.872 (95% CI 0.823–0.914) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.864, outperforming PSAD alone (AUC 0.807; ΔAUC = 0.065, 95% CI 0.012–0.120; P = 0.013). Calibration was satisfactory (Hosmer Lemeshow P = 0.797). The model improved reclassification (continuous NRI = 0.789; IDI = 0.206) and provided greater net benefit than the comparator strategies at the evaluated threshold probabilities of 20%–30%. At a 25% threshold, it avoided 17 biopsies per 100 patients without additional missed GG2+ cancers compared with PSAD ≥0.15 ng/mL/cm 3 . External AUCs were 0.832 (95% CI 0.733–0.917) and 0.880 (95% CI 0.690–1.000). Conclusion The MRI–PSA model showed favorable discrimination and satisfactory development-cohort calibration, with potential clinical utility for GG2+ prediction. Prospective validation in representative non-Chinese populations and diverse healthcare systems is required before broader clinical adoption.

works.title: A reproducible event-driven analytical framework for ECG-derived skin sympathetic nerve activity analysis: towards afferent signal processing for closed-loop neuromodulation
works.abstract: Background Quantifying skin sympathetic nerve activity (SKNA) is challenging because sympathetic signals are noisy, burst-like, and processing-dependent. Electrocardiogram-derived skin sympathetic nerve activity (ECG-derived SKNA) provides a non-invasive surrogate of sympathetic activity. Many existing SKNA analysis methods rely on semi-manual processing or static measurements, with limited attention to dynamic event-based physiology, reproducibility across large cohorts, or near-real-time applications. Objective To develop and evaluate a reproducible event-driven computational framework for analysing ECG-derived SKNA during transient sympathetic activation driven by simulated apnoeas, with potential application to future closed-loop neuromodulation. Methods The framework integrates electrocardiography preprocessing, multi-channel SKNA extraction, adaptive burst detection, event-centred physiological analysis, and sequential replay. It was developed using recordings from 50 pigs during apnoeas induced by intermittent negative upper airway pressure (INAP). Adaptive thresholds were defined as the maximum of a two-component Gaussian mixture model intersection, the baseline 95 th percentile, and a baseline variability criterion. Sequential offline replay was performed on the pre-processed SKNA, with each replay decision restricted to SKNA samples available up to that decision point. Burst occupancy was calculated in a 30-s trailing window updated every 10 s, with trigger activation requiring occupancy above 5% in two consecutive windows. The pipeline was also applied to an independent multi-event INAP recording. Results During sequential replay, a trigger was present during INAP in 43 of 50 recordings (86%). Among the 49 recordings in which the detector was OFF at INAP onset, 42 (85.7%) developed a new post-onset trigger activation, with a median detection latency of 24.0 s (IQR 18.9–54.3 s). In the independent multi-event recording, all three INAP events generated replay triggers, with detection latencies of 28.4, 30.0, and 20.0 s. Continuous replay of an intervention recording also showed event-specific SKNA and trigger outputs before and during dorsal root ganglion (DRG) stimulation. Conclusion This study presents a reproducible event-driven framework for analysing SKNA. The framework captures heterogeneous SKNA responses and allows sequential evaluation as new SKNA samples become available. By enabling dynamic SKNA responses to be monitored during physiological perturbations, the framework provides a practical foundation for prospective real-time validation and future closed-loop neuromodulation using SKNA-derived physiological feedback.

works.title: Fabrication of silk fibroin microspheres via microfluidics for Co-delivery of dexamethasone and epidermal growth factor to promote skin wound healing
works.abstract: Background The skin, serving as the outermost barrier of the human body, is highly susceptible to injury. Wound healing is a complex biological process, and the widely used repair methodssuch as split-thickness autografts have notable drawbacks. Hence, the development of advanced biomaterials that integrate both safety and multifunctionality for skin wound repair holds significant clinical promise. Methods In this study, silk protein (SF) droplets were prepared using microfluidic technology and cross-linked with ultraviolet light to form microspheres loaded with dexamethasone (Dex) and epidermal growth factor (EGF). The fabricated microspheres were subjected to thorough material characterization. In vitro cellular experiment and in vivo animal experiment were performed to explore the anti-inflammatory properties and wound healing efficacy of the microspheres. Results Characterization via scanning electron microscopy and inverted microscopy revealed that microspheres were uniform, loosely structured, and porous, and exhibited strong liquid absorption capacity. Thermogravimetric analysis, X-ray diffraction, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy results indicated that the material was stable and that the modification was successful. Based on the drug loading, encapsulation efficiency, and in vitro release profiles obtained during formulation optimization, 10 μg/mL EGF and 0.8 mg/mL Dex were selected for the preparation of DESF microspheres used in subsequent biological experiments (DESF microspheres, prepared by first loading EGF into SF microspheres followed by Dex post-loading). CCK-8, live/dead cell staining, and scratch assays confirmed that microspheres are non-toxic and promote cell motility. Angiogenesis experiments showed that the experimental group outperformed the control group in terms of total length, number of branching points and nodes. ELISA indicated that levels of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 were significantly reduced, suggesting that the microspheres exhibit good anti-inflammatory effects. In animal experiments, the wound healing rate in the DESF group reached 95.4% ± 3.7%. Histological and immunofluorescence analyses confirmed that DESF microspheres upregulate the expression of VEGF and CD31, downregulate TNF-α, and upregulate IL-10, thereby suppressing early-stage inflammation, promoting angiogenesis, and accelerating wound repair. Conclusion These findings suggest that the DESF microspheres can promot wound healing, with good biocompatibility, anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic properties. Thus, the DESF microspheres hold considerable promise for skin wound repair.

Green synthesis, characterization and catalytic application of silver‐graphene oxide nanocomposite for the reduction of nitrophenols and benzaldehyde
works.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND The industrial effluents contain toxic, persistent, and bioaccumulative nitrophenols and aromatic aldehydes, which pose serious environmental and health hazards. In the present study, a silver‐graphene oxide (Ag‐GO) nanocomposite was synthesized using Berberis lycium plant extract as a green reducing and stabilizing agent. The Ag‐GO nanocomposite was characterized using various techniques that revealed the crystalline nature of silver nanoparticles that were well dispersed on the GO surface with strong interaction. The Ag‐GO nanocomposite was applied as catalyst for the reduction of 2,4,6‐trinitrophenol, 2‐nitrophenol, 4‐nitrophenol, and benzaldehyde in aqueous medium using NaBH 4 as a reducing agent. RESULTS The UV–Visible spectroscopy was used to monitor the progressive decrease in the absorption peaks of nitrophenols and benzaldehyde. The Ag‐GO nanocomposite exhibited high catalytic efficiency in the reduction reactions, which were carried out at 15 °C. The reactions followed pseudo‐first‐order model with high correlation coefficient ( R 2 ) values (0.9806–0.9953) whereas the rate constants ( k ) were found to be in the range of 1.6 × 10 −4 to 4.0 × 10 −4 s −1 . CONCLUSION The catalytic activity of Ag‐GO nanocomposite was attributed to its high adsorption affinity for substrate molecules as well as increased electron transfer due to synergistic effect of Ag nanoparticles and graphene oxide. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

Rational design of dosage compensated expression vectors for multi‐subunit biologics manufacturing
works.abstract: Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells are the predominant platform for biologics production. Expression of multi-subunit proteins within a single CHO cell requires balanced subunit expression to achieve optimal product quality and yield. Through systematic analysis of CHO expression data generated at the discovery stage using co-transfected monocistronic vectors, we found that subunit expression balance strongly correlates with product purity across both monoclonal and bispecific antibodies. These insights enabled the rational design of multicistronic vectors for production cell line development. For bispecific antibodies containing Fab and single-chain variable fragment (scFv) arms, scFv chains were frequently overexpressed, contributing to reduced product purity. Increasing heavy chain (HC) expression, for example through the introduction of an additional HC gene copy, improved both purity and titer across multiple programs. Likewise, optimizing the relative positioning of knob and hole HC genes within bicistronic vectors helped balance chain expression and enhance product purity in a complex IgG-like molecule. Overall, early-stage monocistronic expression analysis provides a framework for rational vector design of multi-subunit biologics, enabling more efficient cell line development with the potential to accelerate preclinical timelines and reduce resource utilization.

works.title: SIM ‐ CaliRam : A workflow combining simulation‐informed references and biomass‐augmented features for in‐line Raman calibration of Saccharomyces cerevisiae
works.abstract: Abstract Raman spectroscopy is a promising in‐situ Process Analytical Technology for upstream bioprocesses, but transferring trained calibration models to new, independent fermentation runs without re‐calibration remains a challenge due to sparse sample references (SaR) and prediction drift caused by biomass‐induced fluorescence and turbidity effects. We present SIM‐CaliRam, a calibration workflow combining two physically motivated interventions. First, Simulation‐Informed References (SiR) densify glucose, ammonium, and phosphate labels using a feed‐driven, non‐reactive mass balance on a dedicated uninoculated non‐reactive feed run, where substrate dynamics are determined by feeding and dilution. SiR labels agreed closely with the SaR values. Additionally, Biomass‐augmented Feature (BaF) appends Raman‐predicted biomass as an additional substrate‐model regressor, providing a proxy for residual biomass‐induced spectral confounding in the feature space. The workflow is demonstrated on Saccharomyces cerevisiae fermentations and evaluated within a systematic grid‐search over established preprocessing options and six calibration methods spanning linear, Bayesian nonparametric, and neural network approaches. Conventional SaR calibration serves as the baseline. Training uses two AV runs, with model selection on a separate CV run and final evaluation on a held‐out TEST run. The best selected models achieve NRMSE TEST of 0.203 (biomass, SaR), 0.206 (glucose, SiR), 0.350 (ammonium, SiR + BaF), and 0.598 (phosphate, SiR). SiR improved phosphate prediction ( R 2 = 0.64) relative to SaR ( R 2 = −1.2), although the remaining prediction error limits standalone process‐control application. Selected preprocessing, learner, and augmentation configurations differed across analytes. These results support target‐specific model selection rather than a universal calibration pipeline.

Amelioration of lipid production by Cunninghamella echinulata: statistical optimization and GC-MS characterization
works.abstract: Lipids have garnered attention for their importance in pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals. Famously, oleaginous filamentous fungi produce essential fatty acids. In this study, optimization using one factor at time (OFAT) and response surface methodology-Box-Behnken design (RSM-BBD) approaches, Cunninghamella echinulata showed the highest lipid content (61.23%) under optimized OFAT conditions (60 g/L, glucose; 2 g/L; ammonium tartrate; pH value, 7 at 30 °C, and shaking for seven days). Lipid content of 59.37% was achieved using the BBD. One-way ANOVA indicated temperature significantly affected lipid content, while two-way ANOVA revealed significant interactions between temperature and ammonium tartrate concentration, pH and incubation time, and inoculum size and glucose concentration. Various agro-wastes used as media for C. echinulata growth and production of lipid with peach yielding the best lipid content (49.30%). Comparative analysis of lipid extracts by GC-MS of the best yield conditions revealed nineteen different fatty acids, with oleic acid, linoleic acid, gamma-linolenic acid, and palmitic acid present in high percentages of 35.49%, 21.31%, 21.78%, and 13.44%, respectively. The extracted lipids demonstrated antibacterial potential towards Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Bacillus subtilis, as well as antifungal efficacy against Candida albicans and C. glabrata. The inhibition zones ranged from 9 to 19 mm with 50 µL of 10% extracts (100 mg/mL). This investigation revealed that optimization of C. echinulata represents promising candidate for high lipid yield in addition to lipid extracts may serve as potential antimicrobial agents in the pharmaceutical industry.

Flocculation using selected cationic polymers reduces high‐risk host cell proteins in monoclonal antibody processes already during primary recovery
works.abstract: Highly intensified monoclonal antibody (mAb) production needs next-generation purification technologies for process streamlining. Cationic flocculants aid in clarification and can reduce DNA and host cell proteins (HCPs) decreasing the burden on purification. Using two different mAbs, we screened five different cationic flocculants for their potential to clarify cell culture fluid, while simultaneously removing host cell DNA and HCPs without affecting antibody yield and integrity. We identified Polymer X as the best performer, excelling in HCP reduction with 30%-50% reduction compared to an un-treated reference. Comparison to a commercially available polymer (Polymer D), showed a significantly higher and more robust reduction of HCPs for four different mAbs. Additionally, we investigated the reduction of high-risk HCPs, that are known to negatively impact final product quality or patient safety. We demonstrated that Polymer X excels in reduction of those compared to flocculation with Polymer D. Polymer X could be used to successfully (1) aid cell culture clarification, with achieved turbidities of less than 25 NTU, (2) maintain high mAb titers, with over 95% yield (in three out of four mAbs), (3) reduce host cell DNA by over 99% and (4) reduce total HCPs by up to 40%, including selected high-risk HCPs to be removed by over 90%. In a typical mAb purification scheme, an anion exchange chromatography is used to get rid of DNA and residual HCPs. The robust removal of HCPs and DNA shown by Polymer X might support streamlining of the purification.

works.title: Correction: Mitochondrial and plasma‑membrane transport‑based engineering enables industrial‑level isocitric acid production in Yarrowia lipolytica
Folding constraints and engineering strategies for functional production of structurally complex phage receptor-binding proteins in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: Bacteriophage receptor-binding proteins (RBPs) provide highly specific recognition of bacterial hosts and are being developed as biorecognition molecules and targeting components in antibacterial applications. However, recombinant production in Escherichia coli is frequently limited by poor soluble recovery and uncertain preservation of native assembly and function. Among the structurally complex RBPs emphasized here, many characterized tail fibers, tailspikes and RBP-associated depolymerases form oligomeric, often trimeric, β-rich assemblies that can create protein-specific folding and assembly constraints. This review critically evaluates four candidate constraints: conformational instability, structural complexity associated with multidomain and β-rich architectures, transient exposure of aggregation-prone surfaces, and imbalances between protein synthesis and productive folding or assembly. We assess domain and construct engineering, fusion partners, cognate chaperone co-expression, and modulation of induction kinetics. The proposed framework draws on experimental evidence from model RBPs and construct-specific studies. It also incorporates findings on other phage structural proteins and general principles of protein folding. Greater soluble recovery alone does not establish native oligomerization, structural integrity, stability or receptor-binding activity. Accordingly, the proposed structure-folding-function framework is hypothesis-generating rather than a universally validated mechanism or predictive algorithm. Based on current evidence, we suggest that poor soluble production of selected structurally complex RBPs reflects interacting, protein-specific folding and assembly constraints rather than a single universal defect. Optimization remains largely empirical because no prospectively validated framework currently links sequence and structural features to suitable expression configurations. Integrating standardized screening, quantitative folding and assembly measurements, and structure-informed prediction may support mechanism-guided strategy selection, provided that soluble recovery is verified by native assembly, stability, receptor binding, or another predefined application-relevant function. Overall, this review evaluates experimentally supported and proposed contributors to RBP insolubility during recombinant expression and summarizes potential strategies for improving soluble and functional production.

works.title: Catalytic pyrolysis of biomass waste using coal fly ash‐derived ZSM ‐5 zeolite for enhanced bioenergy production
works.abstract: Abstract Energy security and sustainability drive the exploration of innovative conversion strategies for abundant biomass waste into energy‐dense products (solid, liquid, and gaseous biofuels). This study demonstrated the catalytic potential of a coal fly ash (CFA)‐derived ZSM‐5 zeolite in enhancing biomass pyrolysis, focusing on lignocellulosic sawmill residues and post‐consumer food waste. The ZSM‐5 was synthesized via hydrothermal methods involving alkali fusion, dealumination, and silica enrichment resulting in a Mobil Five‐type zeolite confirmed by X‐ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and Fourier transform infrared analyses. Catalytic pyrolysis conducted between 350 and 550 °C and residence times of 30 min to 2 h revealed that moderate conditions (330–370 °C) for 30 min significantly enhanced bioenergy yields, with biochar carbon content exceeding 70% and higher heating value approaching 30 MJ kg −1 , condensable bio‐oil, and gaseous fuels. Morphological assessments by SEM revealed pore development conducive to adsorption and catalytic applications. These findings substantiated the potential of CFA‐derived ZSM‐5 to optimize biofuel production, facilitate waste valorization, and advance circular economy practices, aligning with sustainable development goals.

A multiscale population balance model links pellet micromorphology to oxygen-dependent growth of filamentous fungal cultures
works.abstract: Submerged cultivation is widely applied for filamentous fungi such as Aspergillus niger to produce biochemicals, including enzymes, organic acids, and complex secondary metabolites. Cultivation conditions shape morphology, determining whether fungi form dispersed mycelia or compact pellets. The resulting morphology strongly influences overall productivity. Here, we present a multiscale modeling framework that links micromorphological hyphal distributions within pellets to macroscopic population dynamics. We reduced three-dimensional pellet morphology from X-ray micro-computed tomography to a low-dimensional radial master function. This function approximates the local hyphal fraction by scaling a single radial shape function according to pellet volume and hyphal volume. Pellet volume defines the spherical pellet domain, whereas hyphal volume determines the total hyphal content. This morphology-resolved representation enables model-based interpretation of intrapellet oxygen gradients and the fraction of hyphae in shear-exposed peripheral regions. These variables form the basis of a two-dimensional population balance model. The model simulates oxygen-dependent pellet growth, shear-induced abrasion, dispersed hyphal volume formation, and biomass-associated glucose consumption. The calibrated model reproduced experimental pellet size and hyphal volume distributions in low- and high-shear regimes, indicating pronounced heterogeneity in oxygen limitation among pellet populations. At 18 h, the model estimated that 3% of pellets were fully oxygen-penetrated under low-shear conditions, versus 32% under high-shear conditions. Model-derived oxygen-supplied regions accounted for 76% and 91% of total pellet biomass under low- and high-shear conditions, respectively. This work highlights the importance of considering morphological heterogeneity within fungal populations in bioproduct optimization strategies. It provides a foundation for future predictive modeling of filamentous fungal bioprocesses.

Production, surface engineering and immobilization of recombinant Aspergillus oryzae β-galactosidase
works.abstract: β-Galactosidases (β- d -galactohydrolase, EC 3.2.1.23) are valuable enzymes for industrial applications ranging from the production of lactose-free products to prebiotics, low-calorie sweeteners, and surfactants. Specifically, the β-galactosidase from Aspergillus oryzae (Gal Ao ) is recognized as more suitable for synthetic applications owing to its superior lactose transgalactosylation-to-hydrolysis ratio. However, the limited stability of Gal Ao under the harsh conditions dictated by synthetic reactions remains a significant constraint. We produced Gal Ao as His-tagged recombinant protein in the Kluyveromyces lactis heterologous system to comparatively study its properties with respect to the commercial enzyme. Recombinant WT Gal Ao is slightly more stable (+1.4 °C T m value) compared to the commercial protein. Either enzyme showed comparable immobilization yields (~80%), but the recombinant enzyme displayed about 2-fold higher activity, with resulting better recovery (33% vs 18%), which was maintained even after 5 months. Three engineered variants were produced by targeting surface residues that were mutated to Lys to promote the formation of imine linkages with the carrier (glyoxyl Sepabeads TM ) in a controlled rather than random orientation. All variants could be immobilized, though with lower activity compared to WT (0.73-1.25 U/g). Although the recombinant expression system has still low productivity for biocatalytic applications, it represents a starting point for further optimization.

works.title: Integrating non-potable water streams into biomass pretreatment, enzymatic saccharification, and fermentation steps in lignocellulosic biorefineries
works.abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass (LCB)-based biorefineries offer a renewable alternative to first-generation biofuel production systems and petroleum-based refineries. However, their industrial-scale development is constrained by high freshwater consumption and the extensive use of costly chemical and nutrient inputs during biomass pretreatment, enzymatic saccharification, and microbial fermentation, which compromise both process economics and environmental sustainability. Non-potable water (NPW) resources, including seawater (SW) and selected industrial wastewaters (IWW), are increasingly being investigated as alternative process solvents, and depending on their physicochemical composition, may additionally provide chemical or nutritional constituents that support lignocellulosic bioprocessing. This review synthesizes current advances in NPW utilization across LCB pretreatment, enzymatic saccharification and fermentation steps, while distinguishing experimentally validated applications from emerging opportunities supported by mechanistic and physicochemical evidence. The available literature reveals that selected NPW streams can partially or completely replace freshwater in specific process operations and, in some systems, contribute auxiliary chemical or nutritional constituents that support pretreatment efficiency, enzymatic hydrolysis, and microbial fermentation performance. However, the suitability and performance of individual NPW streams are strongly dependent on their composition, the lignocellulosic feedstock, process configuration, and compatibility with downstream enzymes and microorganisms. The broader implementation of NPW-assisted lignocellulosic biorefineries remains limited by compositional variability, inhibitory constituents, salt accumulation, corrosion, inconsistent NPW characterization, downstream biocompatibility, and the scarcity of pilot- and industrial-scale validation. Future research should therefore prioritize standardized characterization and reporting of NPW streams, integrated process optimization, techno-economic and life-cycle assessment, process monitoring, and pilot-scale demonstration. Overall, the strategic integration of suitable NPW resources offers a promising approach for reducing freshwater dependence, improving waste valorization and resource efficiency, and advancing more circular lignocellulosic biorefinery systems.

works.abstract: The growing demand for biostimulants has promoted microalgae as promising biotechnological platforms. Chlorella sorokiniana has shown potential for agricultural applications; however, the effects of carbon substrates under mixotrophic conditions on biomass productivity, metabolite accumulation, and biostimulant activity remain poorly understood. Complex organic carbon substrates enhanced carotenoid production and biostimulant potential. Glucose supported the highest growth rate (0.6 d −1 ) and biomass productivity (2.9-fold the carbon-free control), whereas lactose reduced productivity to 0.57-fold. Lactose at 1 g C·L −1 maximized carotenoid accumulation (0.92% DW, 85% above the control), while skim milk at 5 g C·L −1 yielded the highest volumetric carotenoid productivity (0.46 mg·L −1 ·d −1 ). Quantifiable phytohormone concentrations ranged from 131.0 to 2924.1 ng·g −1 DW. Carbon substrate and concentration influenced phytohormone profiles, with concentration-dependent changes in the relative predominance of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and jasmonic acid (JA). Germination indices ranged from 232% with glucose at 1 g C·L −1 to 10% with bicarbonate at 5 g C·L −1 , maintaining identical substrate rankings across concentrations. Cell adhesion varied from 1671 to 105,544 cells·mm −2 , with bicarbonate promoting attachment at low concentrations, glycerol at high concentrations, and lactose consistently limiting adhesion. These findings demonstrate that carbon substrate selection strongly influences growth, carotenoid accumulation, phytohormone profiles, biostimulant activity, and cell adhesion in mixotrophic C. sorokiniana , highlighting its potential for producing biomass with tailored agricultural applications

Salicylic acid offsets productivity-infrastructure trade-off in marine microalga cultivation without carbon dioxide dosing
works.abstract: Salicylic acid supplementation recovered part of the productivity lost when a marine microalga was grown at elevated salinity without carbon dioxide dosing or pH control. Chrysochromulina rotalis was grown in a six-stage sequential-batch cascade in 10 L bubble-column photobioreactors, with pH control switched off, restored and switched off again at 35 and 50 practical salinity units and paired supplemented and control reactors at every stage. Commercial marine salts served as a controlled proxy for desalination concentrate. Withdrawing carbon dioxide dosing lowered maximum biomass productivity by 54%, whereas higher salinity with pH control retained 85% of reference productivity. With both stressors combined, reactors receiving 30 mg L −1 salicylic acid reached 52–54% higher maximum productivity than paired controls, recovering one-third of the loss relative to the reference, and raised nitrate removal from 55% to 81%; total fatty acid content nearly tripled along the stress gradient and was unaffected by supplementation. Each route was modelled as a 200-t yr −1 plant fed with seawater reverse-osmosis concentrate, with its own mass, energy and equipment balance. Production costs were 12.61, 28.54 and 19.19 € kg −1 , and cradle-to-gate global warming potentials 3.89, 3.92 and 2.65 kg CO 2 -eq kg −1 , for the reference, unsupplemented and supplemented routes. Supplementation was cheaper than the unsupplemented route in every Monte Carlo iteration but did not reach cost parity with the reference and fell below break-even once downstream recovery and processing costs were charged. Salicylic acid makes low-infrastructure cultivation cheaper and lower in carbon, but not yet competitive with conventional pH-controlled operation.

Development and assessment of biodegradable pectin films enhanced with anthocyanin-rich fruit extracts to support innovative sustainable packaging solutions: The potential of chokeberry, elderberry, and honeyberry extracts as natural colorants
works.abstract: This study aimed to develop novel biodegradable films based on citrus pectin enriched with anthocyanin-rich fruit extracts and to evaluate their physicochemical properties. The pH-dependent color response of chokeberry, elderberry, and honeyberry extracts was examined in buffers ranging from pH 2 to 12. The microstructure, optical, mechanical, and structural properties of the films were assessed, alongside changes in total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N) content during beef storage. All anthocyanin-rich extracts exhibited distinct color changes with pH, transitioning from red at acidic pH (pH 2) to blue-violet or green at alkaline pH (pH 10–12), confirming their pH sensitivity. SEM micrographs revealed that films containing the extracts exhibited increased roughness and microstructural heterogeneity compared to the control, likely due to uneven anthocyanin distribution. FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of characteristic hydroxyl (O-H), carbonyl (C=O), and polysaccharide (C-O-C, C-O) groups, indicating strong hydrogen bonding within the film matrix. The addition of fruit extracts significantly altered the optical properties of the films, increasing opacity (up to 4.41 a.u./mm for chokeberry extract). Mechanical testing demonstrated that the extracts slightly increased tensile strength (from 3.27 to 5.23 MPa) and elongation at break (from 12.21% to 20.02%), depending on the specific extract used. The results indicate that pectin-based films enriched with natural anthocyanin extracts possess favorable physicochemical and colorimetric properties, rendering them promising candidates for eco-friendly, pH-sensitive intelligent packaging. The increase in TVB-N content during storage confirmed beef spoilage, which corresponded with pH-induced color changes in the films, demonstrating their efficacy as freshness indicators.

works.title: Composite effect of xanthan gum and inulin on the quality of semi-dry milled glutinous rice flour
Argon Plasma-Induced Surface Functionalization and Antimicrobial Activity in Rice Bran Films: Impact on Barrier and Mechanical Properties
works.abstract: Rice bran is an agricultural byproduct with potential for biodegradable film formation; however, it lacks inherent antimicrobial activity. This study aims to induce antimicrobial activity without additives, rather by inducing functional group changes in films. Argon plasma was applied to rice bran (RB) and rice bran protein (RBP) films for 30 min to evaluate antibacterial, antioxidant, and functional changes. Treated RBP films reduced E. coli O157:H7 , S. aureus , and P. aeruginosa to the detection limit (0.9 log CFU/mL) within 8 h, whereas treated RB films reduced the bacterial populations to approximately 1.6 log CFU/mL at 8 h and inhibited regrowth up to 24 h. Plasma-treated films retained H₂O₂, and DPPH radical-scavenging activity increased to 79.68% in RB and 81.94% in RBP films. Atomic force microscopy revealed increased surface roughness from 0.17 to 0.18 µm in RB films and from 0.13 to 0.43 µm in RBP films. Hydrophilicity increased correspondingly, with water contact angles decreasing from 110.04° to 63.55° in RB films, while RBP films exhibited immediate water absorption. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy showed increases in RB carboxylate ratio (2.7 to 3.2) and RBP O–H/N–H ratio (0.9 to 1.6), indicating enhanced oxygen-containing functionalities. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy further confirmed increases in the oxygen and nitrogen contents by 1.5% in RB films and 4.5% in RBP films, respectively. WVTR increased, tensile strength decreased (RB: 6.17–3.50; RBP: 1.88 to 0.56 MPa), and onset degradation temperatures increased (RB: 261 to 265°C; RBP: 249 to 256°C). This study demonstrates the potential of direct argon plasma treatment to develop antibacterial RB and RBP films without incorporating antimicrobial additives.

Multi-dataset INST 13C metabolic flux analysis reveals robust fluxes but variable metabolite pools
works.abstract: Isotopically non-stationary metabolic flux analysis (INST 13 C-MFA) provides unique insights into cellular physiology but remains limited by low throughput and high experimental costs. This is particularly relevant for emerging C1/C2 bioprocesses, where isotopically stationary 13 C-MFA is generally uninformative due to limited labeling diversity. We developed a miniaturized and automated workflow that combines parallelized transient isotope labeling experiments with high-performance computational analysis to enable INST 13 C-MFA at microliter scale. Applied to an evolved Corynebacterium glutamicum strain growing on ethanol, robotic micro-cultivations with complementary tracers, hot isopropanol quenching, and LC-QToF-MS analytics yielded highly informative datasets. Joint analysis produced the first quantitative flux map of ethanol metabolism in evolved C. glutamicum , revealing strong glyoxylate shunt activity. Multi-dataset INST 13 C-MFA further showed that integrating complementary ILEs increased net flux resolution and preserved flux estimates across tracers and independent experimental runs, while pool size estimates remained dataset-specific. Together, this work establishes a cost-efficient, scalable framework for quantitative fluxomics and its integration into biofoundry pipelines, enabling systematic physiological characterization of microorganisms growing on sustainable C1/C2 feedstocks.

works.title: Machine learning-guided dual optimization of the substrate specificity and thermostability of yeast alcohol dehydrogenase
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Yeast alcohol dehydrogenase I (YADH) catalyzes the reversible reduction of aldehydes to primary alcohols. Thermostable YADH variants with broad substrate specificities at elevated temperatures are desirable for industrial biocatalysis. In this study, we aimed to alter the substrate specificity of YADH to efficiently catalyze the reduction of the non-native substrate, trans-2-nonenal, to trans-2-nonenol, while simultaneously enhancing thermostability. Residues around the substrate-binding site were identified by docking simulation and subjected to saturation and random mutagenesis. Measured activity and thermostability were used to train a machine-learning model to predict YADH variants with improved activity while maintaining thermostability. RESULTS: The machine learning-guided approach identified variants with improved properties. Four variants showed increased specific activity toward trans-2-nonenal compared with the wild type, and one variant also exhibited improved thermostability. The best-performing variant showed a more than twofold increase in specific activity along with retained thermal resistance. Variants that lost activity toward the native substrate acetaldehyde while gaining higher activity toward trans-2-nonenal were also obtained, indicating altered substrate specificity. These results demonstrate efficient identification of beneficial mutations from a limited dataset. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, this study presents a machine learning-guided framework that integrates docking and multi-model evaluation for simultaneously optimizing substrate specificity and thermostability in YADH.
