Moreover, frustule-adsorbed cells cross-linked with 0.5% glutaraldehyde (GA) exhibited enhanced catalytic performance in continuous batch operation. Finally, the repeated biotransformation was carried out by immobilized G. oxydans , achieving an average xylitol titer of 15.44 g/L over six consecutive cycles. This study presents a practical immobilization strategy for xylitol production and offers a reference for microbial production of other biochemicals.

works.title: Valorization of selenium‐enriched Lactobacillus biomass into selenium‐doped carbon dots via hydrothermal conversion: physicochemical properties and biological properties
works.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Selenium‐enriched microbial fermentation residues contain both carbonaceous material and biologically incorporated selenium but are often underutilized. Developing sustainable strategies to convert these residues into value‐added functional nanomaterials is important for waste minimization and circular bioeconomy. This study aimed to directly synthesize selenium‐doped carbon dots (Se‐LCDs) from selenium‐enriched Lactobacillus fermentation residues through a one‐step hydrothermal process and evaluate their physicochemical properties, antioxidant activity, biocompatibility, and potential techno‐economic advantages. RESULTS Hydrothermal treatment at 200 °C for 12 or 20 h produced quasi‐spherical Se‐LCDs with mean diameters of 8.5 ± 0.5 and 2.3 ± 0.7 nm, respectively. Longer treatment decreased the measured Se content and particle size while increasing nitrogen retention. Both samples showed excitation‐dependent fluorescence, with maximum emission at 420 nm under 340 nm excitation, and ABTS radical‐scavenging rates of 37.99% (Se‐LCD1) and 36.76% (Se‐LCD2). No obvious inhibition zones were observed against the three tested bacterial strains. Cell‐viability responses depended on cell type and dilution: high‐dose treatments reduced viability in some mouse‐cell conditions, whereas increased viability was observed in HUVEC and HT‐29 cells. These effects are consistent with possible contributions from particle size, surface functional groups, and heteroatom composition, although the underlying cellular mechanisms were not directly tested. A preliminary scenario‐based estimate suggested lower precursor costs when Se‐enriched biomass was used instead of purified organoselenium reagents. CONCLUSION This study demonstrates a sustainable route for valorizing selenium‐enriched microbial residues into Se‐LCDs with antioxidant activity and biocompatibility, providing a promising platform for sustainable bioprocessing, renewable bioresource utilization, and circular bioeconomy. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: Solar power‐driven, IoT ‐based system for electrochemical degradation of industrial dye using a pair of carbon electrode assemblies
works.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Textile industries discharge synthetic dyes into water bodies that resist conventional treatment, causing serious environmental and health hazards. Electrochemical advanced oxidation using carbon electrodes (graphite) offers an effective alternative by generating hydroxyl radicals that break down recalcitrant dye molecules. Despite its potential, most systems lack real‐world automation and renewable energy integration needed for practical deployment. This study shows that integrating readily available sensors and renewable energy could translate into industrial settings. RESULTS The solar‐powered electrochemical system achieved progressive dye degradation, confirmed by real‐time sensor monitoring. The carbon electrode assembly remained stable throughout treatment, while the Internet of Things (IoT)‐enabled microcontroller continuously logged concentration and electrical parameters, transmitting live data to a mobile interface. Dye concentration from 5 to 100 ppm was easily degraded up to ca 99% in 10–180 min with electrical power consumption ranging from 0.5 to 5 kWh m −3 . Automated feedback between sensors and power regulation reduced energy consumption during low dye‐load periods, improving overall treatment efficiency. CONCLUSION This study presents a functional, IoT‐controlled electrochemical system using carbon electrodes for treatment of industrial dye‐containing wastewater. By integrating solar power, real‐time sensing, and remote automation, the system offers a scalable and sustainable solution for dye‐intensive industries such as textiles and leather processing. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: Multi-omics insights into stress-tolerant HN-AD strains: Putative metabolic coupling and engineering application bottlenecks
A machine learning-driven correction of coarse-mesh errors in computational modeling of radio frequency heating
Multiscale oxygen transfer enhancement in high‑density Komagataella phaffii fermentation: dynamic pressure control and CFD‑guided industrial scale‑up
works.abstract: Oxygen transfer limitation is a key bottleneck in high-cell-density Komagataella phaffii fermentation for recombinant protein production. Conventional approaches based on increasing agitation and aeration may result in high shear stress, foaming, and increased energy demand. In this study, a multiscale oxygen-transfer enhancement strategy integrating dynamic headspace-pressure regulation with computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-guided bioreactor optimization was investigated. At the 5 L scale, response surface methodology demonstrated the combined effects of agitation, aeration, and headspace pressure on the volumetric oxygen-transfer coefficient ( $$ k_{L} a $$ ). A two-stage dynamic pressure (TSP) strategy was subsequently evaluated under fermentation conditions. Compared with the conventional-pressure condition, TSP increased the final dry cell weight (DCW) by 11.2% and the maximum xylanase activity by 19.8%, reaching 120.25 ± 1.04 g/L and 213.23 ± 2.10 KU/mL, respectively. The strategy was further implemented in a 1000 L bioreactor, where the peak oxygen uptake rate reached 185.23 mmol/L/h, with a final DCW of 124.08 ± 2.47 g/L and xylanase activity of 225.07 ± 3.64 KU/mL. At the 30 m3 scale, CFD analysis identified scale-dependent hydrodynamic limitations in the original agitation system and guided a combined redesign from 0.7 m Rushton turbines to a 0.8 m CD-6/3KSX hybrid impeller system. Under identical simulation conditions, the redesigned configuration increased the CFD-predicted average $$ k_{L} a $$ by 46.4% and reduced the predicted mixing time by 43.3%. Following implementation of the redesigned system, the final DCW and xylanase activity reached 134.01 ± 2.98 g/L and 242.02 ± 4.07 KU/mL, respectively. These results demonstrate a case-based multiscale approach combining process-level oxygen-transfer regulation with reactor-level hydrodynamic optimization for the investigated recombinant K. phaffii fermentation process.

works.title: Expanding the catabolic capacity of Pseudomonas putida to acetovanillone, 5-carboxyvanillate, and vanillyl glyoxylate for muconate production from kraft lignin-derived aromatics
works.abstract: The pulp and paper industry produces large volumes of condensed kraft lignin, which is challenging to convert to single chemical products. For this purpose, tandem chemical depolymerization and bioconversion to a single atom-efficient product is a potentially promising strategy. In this study, we conducted copper-catalyzed oxidative depolymerization using pine-derived kraft lignin to generate multiple bioavailable aromatic monomers at a yield of 4.5 weight% (wt%; g monomers per g lignin) from both C–O and C–C bond cleavage, followed by counter-current extraction with a 52 wt% monomer recovery. This resulted in an oxidized lignin product containing vanillin, vanillate, 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde, 4-hydroxybenzoate, 5-formylvanillin, 5-carboxyvanillin, 5-carboxyvanillate, acetovanillone, and vanillyl glyoxylate. Based on this stream composition, we engineered the industrially relevant soil bacterium Pseudomonas putida KT2440 to catabolize the latter five compounds via overexpression of ten heterologous genes ( acvABCDEF SYK-6 , vceAB SYK-6 , ligW2 SYK-6 , and mdlC PP ). We combined these engineered pathways with previously reported strategies for muconate production from G- and H-type monomers to generate P. putida KMM428, which utilized 93.6 ± 0.2 mol% of the quantified aromatic monomers in a depolymerized kraft lignin mixture, and produced muconate at a yield of 99 ± 3 mol%, on a quantified monomer basis. Together, this work increases the theoretical carbon conversion efficiency of this process by 37.6 ± 0.1 mol% through incorporation of three β-5 cleavage products, in addition to traditional G-type monomers.

works.title: An integrated strategy to reprogram NRPS initiation modules for long-chain surfactin biosynthesis
Progressive probing and iterative integration enable strain-state-specific fine-tuning of the MEP pathway for patchoulol biosynthesis in Bacillus subtilis
works.abstract: Abstract Background Efficient optimization of metabolic pathways in microbial cell factories remains challenging because the relative contributions of individual pathway enzymes can change with the metabolic state of engineered strains. Conventional metabolic engineering approaches generally rely on predefined targets or simultaneous overexpression of multiple pathway genes, which may lead to pathway imbalance and limited improvement. Here, we developed a Progressive Probing and Iterative Integration (PP&II) strategy for successive and strain-state-specific optimization of metabolic pathways. Results PP&II integrates a reusable enzyme-probing module with a CRISPR-Cas9-assisted genomic integration module, enabling assessment of enzyme contributions in each engineered strain and targeted genomic integration in successive cycles. After each engineering cycle, enzyme contributions were reassessed to guide the next round of genomic integration. The PP&II strategy was validated in the generally recognized as safe (GRAS) host Bacillus subtilis using patchoulol biosynthesis as a model system. Following establishment of a functional patchoulol biosynthetic pathway through optimization of heterologous patchoulol synthase expression, PP&II enabled successive assessment and genomic optimization of multiple 2C-methyl-D-erythritol-4-phosphate (MEP) pathway enzymes, including Dxs, IspC, and IspA. The optimized strain produced approximately 13-fold more patchoulol than the initial strain. Comparative proteomic analysis further revealed changes in protein expression following PP&II-based engineering, indicating alterations in the cellular state of the engineered strain. Conclusions Overall, PP&II provides a progressive, strain-state-guided workflow for iterative engineering of metabolic pathways and shows potential for improving microbial production of high-value terpenoids and other bioproducts.

works.title: Progress in the microbial synthesis and biomedical applications of silver and gold nanoparticles
works.abstract: Abstract Nanoscience has revolutionized materials synthesis, with noble metal nanoparticles like silver and gold gaining prominence for their unique physicochemical and biological properties. Microbial synthesis offers a sustainable, biocompatible alternative to conventional methods, leveraging bacteria, fungi, and algae as natural biofactories to produce stable silver and gold nanoparticles via enzymatic reduction and biomolecule-mediated capping. Here, we review mechanisms of microbial nanoparticle biosynthesis, characterization techniques, and diverse biomedical applications, including antimicrobial, anticancer, antioxidant, drug-delivery, imaging, and wound-healing functionalities. However, despite their promise, challenges related to toxicity, consistency, process scalability, batch-to-batch variation, and regulatory compliance remain significant concerns. Thus, a thorough assessment of nanoparticle physicochemical properties, biosafety, and therapeutic effectiveness is crucial to advance clinical applications. Overall, microbial nanotechnology offers a promising avenue for biomedical use, but further refinement and standardized assessments are needed to enable reliable, scalable applications. Key points Microbial synthesis of silver and gold nanoparticles is sustainable and biocompatible.Diverse microorganisms act as natural nanofactories capable of producing stable AgNPs and AuNPs.Silver and gold nanoparticles exhibit broad biomedical potential.

works.title: Effect of the moisture content on lignocellulose degradation, lactic acid fermentation, and the bacterial community of Sudangrass ensiled with bacteria‐enzyme inoculants
works.abstract: Abstract This study investigated the effects of ferulic acid esterase‐producing Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (LP) and fibrolytic enzyme on the fermentation quality, lignocellulose degradation, and microbial community of Sudangrass ensiled with different moisture contents. Sudangrass was ensiled at three moisture levels: low (LM, 70%), medium (MM, 76%), and high (HM, 83%), and subjected to one of four treatments: control (CK); LP; cellulase and xylanase mixture (CX); or a combination of LP, cellulase, and xylanase (LP + CX). Results showed that under most conditions, LP + CX generally produced the highest lactic acid (LA) and water‐soluble carbohydrate content, the lowest value of pH, ammonia nitrogen, neutral detergent fiber, and acid detergent fiber contents compared with CK, LP, and CX. Moisture content significantly modulated these effects: LM promoted LA content, resulting in a significantly lower pH, whereas MM was most conducive to lignocellulose degradation and led to a higher relative abundance of Lactiplantibacillus and a lower abundance of Enterobacter . These results indicate that moisture content critically modulates the efficacy of microbial and enzymatic additives, with LM favoring LA fermentation and MM improving fiber degradation and saccharification. Optimizing moisture content thus offers a viable strategy to enhance silage quality for sustainable biomass utilization by adopting LM for feed production and MM for fiber saccharification.

YlYxc1, an ER-associated alkaline ceramidase of Yarrowia lipolytica, has the hydrolytic activity of ceramides, which can be exploited as a metabolic engineering target to enhance long-chain base production.

works.title: Improved Biosynthesis of Ethylene Glycol From Xylose in Engineered E. coli Utilizing Two‐Stage Dynamic Control
works.abstract: ABSTRACT We engineered Escherichia coli for improved ethylene glycol (EG) biosynthesis using two‐stage dynamic metabolic control coupled with pathway optimization. An engineered Dahms pathway ( xylB, xylC, xylD, yqhD ) was induced upon phosphate depletion to enable EG biosynthesis during stationary phase. The performance of our initial strain, expressing a baseline pathway, was improved by the addition of “stoichiometric” valves enabling proteolytic degradation of xylose isomerase and soluble transhydrogenase, upon phosphate depletion. Reduction of these enzymes, which compete for substrates with EG biosynthesis, led to a 3‐fold increase in specific productivity. In contrast, enabling “regulatory” dynamic metabolic valves targeting enoyl‐ACP reductase and glucose‐6‐phosphate dehydrogenase, designed to enhance NADPH flux, did not improve production in this control. Following pathway optimization, regulatory strains exhibited enhanced production rates exceeding 0.5 g gCDW − 1 h − 1 , a 14‐fold improvement over the control, while stoichiometric valves conferred no benefit. Scale‐up in fed‐batch bioreactors achieved 140 g L − 1 EG in 70 h with a yield of 0.38 g g − 1 xylose (92% of theoretical), representing one of the highest reported titers in E. coli . These results demonstrate that optimal engineering strategies shift with pathway capacity. While elimination of competing fluxes benefits low‐flux systems, high‐flux pathways require enhanced cofactor regeneration.

works.title: Engineering Mosaic T7 Bacteriophages for Dual Peptide Display to Enable Cellular Targeting and Ligand‐Directed Protein Capture
works.abstract: Integrating molecular recognition, tracing, and interactome capture within a single nanoparticle could allow for probing, manipulation, and control of complex biological systems. Achieving such multifunctionality within a single well-defined nanostructure remains challenging. T7 bacteriophage-based biological nanoparticles provide a robust and genetically programmable scaffold; however, conventional T7 display systems typically accommodate only one exogenous peptide species per phage particle, limiting multifunctional and combinatorial applications. Here, we describe a mosaic phage platform that enables the simultaneous display of two peptides on separate T7 coat protein subunits. By combining genome-encoded and plasmid-driven expression of peptide-fused capsid proteins, the system provides a modular route for assembling multifunctional phage nanoparticles. We generated mosaic T7 phages co-presenting the neuropilin-1 (NRP-1)-binding peptide RPARPAR alongside either a HA-tag or a Twin-Strep (Tstrep) tag affinity handle. These engineered phages specifically target NRP-1-expressing cells and enable immunofluorescence visualization and pull-down of NRP-1 from complex lysates. Furthermore, a random peptide T7 phage library co-displaying the constant lung-homing peptide RPARPAR shows preferential pulmonary accumulation in vivo, demonstrating utility for combinatorial targeting and tissue-directed phage selection. Collectively, this dual-display approach expands phage display by enabling cell targeting, visualization, molecular interactome probing, and in vivo tissue homing within a single genetically encoded nanoparticle platform.

works.title: Issue Information: Biotechnology Journal 11/2026
ARTP Mutagenesis and Omics‐Guided Target Validation for Improved Human Serum Albumin Fusion Protein Production in Yeast
works.abstract: Efficient production of human serum albumin (HSA) fusion proteins in yeast remains constrained by the combined demands of folding, secretion, and cellular resource allocation. Rational optimization of endoplasmic reticulum folding and unfolded protein response pathways can improve production, but additional cellular constraints may persist in engineered strains. Here, we combined iterative atmospheric and room-temperature plasma (ARTP) mutagenesis, activity-coupled screening, and genome- and transcriptome-guided validation to improve production of an amylase-HSA fusion protein (AGSH) in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Using extracellular α-amylase activity as the screening indicator, five rounds of ARTP mutagenesis in the folding-optimized strain AH28 generated mutants with enhanced AGSH production. The final mutant N5S14 reached 2.12-fold the AH28 level in AGSH-associated α-amylase activity. Physiological profiling showed that enhanced production was associated with altered growth-production balance and changes in glucose, ethanol, and glycerol profiles. Whole-genome sequencing identified 33 candidate mutation sites, and reverse engineering validated genes associated with improved AGSH production, including BUD27, NPR3, NPR2, and IML1. RNA-seq revealed distinct transcriptional states involving central carbon metabolism, protein folding, and stress-related processes. Transcriptome-guided validation identified PFY1 deletion and SSA3 overexpression as additional beneficial interventions. Overall, this strategy improved AGSH production and identified engineering targets beyond previously optimized folding-related modules.

works.title: Biochar-microbe-hydrogel mediated pump-and-leach system for synergistic remediation of manganese-contaminated soil and groundwater
Green nanocomposite films from cottonseed meal proteins and eggshell-derived CaCO3 for blueberry preservation
Dynamic populations control of Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae consortia improves chemical production
Optimizing phosphate feeding through metabolomics and capacitance-based real‑time control enhances L‑threonine production in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: L-threonine is an essential amino acid in high global demand, and its efficient biosynthesis is a major goal of industrial biotechnology. In industrial fermentation, phosphate is typically supplied through fixed or manual feeding strategies that fail to accommodate real-time changes in cell growth and metabolic demand, representing a key process bottleneck. To address this, we first investigated the effect of different initial phosphate concentrations on L‑threonine production in a 5 L bioreactor. The optimal phosphate concentration improved L-threonine titer by 21.9% compared to the control group. Metabolomics and 13 C metabolic flux analysis revealed that this concentration reprograms central carbon metabolism, increasing the pentose phosphate pathway flux by 28.9% to enhance precursor supply and NADPH availability, two critical factors for L-threonine biosynthesis. Building on these mechanistic insights, we further established a more precise phosphate feeding strategy based on real-time on-line capacitance signals, enabling precise matching between phosphate feeding and cell growth status. When scaled up to a 50 L bioreactor, this capacitance-guided strategy achieved an L-threonine titer of 168.41 g/L, representing a 14.3% improvement over conventional manual feeding control. Overall, this work establishes a scalable and physiology-driven nutrient control framework for microbial cell factories and elucidates the metabolic basis of phosphate-mediated regulation, providing a reference for optimizing other industrial fermentation processes.

works.title: Duplex qPCR for detection and discrimination of wild-type and persistent O foot-and-mouth disease virus
works.abstract: Abstract Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), predominantly caused by serotype O foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV), remains highly contagious and economically devastating worldwide. A significant challenge in disease control is that recovered or vaccinated animals can become asymptomatic carriers of persistent strains (Op), which are indistinguishable from acute wild-type (WT) strains using current diagnostic methods. In this study, we developed a duplex TaqMan real-time PCR assay based on comparative next-generation sequencing and genomic analysis of WT and persistent O FMDV strains. Conserved regions were identified for universal detection, and Op-specific single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) mutations were targeted for differential amplification using ARMS-PCR (amplification refractory mutation system PCR). The optimized assay, consisting of a co-detection channel and a typing channel, demonstrated excellent specificity with no cross-reactivity against host nucleic acids or unrelated cell lines, a detection limit of 5 copies/µL, and clear differentiation of WT from Op strains. Furthermore, the duplex assay successfully distinguished wild-type and persistent strains in infected cell samples and across different viral passages (PI30 and PI60). This duplex TaqMan RT-qPCR assay provides, for the first time, a sensitive, specific, and efficient tool for simultaneous detection and differentiation of wild-type and persistent O FMDV strains in infected cell samples and across viral passages. Although clinical validation remains to be performed, this assay offers a promising basis for further studies on FMD surveillance and the detection of viral persistence. Key points • First duplex TaqMan RT-qPCR assay differentiating wild-type and persistent O FMDV. • Detection limit of 5 copies/µL with no cross-reactivity against host nucleic acids. • Differentiates Op strains at passages 30 and 60, monitors persistence, aids control.

works.title: Functional Characterization and Application of Yarrowia lipolytica YlYxc1 for Enhanced Production of Sphingoid Bases
works.abstract: Long-chain bases (LCBs; sphingoid bases), derived from ceramide metabolism, are valuable sphingolipid intermediates for industrial applications. Here, we functionally characterized a putative ceramidase from Yarrowia lipolytica (YlYxc1) and evaluated its potential to enhance LCB production. YlYxc1 contains a conserved alkaline ceramidase motif with seven transmembrane helices and shares ~42% amino acid identity with Saccharomyces cerevisiae alkaline ceramidases ScYpc1 and ScYdc1. Despite lacking a canonical ER retention motif, YlYxc1 localized to the ER membrane. Deletion of YlYXC1 caused no major growth or lipid profile changes. Heterologous overexpression of YlYXC1 in S. cerevisiae wild-type and Scypc1Δydc1Δ strains increased phytosphingosine (PHS) production over dihydrosphingosine (DHS), mimicking ScYPC1 overexpression. In vitro activity assays using microsomal fractions from Scypc1Δydc1Δ cells expressing YlYXC1 revealed preferential hydrolysis of phytoceramide with an alkaline pH optimum. Furthermore, YlYXC1 expression in an engineered Y. lipolytica strain expressing heterologous acetyltransferases WcSLI1 and WcATF2 remarkably enhanced acetylated LCB production. Multi-copy integration of YlYXC1 into the Ylsur2Δsld1Δ strain also increased the secretory production of non-acetylated DHS. These findings establish YlYxc1 as a promising metabolic engineering target for producing value-added LCBs for pharmaceutical and cosmeceutical applications.

works.title: Issue Information
Enhanced violacein production by synthetically engineered mutualistic Escherichia coli co-culture biofilms in a spatially partitioned bioreactor system
works.abstract: Violacein (VIO) is a bacterial secondary metabolite with potential applications in healthcare, textile, and cosmetic industries. Although modular synthetic E. coli co-cultures are promising for biomanufacturing, VIO production in such systems depends on efficient cross-feeding, which requires spatial proximity and stable interactions among co-culture members. Here, we demonstrate that a spatially partitioned bioreactor can support coexisting suspended and carrier-associated states of a mutualistic recombinant E. coli co-culture, enabling direct comparison of their crude VIO production performance. The co-culture was cultivated in a spatially partitioned bioreactor consisting of an aerobic stirred-tank compartment connected to an oxygen-limited cartridge containing Fibra-Cel® discs as carriers, thereby enabling biomass partitioning into suspended and adherent fractions. Across three biological replicates, the adherent biofilm-associated fraction consistently exhibited higher biomass-normalized crude VIO production than the corresponding suspended fraction, with 4.51-, 20.05-, and 5.51-fold increases. Although the adherent fraction represented only 10.6-24.0% of the total biomass, it contributed 35.4-86.3% of the total crude VIO. These results show that carrier-associated spatial organization within the partitioned bioreactor supported the formation of highly productive biofilm-associated E. coli co-culture populations. The presented concept highlights the potential of spatially organized, carrier-associated co-cultures for the intensification of secondary metabolite production and future biofilm-based bioprocessing applications.

works.title: Morphology–Rheology Coupling Enables Predictive Optimization of Hirsutella sinensis Submerged Fermentation: A Case Study With Cross‐Strategy Predictive Modeling
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Hirsutella sinensis , the anamorph of Ophiocordyceps sinensis , is a valuable medicinal fungus, yet its industrial production is constrained by low fermentation efficiency and poorly controlled mycelial morphology. In this study, morphology engineering strategies based on inoculum volume and microparticle‐enhanced cultivation were systematically investigated to improve fermentation performance. Increasing inoculum volume (4%–10%, v/v) promoted a transition from dense (L‐type) to loose (S‐type) pellets, enhancing internal mass transfer and increasing biomass up to 18.7 g/L (compared to 11.1 g/L at 4% inoculum). Among the tested microparticles, talc exhibited the strongest effect, increasing biomass by 1.45‐fold compared to the control without microparticles and significantly enhancing adenosine and mannitol production. Microscopic and elemental analyses revealed that talc modifies pellet architecture via mechanical embedding and structural disruption, leading to increased internal porosity. Quantitative models linking morphology (S%, L%, density H) and rheology (Ln viscosity) to biomass achieved high predictive accuracy ( R 2 up to 0.92). Notably, a cross‐process model demonstrated that morphology descriptors can serve as predictive state variables across different engineering strategies. Scale‐up in a 5 L bioreactor further validated the approach, with a semi‐continuous process achieving 44.68 g/week productivity (compared to 25.93 g/week for batch fermentation, an 73% increase). This study establishes a morphology–rheology–performance framework for H. sinensis and provides a methodological insight applicable to other filamentous fermentation systems.

works.title: A hybrid metabolic graph neural networks based observer for metabolic modeling with sparse data
Particulate and spherical cellulosic supports derived from sugarcane bagasse for oriented immobilization of recombinant CBD-tagged enzymes
works.abstract: This study developed and evaluated particulate and spherical cellulosic supports derived from sugarcane bagasse for the oriented immobilization of recombinant enzymes containing a cellulose-binding domain (CBD), using β-galactosidase-CBD (β-Gal-CBD) as a model. The bagasse was subjected to alkaline hydrolysis (L) and sequential acid and alkaline hydrolysis (LH), resulting in supports with progressively higher cellulose contents, as confirmed by chemical analysis, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The LH treatment yielded the support with the highest cellulosic purity, leading to superior performance in immobilization (LH-Gal). At a loading of 10 U/g, the particulate LH support achieved a recovered activity exceeding 100%, characterizing enzymatic hyperactivation, which is a highly promising result for supports derived from agro-industrial residues. Among the spherical supports (Sph) obtained by ionic gelation of sodium alginate, LH-Sph exhibited the highest yield and recovered activity values, with optimal conditions at 3 h and 1 U/sphere. The alginate control support presented the lowest immobilization parameters, demonstrating that the presence of cellulosic bagasse is determinant for the oriented immobilization. The economic viability of an industrial process for low-lactose milk production employing the LH-Gal biocatalyst was demonstrated in all evaluated scenarios (5-40 reuse cycles of the biocatalyst), with an internal rate of return (IRR) of 42.8-73.1%, a return on investment (ROI) of 340-634%, and a discounted payback period of 1.65-2.98 years. These results demonstrate that particulate and spherical cellulosic supports derived from sugarcane bagasse hold strong potential for the oriented immobilization of CBD-tagged enzymes, with promising applications in industrial bioprocesses.

works.title: Sustainable and miniaturized electrochemical sensors for glyphosate and parabens: integrating biomass‐derived carbons, FDM fabrication, and portable instrumentation
works.abstract: Abstract Glyphosate and parabens are chemically distinct emerging contaminants whose field monitoring is constrained by complex matrices and by the cost and infrastructure requirements of conventional laboratory methods. This review evaluates whether biomass‐derived carbon materials, fused deposition modeling (FDM), and portable electrochemical instrumentation can be combined into a coherent platform for decentralized analysis of these analytes. The review is organized around the sensing chain rather than around broad surveys of electrochemistry or additive manufacturing: analyte‐recognition requirements; biomass‐derived electrode modifiers; FDM fabrication and activation; and low‐cost potentiostatic readout. Glyphosate and parabens are used as complementary model analytes to assess the platform's adaptability. Biomass‐derived porous carbons can provide surface area, functional groups, and routes for heteroatom or metal modification, while FDM can reduce device cost and sample volume and enable customized cells. However, commercial conductive filaments contain an insulating polymer and commonly require activation. Most importantly, the reviewed literature does not yet establish a mature class of FDM‐printed, biomass‐derived sensors validated specifically for both glyphosate and parabens. Existing evidence is distributed across carbon‐paste, screen‐printed, molecularly imprinted, and non‐target FDM studies. The strongest research opportunity is therefore not merely to miniaturize existing electrodes, but to co‐designanalyte‐selective biochar–polymer filaments, printed cell geometry, activation, and portable electronics. Validation in real matrices, reproducible manufacturing, lifecycle assessment, and comparison with reference methods are required before claims of field readiness are justified. © 2026 The Author(s). Journal of Chemical Technology and Biotechnology published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: Integrative Multi-Cohort Analysis of hsa-miR-1277, hsa-miR-301b, and hsa-miR-519a-1 Reveals Diagnostic Potential and Regulatory Associations in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a highly heterogeneous malignancy characterized by extensive molecular dysregulation, including aberrant microRNA (miRNA) expression. Identification of clinically relevant miRNAs and their associated regulatory networks may improve understanding of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) biology and facilitate biomarker discovery. OBJECTIVE: The present study aimed to identify novel dysregulated miRNAs associated with OSCC and to investigate their potential diagnostic relevance, predicted target interactions, and functional pathway associations through integrative transcriptomic and clinical validation analyses. METHODS: Mature miRNA expression profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-HNSCC cohort were retrieved through the UCSC Xena Browser and analyzed using DESeq2 following anatomical site-based filtering to obtain HPV-negative OSCC samples. Differentially expressed miRNAs were identified using adjusted p-value < 0.05 and |log2FoldChange|≥ 0.5 thresholds. Based on differential expression patterns and limited prior characterization in OSCC, hsa-miR-1277, hsa-miR-301b, and hsa-miR-519a-1 were selected for downstream analyses. Kaplan-Meier survival, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), integrative target prediction, Pearson correlation, STRING protein-protein interaction network, Gene Ontology (GO), and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses were subsequently performed. Independent validation was carried out using four Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) cohorts and qRT-PCR analysis in Indian OSCC clinical specimens. RESULTS: Differential expression analysis identified 283 significantly expressed miRNAs in OSCC, including 167 upregulated and 116 downregulated transcripts. ROC analysis demonstrated strong discriminatory performance for hsa-miR-301b (Area Under the Curve = 0.868) and moderate performance for hsa-miR-1277 (AUC = 0.735), whereas hsa-miR-519a-1 exhibited comparatively limited diagnostic utility. Integrative target prediction identified five high-confidence targets each for hsa-miR-1277 and hsa-miR-301b, while hsa-miR-519a-1 demonstrated a broader overlap profile comprising 24 candidate genes. Functional enrichment analyses demonstrated enrichment of neuronal signaling, synaptic regulation, ion channel activity, neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction, and cadherin-associated pathways among candidate target genes. Validation across independent GEO cohorts and clinical specimens demonstrated heterogeneous expression patterns with partial concordance to TCGA-derived observations. CONCLUSION: This integrative multi-cohort analysis identifies hsa-miR-1277, hsa-miR-301b, and hsa-miR-519a-1 as novel miRNA candidates associated with OSCC-related molecular dysregulation. The findings further highlight the substantial biological heterogeneity underlying HNSCC and emphasize the challenges associated with translating large-scale transcriptomic signatures into reproducible clinical biomarkers.

works.title: Mechanism of Action of Qingjin Huazhuo Formula in Treating Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Based on Proteomics, Traditional Chinese Medicine Component Analysis, and Network Pharmacology
Engineered Pseudomonas putida reconfigures metabolic fluxes during muconate bioproduction from lignin-related aromatics
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Muconic acid is a versatile platform chemical that can be biologically produced from lignocellulosic substrates, including from lignin-related aromatic compounds. Pseudomonas putida has been previously engineered to convert lignin-related aromatic compounds to muconate at quantitative molar yields. This high atom efficiency requires a supplemental carbon and energy source to support bacterial growth, and central carbon metabolic efficiency and its interaction with aromatic catabolism are underexplored. Here, we applied proteomics, metabolomics, and 13 C-fluxomics to quantitatively compare central carbon and energy metabolism in wild-type P. putida KT2440 and a muconate-producing strain, P. putida CJ781. During cultivation on glucose and 4-hydroxybenzoate, CJ781 showed increased glucose uptake, reconfigured central fluxes, and increased extracellular leakage of aliphatic acids relative to wild type. These altered fluxes supported a 3-fold higher intracellular ATP concentration and a model-predicted 2.5-fold increase in apparent ATP excess over anabolic demand. Pyruvate and acetate secretion in CJ781 was mitigated by debottlenecking TCA-cycle entry via citrate synthase overexpression. Furthermore, tuned expression of the catechol dioxygenase and protocatechuate decarboxylase enabled the production of 36.3 g L -1 muconate at 1.1 g L -1 h -1 . Overall, this work reveals how P. putida redirects carbon and energy fluxes to support aromatic bioconversion for improved bioproduction from renewable feedstocks.

works.title: Engineering of copper-binding probiotic for the treatment of copper poisoning in a drinking water-induced mouse model
works.abstract: Copper poisoning is a serious condition marked by multi‑organ toxicity, yet existing treatments suffer from limited efficacy and adverse effects, necessitating safer and more effective copper‑depletion approaches. In this study, we aimed to engineer a probiotic strain capable of sequestering intestinal copper and evaluate its therapeutic potential in a mouse model of copper poisoning. We engineered Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 to surface‑display various copper‑binding elements and identified the strain overexpressing Tff1 (EcN‑Tff1) as exhibiting the highest copper‑binding capacity. Oral administration of EcN‑Tff1 in a mouse model of copper poisoning, established by copper‑supplemented drinking water, significantly alleviated disease phenotypes, as evidenced by improved body weight, reduced hepatic inflammation, and attenuated liver pathology. EcN‑Tff1 treatment increased fecal copper excretion while decreasing copper accumulation in the liver and urine, indicating enhanced copper elimination via the intestinal route. 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing revealed that EcN‑Tff1 administration altered gut microbiota composition, including changes in the relative abundances of Ligilactobacillus , Eubacterium siraeum group , Coriobacteriaceae_UCG‑002 , and Faecalibaculum . Functional prediction using PICRUSt2 showed that the engineered strain modulated gut microbial metabolic pathways, with enrichment in pathways related to signal transduction, cofactor and vitamin metabolism, xenobiotic biodegradation, amino acid metabolism, and pathogen infection. Our study demonstrates that EcN‑Tff1 serves as an effective oral bioagent for reducing copper burden and provides a promising microbe‑based therapeutic strategy for copper overload disorders.

works.title: Rapid genome editing mediated by the NH-CR system in Yarrowia lipolytica and its applications
works.abstract: Yarrowia lipolytica is an important non-conventional yeast chassis for synthetic biology and metabolic engineering because of its robust lipid metabolism, protein secretion capacity, and industrial application potential. However, genome engineering in this species remains constrained by its strong non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) activity, which limits the efficiency of conventional homologous recombination-based editing strategies and makes iterative strain construction laborious. Although NHEJ can be exploited for homology-independent DNA integration, its random nature and the limited availability of recyclable selectable markers restrict its broader use in multi-round engineering. In this study, we developed the NH-CR system, a CRISPR/Cas9-assisted genome engineering workflow that couples NHEJ-mediated random DNA integration with delayed CRISPR/Cas9-mediated functional inactivation of the selectable marker in Y. lipolytica. The pYl-CRISPR platform enabled rapid target gene knockout within 3 days, with a gene-disruption efficiency exceeding 95%, and further supported random genomic integration of exogenous DNA fragments. To improve its applicability for iterative integration, Cas9 expression was tuned by promoter truncation, which balanced cotransformation efficiency and selectable-marker disruption efficiency. The optimized pYl-CRISPR-Δ75 system increased cotransformation efficiency to approximately 50 CFU/μg DNA while maintaining a 3-day selectable-marker disruption efficiency of approximately 75% after subculturing. The utility of NH-CR was further demonstrated in two metabolic engineering applications. Reinforcement of the native 2-phenylethanol biosynthetic pathway increased 2-phenylethanol production from 1 g/L in the wild-type strain to 2.5 g/L. In addition, iterative integration of heterologous sclareol biosynthetic genes and reinforcement of the endogenous MVA pathway enabled de novo sclareol production, reaching approximately 11 mg/L after 72 h of shake-flask fermentation. The NH-CR system provides a rapid and tunable workflow for iterative genome engineering in Y. lipolytica. By coupling rapid gene disruption and NHEJ-mediated random integration with delayed functional marker inactivation and reuse, the system reduces the operational burden of multi-round strain construction. NH-CR is particularly suited to rapid pathway assembly and phenotype-based screening when precise insertion-site or copy-number control is not required.

works.title: Distinction between Listeria species and L. monocytogenes serotypes with a handheld, VNIR hyperspectral imaging camera
works.abstract: Abstract A handheld, visible near-infrared (VNIR) hyperspectral imaging (HSI) camera was used to differentiate between Listeria species ( L. monocytogenes , L. ivanovii and L. innocua ) and two L. monocytogenes serotypes: 1/2a and 4b. The results indicated that portable HSI cameras could effectively be used for pathogen detection and distinction applications, despite lower spectral resolution and higher sensitivity to noise when compared to benchtop CCD-based instruments. Five hundred and fifty-five hyperspectral images were collected from pure cultures on agar plates throughout seven sampling campaigns. Sixty-five percent of samples/isolates ( n =± 90 samples per class) were used to train Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA) models and 35% of samples ( n =± 50 samples per class) were used for validation. An overall classification accuracy (validation) of 74.5% was achieved for species-level discrimination through a four-class model ( L. monocytogenes 1/2a, L. monocytogenes 4b, L. ivanovii and L. innocua ), which demonstrates moderate performance within the VNIR range. However, Species-level performance was uneven across classes, with lower validation accuracies for L. innocua (68.0%) and L. ivanovii (63.0%) compared to L. monocytogenes 1/2a (71.8%) and 4b (95.2%). In contrast, a two-class model achieved ~ 90% accuracy for serotype-level discrimination between L. monocytogenes serotypes 1/2a and 4b. This highlights a novel use of portable VNIR cameras as a rapid, non-destructive serotyping aid. Variable Importance in Projection (VIP) score plots were used to characterise valuable wavelengths in the visible range that were significant for discriminant analysis, for example, 690 nm was significant for the classification of L. innocua , whilst 871 nm was associated with L. ivanovii. Notably, all the significant absorption regions used to differentiate between the L. monocytogenes serotypes were in the visible range (480–525 nm, 540–560 nm, 610 nm and 690 nm) despite the colony morphology being virtually identical for these organisms on brain heart infusion agar. Key points • A portable HSI camera was used to distinguish between Listeria colonies on agar • PLS-DA accuracy of 74.5% was obtained for classification between Listeria species • PLS-DA accuracy of 90% obtained for classification between L. monocytogenes serotypes

works.title: Dimyristoylphosphatidylcholine vesicle treatment enhances the storage stability and culturability of Lactococcus lactis suspensions
works.abstract: Abstract Maintaining bacterial culturability during storage is important for microbial biotechnology. This study evaluated dimyristoylphosphatidylcholine (DMPC) liposomes as a treatment for Lactococcus lactis suspensions stored for 28 days at 4 °C and room temperature. Liposomes were formed by thin-film hydration in the presence of bacterial cells. Cryogenic scanning electron microscopy (cryo-SEM) revealed approximately 100–160 nm vesicular structures in the DMPC-only sample and similar nanostructures near cells in treated suspensions, without establishing a continuous coating. On day 28 at 4 °C, treated and untreated suspensions had apparent zeta potentials of −17.31 and −1.56 mV, respectively. Across storage conditions and sampling times, polydispersity indices were 0.34–0.42 for treated suspensions versus 0.46–0.87 for controls, indicating lower apparent size heterogeneity. At room temperature on day 1, turbidity, expressed as optical density at 600 nm, was 0.99 versus 0.43, respectively. Metabolic activity assessed by 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)− 2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) reduction reached 2.50 versus 0.93 MTT-reducing units under the same conditions and subsequently declined, reaching 0.35 units in treated suspensions on day 14. Culturability was higher in treated suspensions from day 7 onward at both temperatures. On day 28 at room temperature, treated and untreated samples contained 2.55 × 10 5 and 3.83 × 10 1 CFU · mL −1 , respectively. DMPC liposome treatment thus supported retention of culturability during storage, with a larger relative benefit at room temperature, although the underlying vesicle-cell interactions remain unresolved. Key points • DMPC liposome treatment was associated with lower PDI in L. lactis suspensions. • DMPC treatment preserved L. lactis culturability during prolonged storage. • The protective effect of DMPC was strongest during room-temperature storage.

works.title: Acid‐activated water hyacinth ( Eichhornia crassipes ) from the Nile River for textile wastewater reclamation: A comparative evaluation of anionic and cationic dye adsorption
works.abstract: Abstract Water hyacinth ( Eichhornia crassipes ) is an extremely invasive aquatic plant with notable environmental and socioeconomic impacts; however, its unique physicochemical properties offer potential for wastewater treatment through adsorption. This study investigates the acid activation of water hyacinth using acetic, sulphuric, hydrochloric, and nitric acids to enhance its performance as an adsorbent for dye removal. The aquatic plant was harvested from the Nile River, processed, and activated with each acid, and a comparative evaluation was performed. Adsorption efficiency was assessed using Methylene Blue (cationic) and Ponceau S (anionic) dyes, with removal percentage determined by spectrophotometric analysis before and after treatment. Sulphuric acid activation produced the highest adsorption capacity, achieving 94.5% removal for Ponceau S and 98.7% for Methylene Blue, attributed to improved surface area and pore structure. Response surface methodology was applied to model the effects of adsorbent dosage, contact time, and dye concentration while maximising adsorption capacity. The adsorption data were fitted to the Langmuir, Freundlich, and Dubinin–Radushkevich isotherms, and adsorption kinetics were evaluated. Sulfonated water hyacinth showed strong conformity with the Langmuir isotherm ( R 2 = 0.99, q m = 4.275 mg g −1 ) and the Dubinin–Radushkevich model ( R 2 = 0.844, Q D = 5.09 mg g −1 ), indicating monolayer adsorption and reliable model fit. Kinetic modelling followed the pseudo‐second‐order model, suggesting that chemisorption was the dominant mechanism. Overall, the study demonstrates the high potential of water hyacinth‐derived adsorbents as sustainable materials for wastewater treatment.

works.title: Bioengineering strategies for prenatal therapy
A Modular Micro‐Chemostat System for High‐Throughput Continuous Cultivations
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Improving the fidelity of computational eukaryotic models will require an enormous amount of high quality and reproducible data from biological experiments. In this study we present and demonstrate a modular 12‐channel micro‐chemostat system. This micro‐chemostat is designed for use by Genesis, a Robot Scientist developed to automate scientific research in yeast systems biology. We performed bioreactor characterization experiments to evaluate the performance of the micro‐chemostat system. We also cultivated the Saccharomyces cerevisiae reference strain, BY4741, at three different dilution rates (0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 h −1 ) and under two aeration conditions (microaerobic and aerobic), resulting in six different conditions. The bioreactor performance fulfilled our requirements, and enabled substrate‐limited continuous cultivation of yeast. Furthermore, the empirical results from the biological experiments were consistent with the literature, suggesting that results obtained from our system are comparable to those reported for other platforms in the field. Based on the evidence presented in this study, we conclude that the 12‐channel micro‐chemostat system is a suitable platform for yeast systems biology research. The modular design of the micro‐chemostat system enables future scaling to hundreds or thousands of concurrent chemostats and facilitates integration with autonomous agents for automated optimization and improvement of eukaryotic model systems.

works.title: Auto-aggregation characteristics and EPS interface-driven mechanisms of a novel salt-tolerant nitrate-reducing bacterium Thauera sp. Z-1
Chloroidium sp. and Tetradesmus obliquus biomass for plant biostimulants: Extraction, characterization and bioactivity on seeds development
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Microalgal biomass has emerged as a promising feedstock for producing sustainable plant biostimulants (PBs), particularly when cultivating microalgae using residual nutrients and CO 2 sources. This study focuses on the extraction of PBs from Chloroidium sp. and Tetradesmus obliquus microalgae cultivated in anaerobic digestion liquid digestate and their impact on seeds development. Alcalase enzymes-assisted extraction at 50 °C emerged as the most efficient method, achieving protein extraction yields of 47.78 ± 1.94% (equivalent to 16.0 ± 0.6% of the biomass dry weight) for Chloroidium sp., and 16.24 ± 1.13% (equivalent to 8.1 ± 0.6% of the biomass dry weigh) for T. obliquus . The influence of protein or peptide size on the potential of the PBs was evaluated using three fractions of the extracts: < 3 kDa, 3-100 kDa, and >100 kDa. Optimized extracts were evaluated on mustard and wheat seeds, revealing a dose-dependent relationship between the potential of the PBs and their molecular sizes. Interestingly, the biostimulant activity of T. obliquus extracts on mustard was attributed to the medium-sized fraction. In contrast, Chloroidium sp. extracts required a synergistic interaction between different molecular sizes to enhance root growth across both seed species. This study reveals species-dependent biological activity of microalgae-based PBs.

works.title: Continuous low‑voltage electrostatic field during frozen storage maintains beef quality by inhibiting ice recrystallization and oxidative deterioration
Efficient continuous lipase-catalyzed oxyfunctionalization of α-pinene in Pickering emulsions: Evaluating performance in water and glyceline-based systems
works.abstract: Pickering emulsions (PEs) have emerged as promising media for multiphasic biocatalysis due to their large interfacial area, droplet stability, and ability to provide protective microenvironments for enzymes. Considering the need to replace conventional oxyfunctionalization processes that rely on harsh reaction conditions, while overcoming challenges such as enzyme deactivation and low specific reaction rates in green alternatives, this work systematically investigates, for the first time, the influence of key operating conditions on continuous lipase-mediated oxyfunctionalization of α-pinene in glyceline-based PEs in comparison with conventional water-based PEs. Glyceline-based PEs maintained reaction performance up to 40 °C, whereas the reaction rate in water-based PEs decreased by 38% when the temperature was increased from 30 to 40 °C. While longer residence times reduced reaction performance in water-based PEs, possibly due to increased α-pinene oxide (PO) hydrolysis, glyceline-based systems maintained high selectivity and achieved increasing H 2 O 2 -based yields. At comparable α-pinene:H 2 O 2 molar ratios of 8.7 for the glyceline-based PE and 8.8 for the water-based PE, the specific reaction rate in the glyceline-based PE was 2.8-fold higher under the respective formulation conditions. Under optimal conditions at 197 mM H 2 O 2 , glyceline-based PEs achieved an H 2 O 2 -based yield of 93% and a space–time yield of 146 g PO ·L -1 ·d -1 . At 295 mM H 2 O 2 , the specific reaction rate in the glyceline-based PE was 37.79 mmol·h -1 ·g -1 , more than five times that of the water-based PE under the respective formulation conditions. These results highlight the potential of PEs for intensified continuous lipase-mediated oxyfunctionalization processes.

works.title: Bioleaching of lithium from lithium refinery residue using A. thiooxidans, A. ferrooxidans, and a mixed culture of the two species
Alginate/pineapple waste composite beads for laccase immobilization: Optimization and characterization
Limits of Knallgas bacteria for autotrophic CO₂ conversion: physiology, H₂ kinetics and reactor constraints
works.abstract: Aerobic hydrogen-oxidizing bacteria, commonly referred to as Knallgas bacteria, are chemoautotrophic microorganisms that oxidize molecular hydrogen (H₂) while fixing carbon dioxide (CO₂) into cellular material. Historically studied as model systems for lithoautotrophic metabolism, these organisms have regained attention due to their potential for renewable H₂ utilization, land-independent biomass production, and electrochemically coupled CO₂ conversion. Among them, Cupriavidus necator has emerged as a promising industrial platform, while thermophilic and high-affinity H₂-oxidizers such as Kyrpidia spormannii are increasingly explored in bioelectrochemical systems. Despite growing interest, substantial gaps remain between laboratory demonstrations and scalable industrial performance. This review analyzes the physiological characteristics of Knallgas bacteria, including growth kinetics and H₂ oxidation parameters, and evaluates their translation into gas fermentation and oxic microbial electrosynthesis systems. Particular emphasis is placed on key engineering limitations, including H₂ mass transfer, electron partitioning during aerobic metabolism, reactor safety constraints, and electrochemical surface scaling.

works.title: Synergistic effects of fibrolytic enzymes and lactic acid bacteria on cassava leaf silage quality and microbial community
works.abstract: Cassava leaves are a valuable protein-rich feed resource, but their high fiber content and poor fermentation characteristics can reduce silage quality. To address these challenges, this study evaluated the synergistic effects of fiber-degrading enzymes and lactic acid bacteria (LAB) on the fermentation profiles, nutritional quality, and microbial community of cassava leaf silage. Silage was prepared using five treatments: CK (2% glucose), T1 (Lactobacillus plantarum + 2% glucose), T2 (glucanase + L. plantarum + 2% glucose), T3 (cellulase + L. plantarum + 2% glucose), and T4 (glucanase + cellulase + L. plantarum + 2% glucose), and ensiled for 0, 21, and 42 days. The findings demonstrated that additive treatments (T1-T4) rapidly decreased silage pH and increased lactic acid compared to the CK (P < 0.001). By day 42, the enzyme-inoculated groups (T2-T4) exhibited elevated crude protein alongside reduced fiber fractions compared to both CK and T1 (P < 0.001). Regarding the microbial community, Shannon and Simpson indices were lower in treated groups than in the CK group (P < 0.05). Beta diversity analysis revealed that the microbial community structure of the CK differed clearly from that of the additive-treated silages. At the phylum level, Bacillota dominated all other groups on day 42, with a relative abundance exceeding 92%. At the species level, Lactobacillus plantarum dominated enzyme-treated silages (relative abundance > 93%, P = 0.036), compared to only 13.1% in CK, which contained higher proportions of Pediococcus and Weissella species. Collectively, the synergistic application of fibrolytic enzymes and LAB improves cassava leaf silage quality by accelerating acidification, reducing fiber fractions, and establishing a highly favorable L. plantarum-dominated microbial community.

works.title: Engineering a Streptomyces albidoflavus cell factory for heterologous biosynthesis of tsukubarubicin
works.abstract: Abstract Background Tsukubarubicin is a nogalamycin-type anthracycline antibiotic with potent cytotoxic activity against human breast cancer cells, making it a promising antitumor candidate. However, its native producer produces only trace amounts of tsukubarubicin and is slow-growing and genetically intractable, limiting further pharmacological evaluation and potential application. To overcome this bottleneck, we developed a multi-layered engineering strategy to improve tsukubarubicin production. Results The complete tsukubarubicin biosynthetic gene cluster ( tsu -BGC) was initially isolated from a PAC library, followed by vector backbone replacement and insertion of an integration module using Red/ET recombineering. The engineered tsu -BGC was introduced into the heterologous host Streptomyces albidoflavus Del14 by conjugation, generating the initial strain D1401. To optimize pathway-specific regulation, the role of the regulatory gene tsuR1 was investigated by gene deletion and overexpression using promoters of different strengths. In situ replacement of the native tsuR1 promoter with the P21 promoter subsequently increased tsukubarubicin production from 3.9 to 37.8 mg/L. Electron beam irradiation mutagenesis was subsequently employed to further improve production, and transcriptomic analysis of the resulting high-producing mutant revealed metabolic changes associated with enhanced tsukubarubicin biosynthesis. Guided by these findings, candidate metabolic pathways were rationally engineered, further improving tsukubarubicin production. The final engineered strain D1404-1 produced 153.0 mg/L tsukubarubicin, representing a 39-fold increase over D1401. Conclusions This study establishes an efficient heterologous production platform for tsukubarubicin and substantially alleviates the supply limitation associated with its native producer. The combination of regulatory engineering, mutagenesis, and rational metabolic optimization provides an effective strategy for improving the production of tsukubarubicin, which provides a valuable foundation for pharmacological evaluation. Furthermore, this multi-level engineering paradigm offers a versatile reference for the heterologous overproduction of other actinomycete-derived polyketide natural products.

works.title: Sequence-diversity-guided discovery, model-guided mutagenesis, and secretory production of GH5 endoglucanases in Bacillus subtilis
works.abstract: Cellulases are central to lignocellulose deconstruction, but identifying additional glycoside hydrolase family 5 (GH5) enzymes remains slow. Deep-learning predictors have proliferated, yet few studies carry their predictions through experimental validation and testing in a production host. A 23-gene panel was assembled by CatPred-based selection from clustered UniProt sequences (25,148 initial entries) and EglS-seeded homology-search results, supplemented by two comparative routes. Twenty-two candidates were assayed on carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) after expression in Escherichia coli , with EglS as a separate control. AQSP_CL and MACA_CL, for which we found no prior biochemical characterisation, were purified alongside EglS and the thermophilic benchmark Cel5A. Both new enzymes had short-assay optima of 70 °C. AQSP_CL was most active at pH 5.0 and gave an apparent mass-based CMC kinetic-efficiency estimate close to EglS (0.201 versus 0.231 U·mL·mg⁻2); Cel5A was more thermostable. CatPred cellotetraose predictions showed no detected correlation with lysate CMC activity in eight assayed candidates with reconciled identities ( ρ = 0.10, p = 0.82). AQSP_CL had the highest fraction of poses meeting the operational distance criterion in ensemble docking (52.0% versus 28.7–39.0%), although the differences were not resolved at the conformer level and Vina scores did not distinguish the enzymes. In first-round screening, M65Q had the highest measured lysate activity among single substitutions (1.61-fold wild type). A few-shot model trained on first-round data nominated the second-round library, but additive predictions did not generalise to combinations. Signal peptide SP3 increased extracellular activity of parental AQSP_CL in Bacillus subtilis approximately eightfold over the signal-peptide-free construct. The study links discovery of two GH5 endoglucanases to experimental assessment of computational nominations, lead-enzyme development and extracellular production. AQSP_CL provides a new scaffold for further biomass-deconstruction research. The CMC and flask-scale measurements establish enzyme properties and extracellular recovery; biomass-conversion performance remains to be evaluated.

works.title: Targeted flavour development in chocolate: omics-driven insights into cocoa fermentation
works.abstract: Cocoa fermentation is the critical microbially driven process that transforms the genetic potential of cocoa beans into the complex flavour precursors essential for high-quality chocolate. Despite its importance, fermentation remains highly variable and poorly controlled, representing a major bottleneck in the production of premium chocolate. This review explores how advanced multi-omics approaches are improving our understanding of cocoa fermentation and flavour formation by linking microbial ecology, metabolite production and sensory outcomes. It highlights the transition of cocoa fermentation from a traditional practice towards a predictive, controllable biotechnological process. Such advances pave the way for the development of tailored starter cultures, optimised fermentation processes, and ultimately, consistent production of targeted flavour development in chocolates with enhanced quality and market value.

works.title: Comparative Modeling of Integrated Fixed‐Film Activated Sludge Membrane Bioreactor and Aerobic Membrane Bioreactor Systems: Nitrogen Dynamics and Energy Demand
works.abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a process‐oriented modeling assessment of a membrane bioreactor (MBR) and a hybrid integrated fixed‐film activated sludge membrane bioreactor (IFAS‐MBR) system using experimental data collected from parallel pilot‐scale systems, with emphasis on performance‐energy trade‐offs relevant to engineering design and operation. Both configurations were calibrated and validated under dynamic conditions to evaluate carbon removal, nitrogen transformation, and operational energy demand. Model results showed high predictive accuracy for mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSS) (mean relative absolute error, MRAE < 5%) and moderate accuracy for soluble chemical oxygen demand (sCOD) (MRAE: 11%–17%), while particulate COD (xCOD) predictions were governed primarily by membrane separation rather than biological kinetics. Nitrogen modeling revealed moderate agreement for ammonium nitrogen (NH 4 ‐N) (MRAE: 24%–36%), whereas nitrate nitrogen (NO 3 ‐N) predictions showed high accuracy, particularly in the IFAS‐MBR system (MRAE: 7%–14%). This improvement was achieved by calibrating oxygen diffusion within the biofilm, demonstrating that oxygen transport processes can dominate nitrogen transformation under non‐limiting bulk oxygen conditions. The IFAS‐MBR configuration increased total energy demand by approximately 27%, mainly due to intensified aeration requirements. These findings highlight the critical role of aeration in simultaneously governing process performance and energy demand.

works.title: In-situ Raman spectroscopy for real-time monitoring of cell density and metabolites during adenovirus production in HEK293 suspension culture
works.abstract: Adenoviral (AdV) vectors are widely used in human and veterinary vaccines as well as in gene and cancer therapies; however, their manufacturing remains challenging due to the complexity of real‑time process monitoring and control arising from the dual phase nature of production, lytic production cycle, and the cell density effect. In this study, in-situ Raman spectroscopy was evaluated as a process analytical technology (PAT) for real-time monitoring of cell density and metabolites during AdV production in suspension HEK293 cells. Raman spectra were acquired every 30 min in six 3 L bioreactor runs, and partial least squares (PLS) models were developed to monitor viable and total cell densities as well as key metabolites, including glucose, lactate, glutamine, ammonium, and glutamate, across both the growth and infection phases using a global model. The performance was estimated by nested leave-one-batch-out validation, in which each batch was predicted by a model whose spectral preprocessing, spectral range and number of latent variables were selected using the other five batches only. Pooled root mean square errors of prediction over the six held-out batches were 0.63 and 0.44 × 10 6 cells/mL for viable and total cell density (R P 2 = 0.80 and 0.94) and 1.18, 2.11, 0.65 and 0.39 mM for glucose, lactate, glutamine and ammonium (R P 2 = 0.99, 0.98, 0.86 and 0.83), and feeding and dilution events were reproduced in the continuous predictions. Glutamate was not predicted reliably (R P 2 = −0.37), and no usable viral-titre model could be established. Compared with a common full-range model, target-specific selection of the normalisation reference and spectral range lowered the pooled prediction error for the cell densities, glucose and lactate, but not for glutamine, ammonium or glutamate, and the Raman shifts selected consistently across folds helped to interpret the models. Overall, the work demonstrates the feasibility of in-situ Raman spectroscopy for monitoring cell density and major metabolites in both phases of adenovirus production and supports its integration into advanced monitoring and process optimization strategies.

works.title: Experimental assessment of sugar losses and energy cost during acid-catalyzed pretreatment of sugarcane bagasse at low solids loading
Proofing the concept of a segmented biophotovoltaic process to produce electricity from marine cyanobacteria: an indoor and outdoor approach
works.abstract: Abstract This study presents an innovative biophotovoltaic (BPV) process with three components: a cyanobacteria reservoir that serves as the biological engine; an electron-capture reactor that redirects transmembrane electrons; and a radiation-harvesting tower designed to maximize energy input and enhance system scalability. For the indoor (LED) and outdoor (solar radiation) tests, the most suitable resistances to yield the maximum current density were 164 Ω and 220 Ω, respectively. Indoor electricity generation peaked at 227 mW m − 2 , with an average of 175 ± 47 mW m − 2 , while outdoor tests peaked at 215 mW m − 2 , with an average of 166 ± 26 mW m − 2 , indicating similar efficiency under both conditions. To explain these efficiencies, the 5% loss in performance is most likely related to the increase in temperature from 20 °C to 32 °C and the resistivity of electrode materials. To confirm this, complementary experiments (in triplicate) demonstrated that an increase in incubator temperature to 32 °C also resulted in lower electricity generation (125 ± 25 mW m − 2 ). The heat conduction to the cyanobacteria medium led to harsher environmental conditions for Synechocystis pevalekii , and the increased resistivity caused voltage drops. Overall, the proof of concept of our BPV process demonstrated that it is technically possible to run in the system in an external laboratory environment using the segmentation approach and the radiation-harvesting tower.

works.title: Absorption of nitrogen oxides by ionic liquids: a mini review
works.abstract: Abstract Nitrous oxide (N 2 O) is a potent greenhouse gas, whereas nitrogen oxides (NOx) are major atmospheric pollutants. Owing to their significant environmental impacts, ionic liquids (ILs) have attracted considerable attention as highly tunable absorbents for nitrogen oxide capture and separation. This mini‐review summarizes recent advances in the absorption of N 2 O, nitric oxide (NO), and nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) by ILs, with emphasis on absorption performance, molecular interaction mechanisms, and structure–property relationships. Mechanistically, N 2 O absorption is primarily governed by anion–N 2 O electrostatic interactions, whereas weakened cation–anion interactions enhance N 2 O solubility. In contrast, NO capture relies predominantly on chemical absorption, while NO 2 exhibits significantly higher physical solubility than NO, suggesting that catalytic oxidation of NO prior to absorption represents a potential strategy. Recent advances in amino‐functionalized ILs and transition metal‐assisted systems have substantially improved NO capture through chemical interactions. Current challenges and future perspectives are also highlighted to facilitate the rational design of task‐specific IL‐based absorbents for industrial gas purification. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: Iron‐modified natural sand as a heterogeneous Fenton catalyst for methylene blue and textile wastewater treatment
works.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND The continuous discharge of organic dyes into freshwater poses long‐term environmental risks. Heterogeneous Fenton‐like processes using iron (Fe)‐modified silica (SiO 2 ) supports are promising for dye removal; however, catalysts derived from natural sand and operating under near‐neutral conditions remain relatively underexplored. This study investigates Fe‐modified Tunisian natural sand (Si‐Fe) as a potentially low‐cost catalyst for methylene blue (MB) removal and textile wastewater treatment. RESULTS The Fenton‐like process was optimized using response surface methodology based on a four‐factor Box–Behnken design. The optimal conditions were initial MB concentration 5 mg L −1 , Si–Fe dose 0.745 g L −1 , pH 7.9 and H 2 O 2 dose 5 mL L −1 , yielding a predicted MB removal efficiency of 95.31%. The catalyst maintained a removal efficiency >83% over five reuse cycles. In real textile wastewater treatment, the process achieved >99% color removal, ≈70% COD reduction and >84% turbidity reduction. CONCLUSION The results demonstrate the potential of Si–Fe, prepared from naturally abundant Tunisian sand, as a durable and potentially low‐cost heterogeneous Fenton‐like catalyst for MB removal and textile wastewater treatment, including under near‐neutral conditions. © 2026 The Author(s). Journal of Chemical Technology and Biotechnology published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: Deep eutectic solvent-based green extraction of prodigiosin: Process optimization, mechanism and bioactivity evaluation
Upstream challenges in the scaling of plastics chemical recycling
works.abstract: Recent advances in chemical recycling have moved innovative pathways from laboratory research toward commercial deployment. However, upstream challenges, including feedstock collection, preprocessing, contaminant removal, and solids handling, remain underappreciated despite major impacts on cost, reliability, and scalability. In this review, we highlight key upstream challenges in feedstock acquisition, quality, and transport that may limit the growth of chemical recycling technologies. Using flexible film packaging, textiles, and electronic waste as case studies, we show how feedstock-specific logistics and pretreatment requirements influence process operability. We also highlight key considerations for heterogeneous solids processing. We argue that achieving cost competitiveness with virgin production will require innovations beyond deconstruction chemistry, including modular process architectures, distributed preprocessing strategies, and reactor systems designed to accommodate variable and contaminated solid feedstocks.

works.title: Base editing-mediated exon-specific knockout of glutamine synthetase generates a high-productivity CHO cell line for antibody manufacturing
works.abstract: The Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell platform dominates recombinant protein production, with the glutamine synthetase (GS) system widely used for clonal selection. However, we observed variable performance between two commercial CHO lines (ATCC CHO-K1 and CHOZN ® ), which carry distinct intragenic GS deletions and differential residual transcript levels, raising the possibility that the premature termination codon (PTC) position contributes to this phenotypic divergence. To systematically assess the impact of the PTC position, we used base editing to introduce PTCs into each of the six coding exons of Glul . Among the resulting clonal lines, the exon 7-edited (E7) variant exhibited complete GS ablation and sustained high viability. In fed-batch production of an anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody, E7 achieved higher titers and specific productivities than CHOZN ® , with sustained viability. Our findings demonstrate that PTC location is a key determinant of GS knockout completeness and cellular phenotype, identifying exon 7 as a critical knockout target that offers a defined, exon-resolved strategy for accelerating CHO cell line development and improving recombinant protein titers.

works.title: Enhanced brevicidine production in Brevibacillus laterosporus by integrated fermentation and ARTP mutagenesis: mechanistic insights into the high‑yield phenotype
works.abstract: Brevicidine is a promising non-ribosomal antimicrobial peptide with potent activity against Gram-negative pathogens, but its practical development is limited by low natural productivity and insufficient understanding of the physiological basis underlying high-yield phenotypes. In this study, an integrated strategy combining fermentation optimization, atmospheric and room-temperature plasma mutagenesis, and mechanistic analysis was established to improve brevicidine production in Brevibacillus laterosporus 811. Single-factor optimization increased the brevicidine titer to 257.32 mg/L, and subsequent Plackett–Burman and Box–Behnken designs further improved production to 326.05 mg/L. A temperature-shift strategy combined with Tween-80 supplementation further increased the titer to 605.1 mg/L in shake-flask fermentation. In parallel, mutagenesis generated a stable high-yield mutant designated as T3, which showed a 26.6% increase in production relative to the wild type. Comparative genomics identified a cis-regulatory mutation located 75 bp upstream of spoVB . Transcriptomic, quantitative reverse-transcription PCR, and transmission electron microscopy analysis consistently showed that downregulation of spoVB in the mutant was associated with impaired spore cortex formation, indicating attenuation of sporulation-related development. Fed-batch fermentation in a 5 L bioreactor, combined with temperature shifting, low-residual-sugar feeding, and pH regulation, further increased brevicidine production to 820 mg/L. This study established an integrated route for improving brevicidine production at both the process and strain levels and provided mechanistic evidence linking suppression of sporulation-related development to the high-yield phenotype. These findings not only strengthen the production basis of brevicidine, but also provide a useful framework for the development and optimization of other non-ribosomal antimicrobial peptides.

works.title: Valorization of non-recyclable polypropylene manufacturing waste via catalytic co-hydrothermal liquefaction with biomass using industrial alumina–silica waste as a heterogeneous catalyst
works.abstract: Non-recyclable polypropylene (PP) manufacturing waste and lignocellulosic/algal biomass residues represent two underutilized waste streams that are commonly disposed of by landfill or incineration. This study investigated the co-hydrothermal liquefaction (co-HTL) of sawdust, rice straw, and Chlorella with non-recyclable PP manufacturing waste under subcritical water conditions (350 °C), using industrial alumina–silica waste recovered from liquid nitrogen processing as a low-cost heterogeneous catalyst. The catalyst was characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), FTIR spectroscopy, and N 2 physisorption. Product distribution, elemental composition, higher heating value (HHV), Van Krevelen analysis, and FTIR spectroscopy were evaluated to determine the influence of catalyst addition on product quality. A screening-level environmental assessment was also performed to compare the estimated embodied carbon footprint of the waste-derived catalyst with reported values for synthetic and bio-derived zeolite catalysts. Catalyst addition increased the maximum bio-crude yield to 47.2 wt.% for the Chlorella–PP blend, while reducing the solid residue from 46.7 wt.% to 37.3 wt.%. The catalyst was mesoporous, with a BET surface area of 226.6 m 2 g −1 and an average pore diameter of 5.3 nm. Co-processing with PP substantially improved fuel characteristics, with the highest HHV reaching 32.95 MJ kg⁻ 1 and the O/C atomic ratio decreasing from 0.43 to 0.19, indicating enhanced deoxygenation and improved energy density.
