FTIR and Van Krevelen analyses were consistent with increased hydrocarbon formation and reduced oxygenated functional groups following catalytic treatment. The observed improvements are proposed to arise from catalyst-assisted cracking of polypropylene together with enhanced interactions between PP-derived hydrocarbons and biomass-derived intermediates during co-liquefaction. The waste-derived catalyst exhibited an estimated embodied carbon footprint of approximately 0.13 kg CO₂-eq kg⁻ 1 , which is substantially lower than values reported for conventional synthetic and bio-derived zeolite catalysts. These results demonstrate that industrial alumina–silica waste can serve as an effective low-cost heterogeneous catalyst for upgrading bio-crude during co-hydrothermal liquefaction, while simultaneously valorizing two problematic industrial waste streams. Further investigation of catalyst stability, aqueous-phase composition, long-term catalyst reusability, and comprehensive life cycle and techno-economic assessment is required before scale-up.

works.title: Nitrogen ion beam mutagenesis improves sophorolipid production and properties in Starmerella bombicola
works.abstract: Abstract Sophorolipids (SLs) are microbial biosurfactants with broad industrial potential, but their large-scale application relies on robust high-producing strains with desirable functional properties. In this study, Starmerella bombicola CGMCC 1576 was subjected to nitrogen (N+) ion beam mutagenesis to improve SL production and product performance. A mutant library containing 124 isolates was constructed, and two stable high-producing mutants, 2–21 and 3–5, were obtained through high-throughput screening and shake-flask validation. Mutant 2–21 preferentially accumulated acidic sophorolipids (ASL) and showed the highest total sophorolipid (TSL) production, whereas mutant 3–5 produced more lactonic sophorolipids (LSL). HPLC profiling showed that the mutants retained the major SL components of the parental strain but differed markedly in component abundance and product distribution. Transcriptional analysis revealed upregulation of genes associated with fatty acid utilization, SL biosynthesis and metabolite transport, particularly in mutant 2–21 at 96 h, suggesting enhanced precursor conversion and product accumulation. Functional assays further showed composition-dependent differences in surface activity and mildness. LSL-rich fractions exhibited stronger surface activity, while ASL-rich fractions showed lower zein solubilization and hemolytic activity. In 100-L bioreactor fermentation, mutant 2–21 produced 224.31 g/L TSL, confirming its scalability and production robustness. These results demonstrate that N+ ion beam mutagenesis is an effective strategy for developing high-producing S. bombicola strains and tailoring SL composition for functional applications. Key points Nitrogen ion beam mutagenesis improved SL production in S. bombicola.ASL-rich and LSL-rich mutants showed distinct SL profiles.Mutant 2–21 produced 224.31 g/L TSL in a 100-L bioreactor.

works.title: Identification and functional characterization of RepE variants that increase plasmid copy number
works.abstract: Abstract Replication of low-copy-number iteron plasmids is tightly controlled by initiator proteins that coordinate replication initiation with transcriptional autoregulation. In the F-plasmid system, RepE fulfills both functions through a balance between monomeric and dimeric forms. Here, random mutagenesis of the repE gene combined with high-stringency selection was used to identify variants that modulate plasmid copy number. Two point mutations, A78S and Q45L, were identified and shown by qPCR and ddPCR to increase the copy number of plasmid pFO1 relative to the parental repE(R118P) allele. The mutations exhibited growth-phase-dependent effects, with A78S having a stronger impact during exponential growth and Q45L during stationary phase. A double mutant showed a cumulative effect, particularly in exponential phase. RepE transcription increased in the presence of pFO1 and correlated with plasmid copy number, supporting a titration-based regulatory model. These findings demonstrate that engineering RepE variants enables tunable control of plasmid copy number, offering a useful strategy for optimizing gene dosage in synthetic biology and biotechnological applications. Key points • RepE variants enable fi ne-tuning of plasmid copy number. • Gene dosage can be modulated without changing plasmid architecture. • RepE engineering off ers potential applications in biotechnology.

works.title: Dual-origin probiotic formulation attenuates intestinal inflammation in experimental colitis
works.abstract: Abstract Intestinal inflammation associated with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is driven by complex interactions between host immunity and gut microbiota, necessitating alternative therapeutic strategies beyond conventional immunosuppressive drugs. In the present study, a dual-origin probiotic formulation comprising Lactobacillus plantarum AG40V (plant-derived) and Lactobacillus fermentum HO17HF (human-derived) was developed and evaluated for its safety and anti-inflammatory efficacy in a 2,4,6-trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS)-induced colitis model in Sprague–Dawley rats. The formulation (1012 CFU/mL; 1:1 ratio) exhibited stability under refrigerated conditions and demonstrated significant in vitro functional antioxidant activities. Acute and sub-acute oral toxicity studies, conducted in accordance with OECD guidelines, confirmed the safety of the formulation, with no mortality or significant alterations in physiological, haematological, biochemical, or histopathological parameters. In the TNBS-induced colitis model, oral administration of the probiotic formulation resulted in marked attenuation of intestinal inflammation, as evidenced by reduced levels of nitric oxide, myeloperoxidase, and lipid peroxidation, along with enhanced catalase activity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the dual-origin probiotic formulation is safe and functionally effective in mitigating intestinal inflammation through modulation of oxidative stress and host inflammatory responses. This study highlights the translational potential of ecologically diverse probiotic consortia as a promising strategy for the management of inflammatory gastrointestinal disorders. Key points Dual-origin probiotics showed safety in experimental colitisTreatment reduced inflammation and improved gut healthFindings support probiotic potential in inflammatory bowel disease

works.title: Expanding the structural landscape of cytochrome P450 reductases and the effect of redox mediators on CYP-catalyzed reactions
works.abstract: Abstract Cytochrome P450 reductases (CPRs) are microsomal diflavin oxidoreductases that transfer electrons from nicotinamide cofactors to class II cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYPs). CPRs can also reduce other proteins, including cytochrome b 5 , heme oxygenase, and components of the fatty acid elongation system, as well as nonphysiological acceptors such as cytochrome c , ferricyanide, and various drugs. Although structural and functional studies have provided valuable insights into CPRs, the available data remain insufficient to fully elucidate their electron transfer mechanism and interactions with diverse redox partners. Here, we report the structural and functional characterization of two fungal CPRs from Candida albicans ( Cal CPR) and Mycosarcoma maydis (formerly Ustilago maydis , Uma CPR) and compare their properties with previously characterized CPRs. N -terminal truncation enabled soluble expression in Escherichia coli , and kinetic parameters were determined using cytochrome c and ferricyanide. Although Uma CPR shares greater sequence similarity with ascomycete CPRs than with mammalian CPRs, its overall structure displays features more closely resembling mammalian CPRs, including its FAD-binding topology. We further investigated the ability of both CPRs to support C. albicans CYP52A21 activity and evaluated the effects of reaction environment and redox mediators on CYP–CPR reconstitution. Both truncated CPRs supported CYP activity, with CPR performance strongly influenced by the reaction environment. Addition of the redox mediator cytochrome b 5 from M. maydis significantly enhanced product formation, including when a nonnative CPR was used. These findings highlight the structural diversity and functional plasticity of CPRs and demonstrate that the broader redox environment can strongly influence CYP–CPR efficiency, extending the complexity of electron transfer beyond the canonical CYP–CPR pairing. Key points • CPRs from ascomycetes and basidiomycetes fungi exhibit distinct structural features. • The CPR from Mycosarcoma (Ustilago) maydis is structurally more similar to mammalian CPRs. • CYP-CPR activity is strongly influenced by reaction environment and cytochrome b5 and extends beyond the canonical protein pairing.

works.title: High-throughput mass spectrometry-based metabolomics for large-scale population studies: technical barriers and recent innovations
works.abstract: Large-scale metabolomic studies are needed to identify and validate biomarkers for their successful translation in emerging population health and precision medicine initiatives. Yet, untargeted mass spectrometry (MS)-based metabolomics remains hampered by low sample throughput, limited coverage, complicated data processing, poor standardization, and high operating costs. These challenges also contribute to a reproducibility crisis, with most reported biomarkers not independently replicated, given variations in study designs, sample workup protocols, instrumental methods, and data pre-processing workflows. This review will focus on new advances in high-throughput MS platforms and computational software with emerging artificial intelligence/machine learning tools that are scalable, faster, and less prone to error. Recent progress to improve data harmonization in population-level metabolomic, lipidomic, and exposomic studies (n > 1000) will also be discussed. This will include strategies to correct for long-term batch effects, improve metabolite identification, and derive biochemical insights into disease mechanisms when integrated with multi-omic studies.

works.title: Editorial overview: Environmental Biotechnology in 2026: challenges, opportunities, and new frontiers
The E. coli lite strains: New expression strains for the production of toxic membrane proteins
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The production of recombinant biopharmaceuticals is a billion-dollar industry, with numerous high-value proteins expressed in the bacterium Escherichia coli. Many recombinant protein production (RPP) systems enable the synthesis and purification of large amounts of soluble recombinant protein. However, such systems are often too strong to allow the expression of difficult-to-fold proteins, such as membrane proteins, with high-level RPP resulting in the production of insoluble aggregates ( i.e. , inclusion bodies), target protein degradation and even cell death. To aid the production of problematic proteins, we have engineered the E. coli lite strains in which the plasmid copy number regulator pcnB has been disrupted to allow expression levels of protein targets to be immediately lowered. Using the E. coli lite strains, we express a variety of proteins including green fluorescent protein (GFP), human growth hormone (hGH) and three toxic membrane proteins (BamA ENm , LetB EPEC and YiaM). We show that the E. coli lite strains are able to substantially lower the expression of target proteins and alleviate the cellular toxicity associated with producing membrane-localised proteins. Additionally, we show that the E. coli lite strains are extremely versatile, functioning with a variety of RPP systems, including lac- , T7 RNA polymerase- and paraBAD- based systems, and operate under different expression and growth regimes. Thus, the E. coli lite strains can be used to quickly lower expression levels of complicated target proteins to improve both protein production and cell growth.

works.title: Biosynthesis of 4-hydroxyvalerate from glycerol in engineered Pseudomonas putida KT2440 and its application for the production of poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate-co-4-hydroxy valerate) (P(3HB-co-3HV-co-4HV)) terpolymer
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The 4-hydroxyvalerate (4HV) is a key intermediate that serves as a precursor for γ-valerolactone (GVL) and terpolymers, contributing to the synthesis of liquid fuels and biodegradable plastics with improved properties. While 4HV is typically derived from levulinic acid (LA) via chemical catalysis, these methods are limited by high costs and operational complexity. In our previous study, we designed an engineered Pseudomonas putida KT2440 with double knockout of pcaIJ and lvaR and introduction of aroG , asbF , and adc , enabling high production of LA from glycerol. Herein, we introduced acyl-CoA synthetase gene ( lvaE ) and 4-hydroxyvaleryl-CoA dehydratase gene ( lvaD ) into LA producing strain to construct a 4HV production pathway from glycerol. The strain harboring both lvaD and lvaE consumed the highest amount of LA, and, subsequently, showed the highest 4HV production. In fed batch fermentation , P. putida KT2440 HP403 produced 28.77 mM of 4HV from glycerol. To expand its potential applications as a PHA precursor, biologically synthesized 4HV was supplied to the high-performing PHA producer Cupriavidus necator PHB -4 / phaC BP-M-CPF4 for polymer synthesis. This produced a terpolymer with the composition P(54.49 mol% 3HB- co -6.98 mol% 3HV- co -38.53 mol% 4HV) with a PHA content of 60.21%. The terpolymer exhibited improved elongation at break and lower glass transition and crystallization temperatures due to increased amorphicity. This study suggests a 4HV bioconversion strategy derived from glycerol by engineered P. putida KT2440 HP403 and demonstrates the production of a high-content P(3HB- co -3HV- co -4HV) terpolymer in C. necator containing high-mole fraction of 4HV, thereby providing a new sustainable approach for PHA production.

works.title: Nuclease‐Free Scalable Purification of Physalis Mottle Virus‐Like Particles Expressed in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: Plant virus-like particles (VLPs) are promising nanotechnology platforms, but their translation requires purification strategies suitable for large-scale production. Here, we developed a nuclease-free downstream process for Physalis mottle virus (PhMV) VLPs expressed in Escherichia coli, combining ammonium sulfate precipitation, low-pH extraction, ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF), and flow-through anion-exchange (AEX) chromatography. Ammonium sulfate precipitation separated the VLPs from bulk host nucleic acids, whereas extraction at low pH removed most host cell proteins (HCPs) while retaining the VLPs in solution. Subsequent UF/DF was used to concentrate VLPs and simultaneously achieve buffer exchange for downstream AEX chromatography, which removed remaining HCPs while the PhMV VLPs were collected in the flow-through fraction. This combined workflow produced PhMV VLPs with > 95% purity and a recovery of ~68%. Compared with conventional workflows based on ultracentrifugation and size-exclusion chromatography, the new process reduced the purification time from ~3 days to 1 day and hands-on processing time from ~18 h to 8 h, also increasing the average yield from ~80 to ~130 mg PhMV VLPs per liter of culture. The resulting particles were intact and monodisperse, with a lower content of encapsulated host nucleic acid than VLPs purified by ultracentrifugation. The VLPs also had increased chemical addressability of lysine and cysteine residues. These results establish a scale-up compatible, nuclease-free purification strategy for PhMV VLPs expressed in bacteria and provide a framework for the downstream processing of plant VLP platforms produced in microbial systems.

works.title: A Hybrid Mechanistic Model Capturing Lactate Run‐Away and Back‐Metabolism in Mammalian Cell Culture
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanistic modeling is important in biopharmaceutical manufacturing by enabling in‐silico experimentation. However, developing a robust mechanistic model for mammalian cell culture remains challenging due to the complexity of the underlying bioprocesses. Existing data‐driven models often suffer from limited extrapolation capability and require extensive datasets. Not all modeling approaches can accurately represent differing metabolic scenarios such as lactate consumption and production. To address these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid mechanistic model for mammalian cell culture to improve predictive accuracy and process understanding. Our model integrates high‐frequency pH data with low‐frequency measurements of viable cell density (VCD), glucose, lactate, monoclonal antibody (mAb) concentrations from 10 runs (7 L). Novel kinetic equations for cell growth and death, and lactate metabolism considering both scenarios were developed. Additionally, our model enables automatic lactate switch detection based on time‐series pH and feeding data. It demonstrated high predictive capability with a mean R 2 of 0.88 for VCD, mAb, glucose, and lactate concentrations across training runs. Real‐time fine‐tuning further improved accuracy, reducing the root mean squared error (RMSE) for glucose by ~50% and for lactate by ~30%. The results indicate that our model provides accurate real‐time predictions of VCD, mAb, glucose, and lactate concentrations under variable bioprocessing conditions.

works.title: Serotype‐Tailored Midstream and Downstream Operations to Advance the Manufacturing of Adeno‐Associated Viral Vectors
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Adeno‐associated viruses (AAVs) are the leading vectors for in vivo gene therapy, fueling a growing demand for scalable and robust biomanufacturing processes. Yet, the impact of cell lysis conditions on the performance of midstream and downstream unit operations across serotypes remains poorly characterized. This study presents a serotype‐resolved investigation of cell lysis and its cascading effects on AAV2, AAV5, AAV8, and AAV9 processing. A panel of lysis methods including inorganic agents, non‐ionic and ionic detergents, and mechanical disruption was evaluated using an analytical framework of at‐ and off‐line assays to quantify AAV yield, purity, and activity at each stage. Our results reveal pronounced serotype‐specific differences: cetrimonium bromide (CTAB) delivered the highest transduction output of any condition evaluated for AAV8 (2.25 × 10 9 TU/mL) at 55.0% capture step yield, while sodium deoxycholate achieved ~ 98% host cell protein (HCP) reduction for AAV9 (HCP log reduction value 1.60) and the highest functional enrichment for AAV5 (6.73‐fold) and AAV8 (5.80‐fold). AAV2 proved uniquely challenging, with CTAB enabling the highest tangential flow filtration (TFF) yield. Acid precipitation paired with high salt addition reduced aggregation and improved permeate flux for AAV5 and AAV9. TFF performance was governed by the detergents' physicochemical properties: micelle‐forming agents generated multicomponent complexes that fouled membranes in condition‐ and serotype‐specific patterns. Rheological characterization revealed that all clarified lysates converged to the viscosity of the media after filtration, supporting transferable TFF parameters. Mixed‐mode chromatography using a peptide‐functionalized resin amplified lysis‐imprinted differences, decoupling step yield from functional enrichment. Bayesian optimization of the chromatographic step improved purification outcomes: for AAV8 residual HCPs in the eluate decreased > 300‐fold, from 0.91 mg/mL to 3 μg/mL, while for AAV9 the yield rose to ~95% at residual HCP as low as 14 μg/mL, demonstrating that purity and recovery are co‐optimizable when lysis, midstream, and downstream conditions are rationally paired.

works.title: Coupled dynamic modeling of biomass, gas-phase CO2, and pH during batch cultivation of Poterioochromonas malhamensis with closed gas recirculation
works.abstract: The coupled dynamics of biomass, carbon dioxide, and pH are important for understanding transient responses in photobioreactor cultures under changing carbon availability. In this study, Poterioochromonas malhamensis was cultivated in batch mode in a flat-panel photobioreactor with closed gas recirculation and an initial CO 2 mole fraction of 0.20. Time profiles of biomass, gas-phase CO 2 , and pH were used to develop a semi-empirical reduced dynamic model (RDM). The RDM comprised four state variables, including a dimensionless delayed carbon-response state, and seven parameters estimated by particle swarm optimization. Biomass concentration increased from 0.238 to 3.921 g L -1 , whereas the CO 2 mole fraction decreased to the lower reading limit of 0.003. The pH remained close to 6.9 for approximately 100 h and subsequently increased to 8.81. The model described all three responses, with coefficients of determination of 0.9967, 0.9930, and 0.9936 for biomass, CO 2 , and pH, respectively. In a descriptive comparison with a high-dimensional dynamic formulation (HDF), the RDM reduced the number of independently adjustable parameters from 31 to 7, increased the observation-to-parameter ratio from 1.45 to 6.43, and decreased the normalized residual sum of squares by 58.7%. Identifiability analysis indicated greater stability for k y , y crit , and τ pH , together with dependencies among parameters associated with the delayed carbon response and cell decay. Overall, structural reduction improved parsimony and transparency, made parameter estimation more tractable, and preserved an integrated description of the experimental responses.

works.title: A robust osmotic shock method for extraction of periplasmic recombinant protein from E. coli
works.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND The selection of a simple, robust and efficient extraction method for periplasmic or soluble recombinant proteins from Escherichia coli is critical for maximizing recovery, preserving protein quality and reducing downstream processing costs. RESULTS Present study proposes an optimized osmotic shock method (OSM) using phosphate buffer saline (PBS) for extraction of periplasmic recombinant protein expressed in E. coli. The effectiveness of the PBS‐based OSM with and without sucrose and EDTA has been successfully demonstrated for two different periplasmic proteins (nanobody and alpha synuclein). In case of nanobody and alpha synuclein products, the highest extraction yields of 89.33 ± 0.9 mg L −1 and 139.3 ± 0.7 mg L −1 of cell culture were obtained, respectively. The PBS‐based OSM with and without sucrose and EDTA also exhibited 87–90% reduction in host cell proteins with purity levels of ~50% for both the proteins without needing excessive downstream processing steps. Analytical characterization via reversed‐phase high‐performance liquid chromatography (RP‐HPLC), intact mass and peptide mapping for both the proteins has assessed the product quality. The purification yield of the nanobody product using PBS‐based OSM was ~67% higher with purity levels 21% better as compared to conventional method ( P < 0.05). Likewise, alpha synuclein protein exhibited 50–55 mg L −1 of purification yield with ~89% purity levels. CONCLUSION The proposed PBS‐based OSM would be interest to manufacturers, engaged in production of periplasmic or soluble recombinant proteins expressed in E. coli , as it provides a simple and efficient approach for protein extraction while maintaining product quality and reducing downstream processing complexity. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: Behavioral and metabolic profiling of endogenous lipids conversion to carotenoids in Rhodosporidium toruloides under sugar depletion
Extraction of curcumin using aqueous biphasic systems: Mechanisms, system design, and pathways to scalable industrial implementation
works.abstract: Curcumin (CCM), a bioactive polyphenol from Curcuma longa , has attracted considerable interest due to its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and its relevance in food and nutraceutical applications. However, its large-scale utilization is limited by poor aqueous solubility, chemical instability, and reliance on volatile organic solvents (VOCs) in conventional extraction processes. Aqueous biphasic systems (ABS) have emerged as a promising alternative for CCM extraction and purification, offering water-rich environments and the potential to reduce reliance on conventional organic solvents. Formed by combinations of polymers or copolymers, carbohydrates, alcohols, surfactants, salts, or ionic liquids, ABS provide tunable environments that promote selective CCM partitioning. Recent studies show that micellar systems and cholinium-based ionic liquids enhance extraction efficiency and recovery, while hybrid systems further improve performance and stability. In addition, computational tools such as COSMO-RS support rational system design and optimization of extraction conditions. This review discusses recent advances in ABS-based CCM extraction, focusing on mechanisms, system performance, and prospects for sustainable industrial applications.

works.title: Microbial electromethanogenesis: a novel approach for biomethane enrichment
works.abstract: Abstract Owing to the limited availability of conventional energy resources and their adverse environmental impacts, there is a need for sustainable, environmentally sound alternative energy sources. Biofuel production through biological processes has gained attention as an environmentally benign alternative fuel. Among various biological processes, anaerobic digestion is one of the oldest and most popularized for producing biogas as a promising future energy source. However, raw biogas cannot be used as a fuel for transportation or other applications because it contains non‐calorific gases, such as CO 2 , which lowers its energy density. Therefore, upgrading biogas by removing CO 2 is necessary to increase its CH 4 content. Microbial electromethanogenesis is a potential technique for converting CO 2 to CH 4 that not only upgrades biogas to biomethane but also increases its energy density, ultimately enhancing its calorific value. In this technique, methane is produced by reducing CO 2 with biocatalysts under a low imposed potential. It can be used to upgrade biogas to biomethane, offering many advantages, such as efficient conversion of waste CO 2 into energy products like CH 4 , which makes the process environmentally friendly, with very low power consumption, a high methane content in the upgraded biogas, and economic benefits. The present study focuses on the operation, scaling‐up, techno‐economic analysis, and future scope of microbial electromethanogenesis for biogas enrichment to improve its efficiency. As a result of techno‐economic assessments, electrode materials can account for approximately 59% of total capital expenditure, while electricity may constitute up to 69% of operating expenditure, demonstrating the importance of electrode costs and electricity demand to process economics. Model‐based analyses have further indicated positive economic performance at electricity prices of ≤€0.045 kWh −1 under the evaluated process assumptions. Overall, the technology presents an excellent opportunity to upgrade biogas and valorize CO 2 , but further improvements in efficiency, reactor design, material durability, microbial stability, and system economics are needed to progress from pilot‐scale demonstrations to commercially viable biomethane production.

works.title: A system dynamics‐based framework for bioenergy planning in sub‐Saharan Africa: integrating circular bioeconomy and Fourth Industrial Revolution technologies
works.abstract: Abstract Energy scarcity remains a persistent challenge in sub‐Saharan Africa (SSA), where limited access to reliable, affordable, and clean energy constrains socioeconomic development. Biomass resources, including agricultural residues, forest waste, and waste from other biological sources, are widely available, but their use for modern energy generation and their management remain inefficient. In this study, a hybrid framework called system dynamics (SD)–techno‐economic analysis (TEA) was developed to analyze biomass utilization and bioenergy transition pathways in SSA based on circular bioeconomy and Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) resource coordination methods, with Nigeria and South Africa as illustrative case studies. The model was parameterized using secondary data on biomass availability, energy demand, energy conversion efficiency, and technoeconomic parameters from international databases and the published literature. The model was tested through structural verification, calibration, and sensitivity analysis. The mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 9.8% for biomass utilization in SSA and 11.2% for installed bioenergy capacity in Nigeria. The Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) installed bioenergy capacity in South Africa was 25 MW. Simulation results indicate that optimized biomass recovery, improved conversion efficiency, and digitally informed resource coordination increased delivered bioenergy services by 12% to 18% while reducing biomass input intensity and improving resource utilization. Comparative analysis shows that Nigeria remained more dependent on traditional biomass, whereas South Africa demonstrated greater potential for integrating circular bioeconomy strategies into modern bioenergy systems. The proposed SD–TEA framework provides a transparent decision‐support tool for evaluating bioenergy transition pathways and supporting evidence‐based energy planning and circular bioeconomy development in SSA.

works.title: Translation of in vivo CAR-T in China
Translating Innovation to Clinic: End‐to‐End Bioprocess Development and cGMP Manufacturing of N332‐GT5 HIV Vaccine Candidate for First‐In‐Human Trials (HVTN144)
works.abstract: The successful translation of rationally designed HIV-1 immunogens into effective vaccines requires manufacturing platforms that maintain structural conformity while meeting clinical-grade quality standards. We developed and scaled up a robust, cGMP-compliant process for N332-GT5 gp140, a germline-targeting envelope trimer designed to initiate broadly neutralizing antibody responses, which is now undergoing first-in-human evaluation in HVTN144. Starting with a stable CHO cell line developed using Leap-In® transposon technology, we established a production clone exhibiting high-titer expression (> 200 mg/L) and genetic stability through 60 population doublings. The manufacturing process scaled up efficiently from Ambr® 250 miniature bioreactors to 200-L single-use systems, delivering consistent product quality across multiple cGMP batches. A streamlined three-step purification strategy-affinity capture, multimodal polishing, and viral clearance -yielded > 99% trimeric purity while preserving quaternary structure and native-like antigenicity. Orthogonal LC-MS analyses confirmed site-specific glycan occupancy matching design specifications, while robust viral clearance exceeded 18-log and 11-log reductions for model retroviruses. Clinical material manufactured through this platform has been successfully administered in clinical trial HVTN144. This work establishes a scalable, reproducible manufacturing paradigm for structurally complex HIV-1 envelope immunogens, advancing the field toward rational vaccine design based on germline-targeting principles.

works.title: Amyloid‐Based Hydrogels as Emerging Biomaterials for Wound Healing: A Review
works.abstract: Wound healing is a complex and dynamic biological process that occurs in a series of coordinated steps, including hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, and tissue remodeling. Traditional wound dressings, such as gauze and bandages, are not suitable for healing because they do not maintain moisture levels and cannot prevent infections. So, hydrogels have been recognized as advanced wound-healing materials because of their high-water content and their ability to mimic the natural ECM. Additionally, amyloid-based hydrogels have been recognized for their unique physicochemical and functional properties, which are constructed by the self-assembly of peptides into highly ordered fibrillar structures. The nanoscale fibrillar structure provides the hydrogels with high mechanical stability and viscoelasticity. The porous structure allows the movement of oxygen and nutrients, as well as the removal of waste products. They can also self-heal and be formulated in injectable forms for application to wounds with irregular surfaces. Their unique structural and functional properties make them highly effective at accelerating wound healing. This review highlights in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrating the efficacy of amyloid-based hydrogels in accelerating wound healing, making them highly promising materials for advanced wound healing.

works.title: Induction Temperature and Feeding Profile Shape the Partitioning Between Soluble Product and Inclusion Body Formation in Escherichia coli
works.abstract: Inclusion body (IB) processes yielding the recombinant product only as IBs are long-established in the biopharmaceutical industry. Yet, for recombinant proteins that accumulate both IBs and soluble fraction depending on the selected upstream processing (USP) strategy, the influence of process parameters on the partitioning between both forms remains poorly characterized. In this study, l-lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) was selected as a model protein as it yields IBs and soluble protein concurrently. We investigated how induction temperature and specific substrate uptake rate shift the relative amount of soluble product. A response surface model revealed a sharp switch between exclusively soluble production at 25°C, exclusive IB formation at 35°C and a mixed production regime at 30°C. Further, we investigated whether these trends hold for the structurally related proteins xylose isomerase (Xiso) and pyranose-2-oxidase (P2O) using a reduced diagonal design and a projection into the LDH latent space by principal component analysis (PCA). Results revealed that the shared structural features were not sufficient to predict the expression form. Still, the LDH model served as a reference framework for identifying the extent to which other mixed producers follow established process-response trends.

works.title: Integrated dual-pathway valorization of Feijoa sellowiana: Adsorption of safranin O and methylene blue and antioxidant capacity evaluation
Unraveling the proteome of Escherichia coli during L-phenylalanine production in a scale-down bioreactor
works.abstract: Large-scale industrial bioprocesses are characterized by spatial and temporal inhomogeneities that expose microorganisms to fluctuating bioprocess conditions. These gradients can strongly influence cellular physiology, thereby affecting bioprocess robustness and product formation. Although phenotypic population heterogeneity under such conditions has been described, the underlying protein-level mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, the impact of environmental fluctuations on the proteome of an L-phenylalanine producing Escherichia coli strain was investigated. Samples were collected from cultivations in a well-mixed stirred-tank bioreactor and a two-compartment bioreactor operated at mean hydraulic residence times of τ = 103s and τ = 404s. Global proteome patterns were analyzed using principal component analysis (PCA), followed by differential protein abundance analysis and functional interpretation by gene ontology (GO) enrichment and clusters of orthologous groups (COG)-based analysis. PCA identified residence time in the bypass as the dominant factor shaping proteome variation. Prolonged exposure to limiting conditions at τ = 404s led to a distinct clustering of proteome profiles, clearly separated from both the stirred-tank bioreactor and the shorter residence time condition. GO enrichment analysis revealed increased abundance of proteins associated with stress response during the batch and product formation phases, and proteins related to cell communication during biomass production. Consistently, COG-based analysis showed a shift from growth- and production-associated proteins toward maintenance and stress adaptation in cells from the two-compartment bioreactor, with this shift becoming more pronounced at longer residence times.

works.title: Synthetic biology strategies for engineering bacteriophages against intracellular tumor-associated bacteria: emerging tools for precision oncology
works.abstract: Abstract The tumor microenvironment (TME) comprises malignant, stromal, immune, and microbial components. Spatial imaging and molecular profiling have identified intracellular bacteria or bacterial signals in selected tumors, although localization, viability, and functional significance vary across tumor types and experimental settings. Certain tumor-associated bacteria can influence cancer progression and treatment response, motivating strategies for selective microbial intervention. Bacteriophages offer bacterial specificity and opportunities for engineering, but their access to intracellular targets remains a major challenge. This narrative review examines three proposed strategies: lytic elimination of intracellular bacteria, modification of bacterial functions, and bacterial production of therapeutic payloads following phage-mediated delivery. Evidence from mammalian-cell uptake studies, intracellular infection models, and emerging cancer cell-bacterium co-cultures supports individual components of these strategies. However, the complete sequence linking systemic engineered phage delivery, intracellular bacterial clearance, and antitumor immune reprogramming has not been established in orthotopic tumor models or human tumor organoid systems. We therefore present the intracellular scalpel as a testable hypothesis and discuss its potential combinations with established cancer treatments and exploratory adjuvants. Particular attention is given to delivery barriers, evidence limitations, biosafety, and the preclinical measurements required to determine whether intracellular bacterial targeting can improve cancer treatment.

works.title: Novel combined effect of sublethal heat and ethanol for enhanced gamma-aminobutyric acid production via whole-cell catalysis of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
works.abstract: Maintaining cell envelope integrity and intracellular enzyme stability while alleviating transmembrane mass-transfer limitations is important for sustained γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) production by whole-cell biocatalysis. We investigated the effects of ethanol on the apparent whole-cell glutamate decarboxylase (GAD) activity of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum SS5 and optimized the corresponding GABA production process. Co-incubation with 6–8% (v/v) ethanol increased the apparent whole-cell GAD activity and its residual activity after prolonged heat exposure. Scanning electron microscopy and extracellular GAD assays after 30 min of treatment with 7% (v/v) ethanol showed no gross morphological disruption or detectable GAD leakage. After ethanol removal, the apparent whole-cell GAD activity of ethanol-treated cells showed no significant difference from that of untreated cells ( p > 0.05). These findings are consistent with a transient, condition-dependent effect of ethanol on the cell envelope. The optimized system consisted of a 0.20 mol·L⁻¹ L-monosodium glutamate (MSG) working solution and a 100 mg·mL⁻¹ wet cell suspension mixed at a volume ratio of 1:1 (v/v), followed by the addition of 6% (v/v) ethanol (approximately 0.09 mol·L⁻¹ MSG in the complete reaction mixture), with the reaction conditions set at pH 5.2, 42 °C, 80 rpm, and a reaction time of 56 h. In triplicate experiments, the GABA titer reached 8.87 ± 0.13 mmol·L⁻¹, corresponding to a 27.23 ± 1.83% increase over the ethanol-free control. Thus, ethanol can serve as a food-grade process additive for enhancing the efficiency of this laboratory-scale whole-cell bioconversion process.

works.title: Optimization of acid‐catalyzed transesterification of oil derived from mango processing seed waste: a step towards the circular economy
works.abstract: Abstract Energy is the basis for socio‐economic development. The effects of fossil‐based energy sources underscore the urgent need for renewable and cost‐effective alternatives. Biofuels derived from non‐edible and low‐cost feedstocks are a promising alternative. This study focused on optimizing biodiesel production from mango seed waste‐derived oils using sulfuric acid‐catalyzed transesterification. A central composite design involving molar ratio (M) and catalyst amount (C) at three levels, excluding the axial points, was employed to investigate their effects on conversion ( X MO ) and fatty acid methyl esters (FAME) yield. Response surface methodology was used to optimize the reaction conditions of the process. The results of the statistical analysis revealed distinct trends in the responses, which were influenced by the M and C levels. The maximum X MO (78.79%) and FAME yield (78.87%) were achieved at a linear point with M of 1:35 and 65% C, whereas the lowest responses were at 1:65 and 35%, respectively. This implies that M and C have significant effects on conversion and FAME yield. The statistical analysis showed that curvature is not significant ( P > 0.05), implying that the linear model is found to be suitable to optimize the responses. The optimization resulted in a FAME yield of 78.775% and X MO of 78.238% at M of 1:35, C of 65 wt.%, a mild reaction temperature of 60 °C, and a stirring speed of 700 rpm. The regression analysis revealed that the model was significant and robust in capturing the impact of the factors, with excellent agreement between the experimental and predicted values.

works.title: Computer-aided design of halohydrin dehalogenase for simultaneous improvement of thermostability and activity
CYP1B1 is a potential target of kaempferol in renal fibrosis: a multi‑omics and single‑cell transcriptomics study
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Renal fibrosis (RF) is a progressive and irreversible pathological process for which effective treatments are limited. This study explores the molecular targets and mechanisms through which kaempferol (Kae) ameliorates RF, with particular emphasis on cytochrome P450 1B1 (CYP1B1). METHODS: Using a combination of transcriptomic profiling, weighted gene co‑expression network analysis (WGCNA), multi‑algorithm machine learning [least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), support vector machine‑recursive feature elimination (SVM‑RFE), and Random Forest], and single‑cell transcriptomics, we identified the core targets of Kae intervention in RF. shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis evaluated gene contributions to the predictive model, while cell‑type identification by estimating relative subsets of RNA transcripts (CIBERSORT) estimated the immune microenvironment. The cell type-specific distribution of core targets was further characterized through single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and the scTenifoldKnk (a machine learning-based virtual gene knockout tool) algorithm simulated the effects of CYP1B1 loss-of-function on fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. Finally, molecular docking was performed to predict the binding conformations of kaempferol with the proteins encoded by the six prioritized genes. RESULTS: Six core genes (VCAM1, NFKBIA, SFN, CCL5, CYP1B1, and AXL) were identified from 25 Kae-RF-related genes, with CYP1B1 as an upstream regulatory hub. Immune infiltration analysis revealed increased plasma cells and eosinophils, alongside decreased M0/M1 macrophages and activated NK cells. Single-cell analysis localized CYP1B1 to smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts, with significant upregulation during late-stage fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation. Virtual knockdown of CYP1B1 upregulated 46 genes associated with fibrosis-related biological processes, including cell adhesion, G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling, ion transport, and cytoskeletal remodeling. The six-gene diagnostic model achieved area under the curves (AUCs) of 0.889 (training) and 0.759 (external validation). Molecular docking showed favorable Kae-CYP1B1 binding (- 6.5 kcal/mol). CONCLUSION: CYP1B1 may serve as a potential functional target of Kae in RF, likely through modulation of fibroblast activation and ECM remodeling. These findings are hypothesis‑generating and provide a computational basis for future experimental validation of CYP1B1‑targeted strategies in RF.

works.title: A gut microbiota–metabolite–host gene score for subtyping and predicting the treatment response in rheumatoid arthritis: integrative analysis with in silico knockout validation
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: The pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves a complex interplay between immune dysregulation and metabolic disturbance, with the gut microbiota and its metabolites playing pivotal roles. However, integrated biomarkers based on the "gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene" regulatory axis that can quantify its impact on RA stratification and therapeutic response are lacking. METHODS: We integrated multiple RA transcriptomic datasets to screen for host genes explicitly associated with the gut microbiota and metabolites using the gutMGene database. A gut microbiota-metabolite-host score (GMS) was constructed via principal component analysis (PCA). Immune infiltration patterns were evaluated using CIBERSORT. Furthermore, scRNA-seq was employed to map the cellular origins of key genes, and in silico knockout analysis using scTenifoldKnk was performed to simulate the functional ablation of core host genes within this regulatory axis. Additionally, molecular docking was conducted to validate the binding affinities between the key host proteins and the optimal small molecule. RESULTS: We identified seven microbiota-metabolite-host hub genes (FOS, JUN, IDO1, PEMT, EGFR, ABCC4, and FADS3) and constructed the GMS. The GMS stratified patients with RA into two distinct functional subtypes: an adaptive immune activation subtype and an inflammatory-metabolic composite subtype. Notably, the GMS demonstrated superior performance in predicting responses to anti-TNF and rituximab therapies. The scRNA-seq analysis revealed high expression of FOS and JUN in T cells and NK cells. In silico knockout analysis further revealed the central transcription factors FOS and JUN as key executors of this axis, as their ablation significantly affected osteoclast differentiation and the enrichment of TNF/MAPK inflammatory pathways. These computational findings support the core mechanism by which gut microbiota-metabolite signalling drives RA joint pathology via FOS/JUN. Molecular docking results confirmed strong binding interactions between the identified active molecules and their respective target proteins. CONCLUSION: This study establishes a GMS based on the gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene regulatory axis as a robust tool for molecular subtyping and predicting biological therapy responses in patients with RA. Crucially, through integrated computational modelling, including in silico knockout and molecular docking validation, we identified FOS/JUN as critical executor genes linking the gut microenvironment to RA bone destruction, providing novel targets for therapeutic strategies aimed at the gut-joint axis.

works.title: Lignin separation modification and high-value utilization based on low eutectic solvents: a review
works.abstract: Agricultural and forestry waste is rich in renewable lignin, which holds natural potential for the production of fine chemicals and functional materials. However, lignin is tightly cross-linked with cellulose and hemicellulose. Traditional extraction processes using strong acids and bases can easily cause lignin molecular condensation and damage to the molecular framework. At the same time, there are problems such as high energy consumption and heavy environmental burden, which seriously restrict its resource utilization. Due to their advantages of simple synthesis, high tunability, and environmental friendliness, deep eutectic solvents (DES) have become a research hotspot for the green and efficient extraction of lignin. This paper systematically reviews the latest research findings on DES-based extraction of lignin from agricultural and forestry waste, summarizes the characteristics of different types of DES components, investigates the effects of process parameters on lignin extraction efficiency and structural retention, and provides an in-depth analysis of the lignin's characteristic bonds, functional group composition, and other microstructural features. The study confirms that DES can achieve selective dissolution of lignin and effectively cleave ether bonds such as β-O-4; the resulting lignin has a low molecular weight, a narrow distribution, and a high content of phenolic hydroxyl groups, laying an excellent structural foundation for subsequent chemical modification and deep processing. The paper also further summarizes the high-value application potential of this type of lignin in fields such as the preparation of phenolic compounds and the synthesis of functional materials. At the same time, it objectively analyzes the practical challenges currently faced by DES technology in process optimization, solvent recycling, and industrial-scale upscaling, and makes targeted predictions regarding future key development directions. The aim is to provide a theoretical basis and practical reference for the iteration of green lignin separation technologies and the construction of high-value conversion systems for waste biomass.

works.title: De novo production of mandelic- and 3-phenyllactic acid from lignocellulosic feedstock through Phlebia radiata IBWF-87241
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Phlebia radiata is a white-rot basidiomycete that secretes a repertoire of oxidative enzymes making it a promising organism for the sustainable bio-production of aromatic compounds during lignocellulose-containing cultivation. Here, we investigate the association between wood supplementation and extracellular production of aromatic α-hydroxy acids by P. radiata IBWF 87241 under defined axenic conditions, while accompanying changes in extracellular oxidative enzyme activity and residual wood fibres were characterized using enzyme assays and ATR-FTIR spectroscopy. RESULTS: GC-EI-MS analysis of culture filtrate extracts, confirmed by authentic standards, revealed two aromatic α-hydroxy acids produced exclusively under wood-containing conditions. Mandelic acid and 3-phenyllactic acid were produced by P. radiata in ½ soy medium supplemented with 1% (w/v) spruce wood powder, but were absent from un-supplemented and uninoculated controls across repeated cultivation experiments. Continuous monitoring of the cultivation shows that extracellular laccase activity increased throughout fermentation and reached a maximum on day 7, whereas H₂O₂-dependent ABTS oxidation remained low throughout the experiment, while esterase activity showed a minor transient increase. ATR-FTIR analysis of recovered wood powder revealed reproducible treatment-associated spectral differences relative to untreated controls in regions assigned to lignin- and carbohydrate-associated functional groups. Scale-up cultivation in a 20 L stirred-tank bioreactor yielded preliminary titers of 0.79 mg/L mandelic acid and 4.11 mg/L 3-phenyllactic acid, establishing baseline production levels under controlled process conditions. CONCLUSIONS: These findings establish P. radiata IBWF 87241 as a non-engineered fungal host for the production of aromatic α-hydroxy acids under wood-containing cultivation conditions and provide a quantitative baseline for future metabolic engineering and bioprocess optimisation strategies targeting mandelic acid and 3-phenyllactic acid production. To our knowledge, this is the first report of production of mandelic acid and 3-phenyllactic acid by P. radiata under defined cultivation conditions. The combined characterization of extracellular oxidative activity, FTIR spectral differences in recovered wood, and aromatic α-hydroxy acid production provides a framework for future investigations of extracellular oxidative metabolism, substrate-associated spectral alterations, and aromatic metabolite formation during fungal lignocellulose conversion.

works.title: Highly selective ethanol production via the thermophilic bioconversion of sugars and syngas using metabolically engineered Neomoorella thermoacetica
works.abstract: Abstract Background Ethanol production from biomass-derived and gaseous substrates (CO, H 2 and CO 2 ) is essential for achieving a carbon-neutral society. The thermophilic acetogen Neomoorella thermoacetica offers notable industrial advantages for converting such diverse feedstocks; however, its physiology and metabolic engineering strategies remain insufficiently understood. Results Using stoichiometric analysis, we evaluated the metabolic pathways for ethanol production from sugars and gaseous substrates, with particular attention to redox balance and ATP conservation. This analysis suggested that introducing an NADPH-dependent route for reducing acetyl-CoA to ethanol could maintain redox-balanced metabolism under conditions that support sufficient energy generation. Consistent with this prediction, disruption of the major acetate-forming pathway, together with the introduction of heterologous NADPH-dependent reductases, enabled high-selectivity ethanol production (> 90%) from both sugars and syngas. Inactivation of the acetate pathway did not result in growth arrest. In contrast, little to no growth occurred when H 2 was supplied as the sole energy source. However, growth and ethanol production were restored by the addition of an external electron acceptor that supported anaerobic respiration. This result was consistent with the predicted energy deficit. Conclusion The strain constructed using a redox-guided metabolic design attained > 90% ethanol selectivity from both sugar- and syngas-based substrates. These findings demonstrate that stoichiometric analysis of redox balance and ATP conservation can provide useful guidance for engineering ethanol-producing thermophilic acetogens.

works.title: Waste‐to‐resource synthesis of TiO 2 /activated carbon nanocomposites from coffee husk and ilmenite for tetracycline removal
works.abstract: Abstract A waste‐to‐resource TiO 2 /activated carbon (TiO 2 /AC) nanocomposite was synthesized from Vietnamese Robusta coffee husk and locally sourced ilmenite for tetracycline (TC) removal from aqueous solution. Coffee husk was converted into porous activated carbon, while ilmenite was used as the titanium precursor, enabling the integration of agricultural and mineral‐resource valorization into a single photocatalytic material. The TiO 2 /AC composite was prepared through in situ deposition followed by calcination, producing an anatase–rutile TiO 2 phase anchored on a porous carbon matrix. Scanning electron microscopy, X‐ray diffraction, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, Brunauer–Emmett–Teller, UV–vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy, and photoluminescence analyses confirmed the formation of a hierarchical TiO 2 /AC structure with preserved mesoporosity, improved light absorption, and suppressed charge recombination. The activated carbon exhibited a high specific surface area of 535.53 m 2 g −1 and a pore volume of 0.16 cm 3 g −1 , whereas TiO 2 /AC retained a surface area of 211.36 m 2 g −1 with an increased pore volume of 0.38 cm 3 g −1 , indicating the formation of additional interparticle mesoporosity. Dark adsorption experiments showed that TC uptake on TiO 2 /AC was mainly surface‐controlled and heterogeneous, with pseudo‐first‐order and Elovich models providing better kinetic fitting than the Bangham model. Under simulated sunlight, TiO 2 /AC achieved 97.01% TC removal, exceeding pristine TiO 2 and AC, demonstrating the combined contribution of adsorption enrichment and photocatalytic oxidation. Radical scavenger tests identified photogenerated holes, hydroxyl radicals, and superoxide radicals as the principal reactive species. The composite retained high activity after five cycles, with removal efficiency remaining above 91%. These findings indicate that coffee‐husk‐derived activated carbon can act as an effective adsorptive and interfacial modifier for ilmenite‐derived TiO 2 , offering a low‐cost and environmentally compatible strategy for antibiotic‐contaminated wastewater treatment.

works.title: Structurally informed metabolite measurements with ion mobility-mass spectrometry
works.abstract: Although ion mobility-mass spectrometry (IM-MS) is no longer a new technology, new developments in instrumentation and resources for structurally informed measurements are enabling the use of IM-MS in emerging metabolomic applications. Once limited by experimental measurements, the growth of machine-learning strategies to predict collision cross-section values is rapidly increasing the coverage of IM-MS information in metabolite databases. IM-MS instrumentation capable of high-resolution separations is bringing new depth to the level of structural annotation that can be achieved, while creative strategies to combine IM-MS with complementary analytical or chemical methods are further leveraging its ability to resolve small molecule isomers and isobars. This brief review highlights the recent developments of IM-MS for metabolomics with a focus on applications to mass spectrometry imaging, rapid multi-omics, and single-cell analyses.

works.title: Engineering sticky microbes: A framework for appraisal of microbial cell-cell adhesion
works.abstract: Engineering bacterial consortia is key in biotechnological applications where specific spatial interactions among their components determine system performance. Genetic tools for programming cell-cell binding such as the nanobody-antigen (Nb-Ag; relying on non-covalent binding) and SpyCatcher-SpyTag (Spy; based on covalent linkage) systems are increasingly adopted as assets for enabling specific interactions of interest among otherwise detached members of a given combination of strains or species. Yet, despite the potential of these technologies, a robust metrology to quantify and compare the efficacy, stability, and specificity of inter-cell binding in a consortium is lacking. This work introduces a conceptual and experimental framework to systematically evaluate synthetic binding systems by combining aggregation assays, flow cytometry, and microscopy. Together, these techniques provide detailed insights into the structure and composition of engineered bacterial aggregates. This methodology was benchmarked with two Escherichia coli strains tagged with different fluorescent markers and engineered to surface-display matching adhesins. Under the test conditions, results showed that the Spy system outperformed the Nb-Ag system in terms of aggregation speed and stability. We also applied the same metrics for assessing the efficacy of the Spy system to mediate synthetic consortia of the opportunistic pathogenic bacterium Enterobacter cloacae. The robustness of the results suggests that the proposed framework could become a valuable tool for quantitative studies on designer bacterial consortia.

works.title: Host physiological constraints limit microbial production of partially acetylated chitooligosaccharides
works.abstract: Chitooligosaccharides (COS) are versatile biomolecules with applications across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic industries. Expanding the COS portfolio, particularly with partially acetylated COS (paCOS) possessing defined structural characteristics, including degree of deacetylation and pattern of acetylation, is essential for advancing structure-function studies and enabling tailored applications. This study investigates the heterologous co-expression of chitin deacetylases (CDAs) with a chitin oligosaccharide synthase (oCS) RhNodC in Escherichia coli for the in vivo production of paCOS. Although this approach enables paCOS formation, co-expression of NodC and CDAs results in reduced COS yields and incomplete conversion of fully acetylated COS into paCOS. To identify potential cellular bottlenecks underlying these limitations, stress responses were monitored using a stress promoter-based fluorescent reporter system. CDA co-expression activated protein quality control and membrane-associated stress responses. Furthermore, confocal microscopy revealed altered intracellular localization of both RhNodC and CDAs compared to individual expression, with enzymes detected in the cytoplasm, membrane and inclusion bodies. Co-expression also resulted in pronounced cellular elongation, further indicating cellular stress during pathway implementation. Together, these findings reveal cellular bottlenecks associated with enzyme co-expression and highlight the need for deeper exploration of RhNodC-CDA co-expression and approaches to mitigate cellular stress to improve in vivo paCOS production.

works.title: Comprehensive review of hydrogen energy systems: trends, technologies, and future applications
works.abstract: Abstract Green hydrogen, the renewable energy‐driven hydrogen produced through water electrolysis, has become one of the key decarbonization options across energy‐intensive industries. The present review describes the primary technologies of hydrogen which are mature alkaline, proton exchange membrane, solid oxide, and newer technologies like anion exchange membrane and photo electrochemical processes. Additionally, the current review covers the choice of hydrogen storage and distribution by alternatives as compression, liquefaction, ammonia, and liquid organic hydrogen carriers that have different energy and infrastructure requirements. The current review also discusses the large‐scale decarbonization efforts focus on the steel sector, the chemical industry, and transport use currently represented by fuel‐cell cars, ammonia‐fueled ships, or e‐kerosene‐powered flights. The review additionally covers the aspects related artificial intelligence and digitalization in hydrogen systems The constant issues of infrastructure, materials, and safety are still apparent but AI advances, the integration of systems, and the global collaboration of scientific entities are making green hydrogen one of the backbones of future sustainable energy systems. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: An immobilized system with swapping cofactor-recycling enzymes in the synthesis of natural products
works.abstract: Sustainable biosynthesis of small-molecule natural products (NPs) is often hampered by enzyme instability and high cofactor costs. Herein, we developed a modular bi-functional immobilization system to synthesize two NPs (carvone and vanillyl alcohol). Building on the glyoxyl-agarose technology pioneered by Prof. José M. Guisán, we covalently immobilized an alcohol dehydrogenase (BsADH) to allow for biocatalyst reusability. This system was then coupled with two different cofactor-recycling enzymes (LpNOX for NAD + regeneration, and CbFDH for NADH regeneration), which were reversibly immobilized on the same support. The co-immobilization enabled 25–50% higher productivity compared to independently immobilized enzymes. This modular system allows the selective desorption of a cofactor-recycling enzyme (LpNOX, >90% desorption) without affecting the covalently attached ADH, and enabling the co-immobilization of another cofactor-recycling enzyme (CbFDH). This flexible and sustainable platform for redox biocatalysis was applied to the consecutive synthesis of NPs of interest for the pharmaceutical and fragrance industries.

works.title: Controlled protein hydrolysis as a strategy to modulate gelation in meltable and stretchable multicomponent gels based on canola protein, waxy corn starch, and coconut oil
Small particles but big clusters
Elevating CO2 electrolyzer temperature accelerates the viability of chemical electrification
works.abstract: Abstract Climate change mitigation has spurred interest in producing chemicals from CO 2 . CO 2 reduction by electrochemistry can be driven directly by green electricity, yielding even multi-carbon (C2+) products. However, the resulting processes still suffer from high electrolyzer losses and substantial energy demands. This study evaluates the environmental and economic benefits of integrating optimized electrolyzers into complete processes. For CO 2 electroreduction to ethylene and dimerization to 1-butene, elevated-temperature electrolysis effectively utilizes waste heat. Challenging the ambient-temperature paradigm, this strategy achieves system-wide savings in energy (10%), climate impacts (9%) and overall cost (11%). Generalizing these findings across various CO 2 electroreduction pathways identifies energy savings of up to 25% and the heating system as a key design variable affecting electrolyzer design targets. Our study demonstrates how process integration can guide CO 2 electrolyzer development toward sustainable processes.

works.title: Charging up direct air capture
Resources for engineering across scales
Agents intuit enzyme design
Rumen microbiome carbohydrate metabolism is associated with host lipid metabolic differences between Wagyu and Nanyang cattle
works.abstract: Abstract The rumen microbiome plays an important role in converting dietary carbohydrates into metabolites associated with host physiology, yet the relationships between microbial carbohydrate metabolism and host lipid metabolism remain incompletely understood. Here, we compared Japanese Wagyu and Nanyang cattle to investigate microbiota–metabolite–host associations in relation to breed-associated differences in intramuscular fat (IMF) deposition. Metagenomic analysis revealed differences in rumen microbial community composition and functional profiles between breeds, including differential abundances of carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) families associated with polysaccharide degradation. Wagyu cattle exhibited higher abundances of glycoside hydrolase (GH) families GH5 (cellulose degradation) and GH92 (alpha-mannan degradation), whereas GH13 (starch degradation) and GH43 (arabinoxylan and arabinan degradation) were enriched in Nanyang cattle, together with differences in carbohydrate-degrading genera, including Prevotella , Fibrobacter , and Butyrivibrio . These microbial functional differences were accompanied by distinct fermentation profiles, with higher ruminal acetate and butyrate concentrations in Wagyu cattle and higher propionate concentrations in Nanyang cattle. Proteomic analysis of the longissimus dorsi muscle identified breed-associated differences in proteins involved in lipid synthesis, lipid storage, and energy metabolism, including FABP4, FASN, PLIN1, ACSS2, and IDH1, which showed higher abundances in Wagyu cattle. Correlation analyses identified associations among microbial taxa, CAZyme families, fermentation metabolites, and host proteins related to lipid metabolism and IMF deposition. Overall, these findings reveal coordinated breed-associated differences in rumen microbial functions, fermentation characteristics, and host lipid metabolic profiles, providing insights into microbiota–host metabolic associations related to IMF deposition in cattle. Keypoints • Rumen carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) profiles differ between Wagyu and Nanyang cattle. • Wagyu cattle show higher acetate and butyrate levels. • Microbiota–volatile fatty acids (VFAs)–proteome axis is linked to intramuscular fat (IMF) deposition

works.title: Numerical analysis of shear rate in a rocking bioreactor and its impact on HL-60 lymphocytes
works.abstract: Abstract The aim of the study was to investigate the influence of hydrodynamic parameters on HL-60 lymphocyte cultures in a rocking disposable bioreactor. A 2D CFD-based model employing the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method was used to characterize the culture microenvironment, while a rotational rheometer was used to determine critical shear thresholds. The developed numerical model was validated against experimental mixing times, yielding an absolute mean percentage difference of 29.2%, demonstrating high predictive accuracy at very low and very high Reynolds numbers, though limitations were observed at medium Reynolds numbers. Results indicated that while averaged shear rates remained below 22.5 s⁻1, local maximum shear rates significantly exceeded the lethal threshold of 1500 s⁻1 for all studied rocking conditions, reaching over 30 000 s⁻1 at the highest parameters. Analysis of shear rate effects on HL-60 lymphocytes demonstrated that cell viability decreases at shear rates higher than 1000 s⁻1 due to cell membrane disruption, up to total disintegration of cells above 1500 s⁻1. The consistent exceeding of these lethal thresholds, particularly during intensified rocking, was shown to negatively impact cell growth and increase the release of intracellular enzymes. Consequently, the successful application of rocking disposable bioreactors for shear-sensitive cultures requires a strategic trade-off between mixing intensification and the mitigation of lethal local shear effects. The developed computational model provides a valuable framework for such optimization and subsequent bioprocess scale-up. Keypoints • 2D CFD VOF model well predicts hydrodynamics in rocking bioreactors. • Local maximum shear rates exceed 1500 s−1 as lethal threshold for HL-60 cells. • Intensification of cell culture requires balanced mixing and hydrodynamic stress.

works.title: Valorization of seaweed biomass into silica‐reinforced biopolymer films: structure–property relationships and interfacial mechanisms
works.abstract: Abstract The valorization of marine biomass into high‐value bioproducts is crucial for reducing reliance on petroleum‐based plastics while supporting circular bioeconomy strategies. In this study, seaweed ( Kappaphycus alvarezii ) biomass was converted into biodegradable biopolymer films and reinforced with commercial silica nanoparticles (SNPs) to enhance structural integrity and functional performance. Nanocomposite films containing 0–7 wt% SNP were fabricated via solution casting and systematically investigated using Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, X‐ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy, and atomic force microscopy. Spectroscopic analyses confirmed SiOSi contributions and strong polymer–silica interfacial interactions, while XRD results showed that SNP addition maintained the semi‐crystalline characteristics of the seaweed matrix with subtle structural refinement. Morphological assessments revealed that 3–5 wt% SNP loadings produced dense, uniform surfaces and improved microstructural organization owing to effective filler dispersion, whereas higher loadings resulted in particle agglomeration and interfacial defects. The study demonstrates that controlled incorporation of SNPs can tailor microstructure, interfacial bonding, and stability in seaweed‐derived biopolymers, offering valuable insights for developing renewable, biodegradable nanocomposite materials within sustainable biorefining and bio‐product applications.

works.title: Design of azine antioxidants for sustainable biodiesel: integrating structural characterization and molecular modeling
works.abstract: Abstract The growing global demand for sustainable energy solutions has intensified the search for renewable alternatives to fossil fuels, with biodiesel emerging as a promising candidate due to its biodegradability and lower emissions. However, its large‐scale application is limited by low oxidative stability, which compromises storage and performance. In this study, three nitrobenzylidene azine derivatives (ACN1, ACN2, and ACN3) were synthesized and evaluated as potential antioxidant additives for biodiesel, integrating structural characterization, molecular modeling, and machine learning. Single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction revealed that the supramolecular organization was stabilized by weak intermolecular interactions, such as CH···O, OH···N, and π  π contacts, which influenced molecular packing and favored radical scavenging. Density functional theory calculations showed that substituent effects strongly modulated antioxidant behavior. ACN2 exhibited the lowest energy gap between the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), whereas ACN1 demonstrated superior antioxidant potential due to its lower ionization potential and enhanced stabilization of radical intermediates. Fukui function and spin density analyses identified the azine R 1 R 2 C=N–N=CR 3 R 4 fragment as the key site for radical scavenging across the series. Machine learning models predicted that ACN1 would react with hydroxyl radicals at rates comparable with widely used commercial antioxidants such as butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) and tert ‐butylhydroquinone (TBHQ). Toxicological assessments highlighted structure‐dependent safety profiles, with ACN3 showing a significantly higher LD 50 (2000 mg kg −1 ) in comparison with its counterparts, suggesting that it may be a safer candidate for industrial application. Overall, these findings confirm that azine derivatives are a promising and tunable class of additives for enhancing the oxidative stability of biodiesel.

works.title: Feasibility Assessment of a Single‐pH Connected Polishing Train for Monoclonal Antibody Purification Using Mildly Acidic Protein A Elution and an Acidic‐Window Anion Exchange Membrane
works.abstract: Monoclonal antibody downstream processing often requires multiple pH adjustments between Protein A capture and polishing steps. These adjustments increase process complexity and make direct unit-operation connection more difficult. We evaluated a connected post-capture polishing block operated at approximately pH 5.0 using mild-pH Protein A elution, an acidic-window anion exchange (AEX) membrane, and cation exchange (CEX) chromatography. Praesto Jetted A50 HipH generated IgG1 eluates near pH 5.0 with conductivity suitable for direct AEX loading. Under standard condition (pH 5.0, 5.0 mS/cm), the AEX membrane reduced xenotropic murine leukemia virus to the assay limit (≥ 3 log10) and minute virus of mice by approximately 2-3 log10. In a connected proof-of-concept run without intermediate pH adjustment, the AEX-CEX polishing block reduced host cell proteins from > 25 to < 10 ng/mg-IgG and high-molecular-weight species from 1.3% to < 1% in the final product pool, maintained low-molecular-weight species below 1%, and achieved 97.6% product recovery. For two additional IgGs, archived strong-AEX flow-through records at pH 7.5 and sequence-derived charge descriptors supported the plausibility of product flow-through at pH 5.0. In a same-IgG1 retrospective comparison, the connected configuration used fewer vessels and conditioning operations and had shorter recipe-derived programmed chromatography time. These findings support process-representative evaluation of single-pH connected polishing.

works.title: Biogenic Magnetic Nanoplatform for Dual Tumor Microenvironment‐Responsive Aripiprazole Delivery in Breast Cancer
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Breast cancer remains a major global health challenge, highlighting the need for targeted drug delivery systems with improved therapeutic efficacy and reduced systemic toxicity. In this study, a green‐synthesized dual‐responsive magnetic nanoplatform, Iron oxide@Tween 80‐PEG‐ARI‐NPs, was developed for targeted breast cancer therapy. Iron oxide nanoparticles were synthesized using Nephelium lappaceum ( Rambutan ) peel extract as an eco‐friendly reducing and stabilizing agent, followed by functionalization with Tween 80, polyethylene glycol (PEG), and aripiprazole (ARI) loading. Comprehensive characterization using FTIR, XRD, SEM‐EDX, HR‐TEM, DLS, TGA/DTA, and VSM confirmed successful surface modification, spherical morphology, preserved crystallinity, superparamagnetic behavior, and enhanced colloidal stability. In vitro drug release studies demonstrated minimal ARI leakage at physiological pH 7.4 and accelerated release under acidic pH 5.5 and oxidative conditions, reaching 70.40% ± 0.55% and 90.35% ± 5.15% cumulative release after 60 h, respectively. Release kinetics followed anomalous non‐Fickian diffusion under acidic conditions and quasi‐Fickian diffusion at physiological pH. The nanoparticles exhibited significant anti‐inflammatory activity and potent cytotoxicity against MCF‐7 breast cancer cells, with an IC 50 of 40.2 ± 2.15 µg/mL, inducing pronounced apoptotic morphological changes. These findings demonstrate the potential of Iron oxide@Tween 80‐PEG‐ARI‐NPs as an effective dual‐responsive magnetic nanocarrier for targeted breast cancer therapy with enhanced therapeutic potential.

works.title: Engineering 4‐Vinylcatechol Biosynthesis in Escherichia coli Through Host–Enzyme Combination
works.abstract: De novo biosynthesis of 4-vinylcatechol (VCAT), a valuable bio-based monomer and potent antioxidant, has emerged as a crucial objective due to its profound industrial and pharmacological significance. However, its biosynthesis is frequently hindered by limited precursor availability. In this study, we developed a highly efficient, dual-plasmid platform utilizing engineered Escherichia coli cell factories to synthesize VCAT directly from glucose without precursor feeding. To establish optimal production cells, we evaluated combinations of different host strains and phenolic acid decarboxylase (PAD) sources. Our results indicate that BL21(DE3) is less suitable for efficient de novo VCAT biosynthesis under the conditions tested. In contrast, the rpoA14(DE3), featuring a reprogrammed shikimate pathway, provided a more favorable host for VCAT production and enabled endogenous tyrosine supply, thereby eliminating the need for exogenous tyrosine supplementation required in BL21(DE3). To maximize this enhanced intracellular flux, we comparatively evaluated padC genes from different Bacillus subtilis strains. Comparative analysis demonstrated that the rpoA14(DE3)-10A5 exhibited significantly superior production titers, markedly outperforming both its 168-PAD counterpart and the standard BL21(DE3) expression hosts. Cultivated in single-step, aqueous fermentation at mild conditions, this optimal host-enzyme combination achieved de novo accumulation of 200 mg/L VCAT, promising scalable biosynthesis.

works.title: Protein language model aided library generation for discovery of affinity peptides targeting the respiratory syncytial virus F protein
Biotransformation of oleanolic acid using Saccharomyces cerevisiae: New triterpenoids tentatively identified by GC-MS and evaluation of cytotoxic properties
works.abstract: In this context, microbial biotransformation has emerged as an effective, sustainable, and environmentally friendly strategy for generating novel structural derivatives. In the present study, oleanolic acid (OA), one of the most well-known pentacyclic triterpenoids due to its numerous biological activities, was subjected for the first time to biotransformation by Saccharomyces cerevisiae, leading to the formation of new triterpenoid.
